But when Katie brought the required dress, Princess Mary remained
sitting motionless before the glass, looking at her face, and saw in the
mirror her eyes full of tears and her mouth quivering, ready to burst
into sobs.

“Come, dear princess,” said Mademoiselle Bourienne, “just one more
little effort.”

The little princess, taking the dress from the maid, came up to Princess
Mary.

“Well, now we’ll arrange something quite simple and becoming,” she
said.

The three voices, hers, Mademoiselle Bourienne’s, and Katie’s, who
was laughing at something, mingled in a merry sound, like the chirping
of birds.

“No, leave me alone,” said Princess Mary.

Her voice sounded so serious and so sad that the chirping of the birds
was silenced at once. They looked at the beautiful, large, thoughtful
eyes full of tears and of thoughts, gazing shiningly and imploringly at
them, and understood that it was useless and even cruel to insist.

“At least, change your coiffure,” said the little princess.
“Didn’t I tell you,” she went on, turning reproachfully to
Mademoiselle Bourienne, “Mary’s is a face which such a coiffure does
not suit in the least. Not in the least! Please change it.”

“Leave me alone, please leave me alone! It is all quite the same to
me,” answered a voice struggling with tears.

Mademoiselle Bourienne and the little princess had to own to themselves
that Princess Mary in this guise looked very plain, worse than usual,
but it was too late. She was looking at them with an expression they
both knew, an expression thoughtful and sad. This expression in Princess
Mary did not frighten them (she never inspired fear in anyone), but they
knew that when it appeared on her face, she became mute and was not to
be shaken in her determination.

“You will change it, won’t you?” said Lise. And as Princess Mary
gave no answer, she left the room.

Princess Mary was left alone. She did not comply with Lise’s request,
she not only left her hair as it was, but did not even look in her
glass. Letting her arms fall helplessly, she sat with downcast eyes and
pondered. A husband, a man, a strong dominant and strangely attractive
being rose in her imagination, and carried her into a totally different
happy world of his own. She fancied a child, her own—such as she had
seen the day before in the arms of her nurse’s daughter—at her
own breast, the husband standing by and gazing tenderly at her and the
child. “But no, it is impossible, I am too ugly,” she thought.

“Please come to tea. The prince will be out in a moment,” came the
maid’s voice at the door.

She roused herself, and felt appalled at what she had been thinking, and
before going down she went into the room where the icons hung and, her
eyes fixed on the dark face of a large icon of the Saviour lit by a
lamp, she stood before it with folded hands for a few moments. A painful
doubt filled her soul. Could the joy of love, of earthly love for a
man, be for her? In her thoughts of marriage Princess Mary dreamed of
happiness and of children, but her strongest, most deeply hidden longing
was for earthly love. The more she tried to hide this feeling from
others and even from herself, the stronger it grew. “O God,” she
said, “how am I to stifle in my heart these temptations of the devil?
How am I to renounce forever these vile fancies, so as peacefully to
fulfill Thy will?” And scarcely had she put that question than God
gave her the answer in her own heart. “Desire nothing for thyself,
seek nothing, be not anxious or envious. Man’s future and thy own fate
must remain hidden from thee, but live so that thou mayest be ready for
anything. If it be God’s will to prove thee in the duties of marriage,
be ready to fulfill His will.” With this consoling thought (but
yet with a hope for the fulfillment of her forbidden earthly longing)
Princess Mary sighed, and having crossed herself went down, thinking
neither of her gown and coiffure nor of how she would go in nor of what
she would say. What could all that matter in comparison with the will of
God, without Whose care not a hair of man’s head can fall?

CHAPTER IV

When Princess Mary came down, Prince Vasíli and his son were already
in the drawing room, talking to the little princess and Mademoiselle
Bourienne. When she entered with her heavy step, treading on her heels,
the gentlemen and Mademoiselle Bourienne rose and the little princess,
indicating her to the gentlemen, said: “Voilà Marie!” Princess Mary
saw them all and saw them in detail. She saw Prince Vasíli’s face,
serious for an instant at the sight of her, but immediately smiling
again, and the little princess curiously noting the impression
“Marie” produced on the visitors. And she saw Mademoiselle
Bourienne, with her ribbon and pretty face, and her unusually animated
look which was fixed on him, but him she could not see, she only saw
something large, brilliant, and handsome moving toward her as she
entered the room. Prince Vasíli approached first, and she kissed the
bold forehead that bent over her hand and answered his question by
saying that, on the contrary, she remembered him quite well. Then
Anatole came up to her. She still could not see him. She only felt a
soft hand taking hers firmly, and she touched with her lips a white
forehead, over which was beautiful light-brown hair smelling of pomade.
When she looked up at him she was struck by his beauty. Anatole stood
with his right thumb under a button of his uniform, his chest expanded
and his back drawn in, slightly swinging one foot, and, with his head a
little bent, looked with beaming face at the princess without
speaking and evidently not thinking about her at all. Anatole was not
quick-witted, nor ready or eloquent in conversation, but he had the
faculty, so invaluable in society, of composure and imperturbable
self-possession. If a man lacking in self-confidence remains dumb on
a first introduction and betrays a consciousness of the impropriety of
such silence and an anxiety to find something to say, the effect is
bad. But Anatole was dumb, swung his foot, and smilingly examined the
princess’ hair. It was evident that he could be silent in this way for
a very long time. “If anyone finds this silence inconvenient, let him
talk, but I don’t want to,” he seemed to say. Besides this, in his
behavior to women Anatole had a manner which particularly inspires in
them curiosity, awe, and even love—a supercilious consciousness of
his own superiority. It was as if he said to them: “I know you, I know
you, but why should I bother about you? You’d be only too glad, of
course.” Perhaps he did not really think this when he met women—even
probably he did not, for in general he thought very little—but his
looks and manner gave that impression. The princess felt this, and as if
wishing to show him that she did not even dare expect to interest him,
she turned to his father. The conversation was general and animated,
thanks to Princess Lise’s voice and little downy lip that lifted over
her white teeth. She met Prince Vasíli with that playful manner often
employed by lively chatty people, and consisting in the assumption
that between the person they so address and themselves there are some
semi-private, long-established jokes and amusing reminiscences, though
no such reminiscences really exist—just as none existed in this case.
Prince Vasíli readily adopted her tone and the little princess also
drew Anatole, whom she hardly knew, into these amusing recollections of
things that had never occurred. Mademoiselle Bourienne also shared them
and even Princess Mary felt herself pleasantly made to share in these
merry reminiscences.

“Here at least we shall have the benefit of your company all to
ourselves, dear prince,” said the little princess (of course, in
French) to Prince Vasíli. “It’s not as at Annette’s * receptions
where you always ran away; you remember cette chère Annette!”

    * Anna Pávlovna.

“Ah, but you won’t talk politics to me like Annette!”

“And our little tea table?”

“Oh, yes!”

“Why is it you were never at Annette’s?” the little princess asked
Anatole. “Ah, I know, I know,” she said with a sly glance, “your
brother Hippolyte told me about your goings on. Oh!” and she shook her
finger at him, “I have even heard of your doings in Paris!”

“And didn’t Hippolyte tell you?” asked Prince Vasíli, turning to
his son and seizing the little princess’ arm as if she would have run
away and he had just managed to catch her, “didn’t he tell you how
he himself was pining for the dear princess, and how she showed him the
door? Oh, she is a pearl among women, Princess,” he added, turning to
Princess Mary.

When Paris was mentioned, Mademoiselle Bourienne for her part seized the
opportunity of joining in the general current of recollections.

She took the liberty of inquiring whether it was long since Anatole
had left Paris and how he had liked that city. Anatole answered the
Frenchwoman very readily and, looking at her with a smile, talked to her
about her native land. When he saw the pretty little Bourienne, Anatole
came to the conclusion that he would not find Bald Hills dull either.
“Not at all bad!” he thought, examining her, “not at all bad, that
little companion! I hope she will bring her along with her when we’re
married, la petite est gentille.” *

    * The little one is charming.

The old prince dressed leisurely in his study, frowning and considering
what he was to do. The coming of these visitors annoyed him. “What are
Prince Vasíli and that son of his to me? Prince Vasíli is a shallow
braggart and his son, no doubt, is a fine specimen,” he grumbled to
himself. What angered him was that the coming of these visitors revived
in his mind an unsettled question he always tried to stifle, one about
which he always deceived himself. The question was whether he could ever
bring himself to part from his daughter and give her to a husband. The
prince never directly asked himself that question, knowing beforehand
that he would have to answer it justly, and justice clashed not only
with his feelings but with the very possibility of life. Life without
Princess Mary, little as he seemed to value her, was unthinkable to
him. “And why should she marry?” he thought. “To be unhappy for
certain. There’s Lise, married to Andrew—a better husband one would
think could hardly be found nowadays—but is she contented with her
lot? And who would marry Marie for love? Plain and awkward! They’ll
take her for her connections and wealth. Are there no women living
unmarried, and even the happier for it?” So thought Prince Bolkónski
while dressing, and yet the question he was always putting off demanded
an immediate answer. Prince Vasíli had brought his son with the evident
intention of proposing, and today or tomorrow he would probably ask
for an answer. His birth and position in society were not bad. “Well,
I’ve nothing against it,” the prince said to himself, “but he must
be worthy of her. And that is what we shall see.”

“That is what we shall see! That is what we shall see!” he added
aloud.

He entered the drawing room with his usual alert step, glancing rapidly
round the company. He noticed the change in the little princess’
dress, Mademoiselle Bourienne’s ribbon, Princess Mary’s unbecoming
coiffure, Mademoiselle Bourienne’s and Anatole’s smiles, and the
loneliness of his daughter amid the general conversation. “Got herself
up like a fool!” he thought, looking irritably at her. “She is
shameless, and he ignores her!”

He went straight up to Prince Vasíli.

“Well! How d’ye do? How d’ye do? Glad to see you!”

“Friendship laughs at distance,” began Prince Vasíli in his usual
rapid, self-confident, familiar tone. “Here is my second son; please
love and befriend him.”

Prince Bolkónski surveyed Anatole.

“Fine young fellow! Fine young fellow!” he said. “Well, come and
kiss me,” and he offered his cheek.

Anatole kissed the old man, and looked at him with curiosity and perfect
composure, waiting for a display of the eccentricities his father had
told him to expect.

Prince Bolkónski sat down in his usual place in the corner of the sofa
and, drawing up an armchair for Prince Vasíli, pointed to it and began
questioning him about political affairs and news. He seemed to listen
attentively to what Prince Vasíli said, but kept glancing at Princess
Mary.

“And so they are writing from Potsdam already?” he said, repeating
Prince Vasíli’s last words. Then rising, he suddenly went up to his
daughter.

“Is it for visitors you’ve got yourself up like that, eh?” said

text:
The Twelve Months Sanctified by Prayer: November, Month of the Souls in Purgatory by M. L'ABBE A. RICARD, D.S.G. Translated from the French. 1877 November 12 THE GREATEST OF THE WORKS OF MERCY.

.

Prelude.

.

Let us transport ourselves in spirit to the judgment-seat, and hear the just Judge say to the elect, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry, and you gave Me to eat: I was thirsty, and you gave Me to drink : I was a stranger, and you took Me in: naked, and you covered Me: sick, and you visited Me: I was in prison, and you came to Me."

.

Meditation.

.

Charity towards the souls in Pur­gatory comprises in itself all the works of mercy which have just been enumerated, and also greatly surpasses them in merit; for in fact the Christian who delivers a soul from Purgatory, and who opens heaven for him, gives him not only the crumbs from his table, but the bread of angels and all the delights of paradise, for which he hungers to such a degree that no torment is equal to this pain. He gives him not only a glass of water, but the entire fountain of that water which springs to eternal life, of that water for which he thirsts so ardently that he burns day and night without being able to procure the least refreshment. He does not harbour him as he would have done a passing stranger, but he introduces him into the blissful abode for which he sighs, and whose entrance was closed to him from the time of creation. He clothes him not in a perishable garment, but in a robe of immor­tality which will eternally preserve him from cold and heat. He visits to assist him, not during a slight attack of fever, but amidst the ardour of pitiless flames which torment him with­ out allowing him any repose. Finally, he descends into his prison to break his chains, and give him the glorious liberty of the children of God.

.

Resolution.

.

Offer up something to-day, for the most suffering soul in Purgatory.

.

Aspiration.

.

Come, ye blessed of My Father. (Gospel according to St. Matthew xxv. 34.)

.

EXAMPLE: ST. AUGUSTINE'S REPRIMAND.

.

St. Augustine strongly reproved the temerity of a writer of his time, who said that we ought not to fear Purgatory, since the torments suffered there would not last for ever. " What does it signify," he said, "how long a time I shall spend there, so that I enter heaven at last;" and St. Augustine says in answer to this: "Let no one speak thus, for the fire of expiation will be more terrible than any suffering in this world, however dreadful we may imagine it to be."

.

Senno . VI . de Sandis.

text:
The Twelve Months Sanctified by Prayer: November, Month of the Souls in Purgatory by M. L'ABBE A. RICARD, D.S.G. Translated from the French. 1877 November 11 YOU DID IT TO ME.
.
Prelude.
.
Our Lord Himself invites us to in­tercede for the souls in Purgatory.  Let us listen reverently to Him, and after spending a few minutes in lovingly considering His infinite goodness, let us meditate on one of the most powerful motives which could excite our devotion to the souls in Purgatory.
.
Meditation.
.
The motives on which we have already meditated must. if our soul is Christian and full of faith, have made a great impression. Today we shall meditate on another motive, which, if it leaves us cold and insensible, will show that we do not even deserve the name of Christian, and that we have not an atom of faith.
.
God, Whose majesty is immense, Whose goodness and liberality are infinite, God Whom we have so often offended, and Who has obliged us, in a thousand ways, to pay Him every homage, God, I say, has vouchsafed by an inconceivable prodigy to accept all the good which we do to man as if it was done to Himself. His Son has assured us of it when He said, "Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these, My least brethren, you did it to Me." It is as if He said : All the works of mercy which you have exercised towards My brethren have been as agreeable to Me as if you had done them to Me. I am not the less obliged for the help given to the soul of one of My brethren than if you had delivered it from Purgatory, and sent it to heaven. How then can we neglect anything which pleases the Son of God so much? Can we be influenced by a more powerful motive?
.
Resolution.
.
Remember sometimes that Our Lord considers as done to Himself the help which we give the souls in Purgatory.
.
Aspiration.
.
"You did it to Me." (Gospel according to St. Matthew xxv. 40.)
.
EXAMPLE: MARY OF THE ANGELS (Maria degli Angeli).
.
A very edifying life has been published of Mary of the Angels, a Carmelite beatified by his Holiness Pius IX. Here are some extracts from it:
.
"It is quite certain that this blessed soul pos­sessed an heroic charity and devotion to the souls in Purgatory, and two causes conspired to give her these sentiments. First, it was her love of God. Nothing is dearer to God than these souls which the flames of Purgatory cleanse from every stain, and Mary of the Angels did not forget this, and therefore as deep as was her love for her divine Master, so deep also was her desire of delivering those souls which she knew He loved so tenderly. Secondly, it was her charity towards her neighbour. A super­ natural light had shown her the sad condition of those souls, and the unspeakable torments which they suffer, and this knowledge had so excited her compassion in their favour that she left nothing undone to procure their deliverance. She spared neither prayers, fasting, nor penances, to attain this holy end, and she tried also to in­ spire the same feelings in her sisters and secular­ persons.
.
As there is no work holier or more beneficial to the souls in Purgatory than the sacrifice of the Mass, Mary of the Angels was careful to have it often offered up for the repose of their souls, and for this end she held out her hand to the rich, and occupied herself in pious labours. When she filled the office of prioress, she employed herself in working altar-linen and ornaments, which she sent to some priest or church, asking for sole payment that Masses should be celebrated for the holy souls; she inspired her sisters with the same generous feelings, and induced them to employ themselves in the same manner. During one of her priorships, as she was praying one night for the souls in Purgatory, she yielded to an impulse of fervour, and promised to have five Masses celebrated for their intention every month.
.
In the morning, she made known her promise to her assistants,. who remarked that her desire could not be accomplished, because of the extreme poverty of the house. God then came in a wonderful manner to the help of the generous prioress. During the day, a stranger came to seek her, and told her that it was his custom to have a great many Masses celebrated, and that he felt himself inspired to give her an alms, so that she could have five celebrated every month, leaving her also entire liberty with regard to the application of the holy sacrifice."

DID YOU KNOW??

Before ESPN television analyst Marcus "Swagu" Spears became a 298-pound Consensus All-American defensive lineman and first-round NFL draft pick, he was one of the top high school basketball players in America, winning the Louisiana Gatorade Basketball Player of the Year award in high school over future NBA Hall of Famer Shaquille O'Neal's alma mater territory.

Growing up in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, Spears was a true dual-sport phenom. At Southern University Laboratory School, he dominated both the gridiron and the court. On the basketball court, his combination of size, footwork, and agility earned him the state's highest high school basketball honor in 2001, drawing recruitment offers from major college hoops programs across the nation.

​When he arrived at Louisiana State University (LSU) in 2001, head coach Nick Saban initially utilized Spears' rare athletic dexterity on both sides of the ball, playing him as a tight end on offense (catching two touchdown passes as a freshman) before shifting him permanently to defensive tackle and defensive end.

His unique combination of basketball footwork and football power allowed him to anchor LSU's 2003 National Championship defense, leading to a 9-year NFL career spent primarily with the Dallas Cowboys and a subsequent breakout television broadcasting career on ESPN's NFL Live and Get Up. Walk with me 👇🏾👇🏾 

The Career Evolution of Marcus Spears:

​How a high school basketball standout built a championship football legacy and a broadcasting empire:

1. Dual-Sport High School Dominance
2000–2001
Named an All-American in football and Louisiana Gatorade Basketball Player of the Year after leading his high school in both sports.

2. Two-Way Player & National Champion at LSU
2001–2004
Recruited by Nick Saban, Spears transitions from two-way tight end/defensive end to consensus First-Team All-American defensive lineman, winning the 2003 BCS National Championship.

3. NFL First-Round Pick & Cowboys Tenure
2005–2013
Selected 20th overall in the 2005 NFL Draft by Bill Parcells and the Dallas Cowboys, going on to play 9 seasons as a defensive line anchor.

4. SEC Network & ESPN 'Swagu' Era
2014–Present
Launches his broadcasting career on SEC Network before joining flagship shows NFL Live and Get Up, becoming a fan-favorite personality nicknamed "The Big Swagu."

More Surprising Facts About Marcus Spears:

A. ​The Pick-Six in the Sugar Bowl: In the 2004 BCS National Championship Game against Oklahoma, Spears scored a game-changing 20-yard interception return for a touchdown (pick-six), securing LSU's 21–14 victory.

B. ​Origin of "Swagu": His famous media persona and nickname, "Swagu" (or "The Big Swagu"), originated from a playful catchphrase celebrating swagger and flair, which eventually became so popular that NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell gave it an official stamp of approval on television.

C. ​Drafted Alongside DeMarcus Ware: In the 2005 NFL Draft, Bill Parcells famously used the Dallas Cowboys' two first-round picks to draft DeMarcus Ware at #11 and Marcus Spears at #20, establishing the foundation of the Cowboys' defense for nearly a decade.

​SUMMARILY! 
​From winning Louisiana's top high school basketball award to scoring a championship pick-six for Nick Saban at LSU, Marcus Spears leveraged his dual-sport athletic agility to become an NFL first-round pick and a premier ESPN personality.

text:
Marcus Spears had to miss his son's first college game for work. Problem is, his work is ESPN. So in the middle of Monday Night Countdown they cut live to the arena in Austin, more than 2,000 miles away, and let him watch his 17-year-old walk out of the tunnel while the whole country watched his face.

He almost didn't go to Seattle at all. He told the producers he was thinking about skipping the trip so he could be in the building. He got in the day before and said he felt terrible about it. Then he talked himself down with one line. "My wife and myself have prepared him to be where he is," he said.

And when he says his wife helped prepare him, he means it pretty literally.

Aiysha Spears was the 7th overall pick in the 2003 WNBA draft out of LSU. Marcus went in the first round to the Cowboys two years later and played nine seasons in the NFL. Their oldest, Cari, was the national high school volleyball player of the year and is now an All-American at Texas. Marcus Jr. was ESPN's No. 1 player in the entire class of 2027, and he graduated a year early so he could get to Austin at 17. The youngest, Miko, is coming up in volleyball too.

So you've got a house where both parents were first-round picks and two of the kids became top recruits in the country in two different sports. That kind of thing basically doesn't happen.

He did get to see his son play once before Monday, at an exhibition at Madison Square Garden the weekend before. The opponent that night was St. John's, which happens to be where Aiysha started her own college career back in 1999.

When the live shot came up, the guy who breaks down NFL film on TV every week told the crew he was about to cry, and said the kid had worked his butt off to get there.

Then Junior came off the bench, and the first time he got on the floor he blocked a guy driving to the rim. A minute later he bullied his way into the paint and finished through contact for an and-one.

"He'll be fine," his dad had said.

How do you choose the right turnstile for a commercial facility?

Start with how people use the entrance: who needs access, how many people arrive at once, and what level of entry control the facility requires.

An employee entrance at an industrial site has different needs than a staffed corporate lobby. Full-height turnstiles, waist-high turnstiles, and optical lanes offer different approaches to managing pedestrian passage.

Before selecting equipment, ask:
• What happens during peak shift changes?
• How will visitors and contractors enter?
• How will an accessible route be incorporated?
• How will the system connect with existing credentials and Access Control?
• What should happen during an emergency or power outage?
• Does the facility need to deter, detect, or physically restrict unauthorized passage?

A valid credential confirms permission. The entrance equipment helps manage the passage that follows. Both need to support the facility’s security procedures and daily operations.

FDC installs turnstiles and pedestrian entry systems for commercial, industrial, government, and critical infrastructure facilities throughout Florida.

@SteaknShake 🔥Steak ’n Shake is the main (and best-known) example in the U.S. of a business that gives free items specifically to Tesla owners who drive up.
They regularly run “Tesla Tallow Tuesday” (or similar) promotions. These usually happen in a short window like 2:22–4:20 p.m. local time and include freebies such as:
•Free small orders of beef tallow fries or tots
•Free super-size upgrades on fries
•Occasional free jars of grass-fed or Wagyu beef tallow cooking oil, lip balm, or other items (sometimes for the first few Tesla customers, sometimes for all)
These are promotional rather than everyday permanent discounts, and they tie into the chain’s switch to beef tallow and its Supercharger partnership. Check their social accounts (especially on Tuesdays) for the current offer.
Other notes
•Few other widespread examples exist in the U.S. for restaurants, coffee shops, or similar businesses that automatically give something free just because you own a Tesla and drive up. Most Tesla-related perks involve buying another car (competitor conquest cash), Tesla’s own referral/loyalty programs, free Supercharging offers on new purchases, or the special experience at Tesla’s Hollywood Diner (in-car ordering, movie syncing, etc.—open to non-Tesla vehicles too).
•Some Supercharger locations have had partner businesses offering free coffee or drinks to Tesla owners (e.g., older reports of free coffee/tea at Collin Street Bakery near a Texas Supercharger). These are location-specific and can change.
•Tesla Service centers or charging lounges sometimes provide free coffee while you wait, but that’s not a public restaurant/coffee shop deal.
•Outside the U.S., official Tesla Owners Clubs in places like Hong Kong, Singapore, and Malaysia partner with local cafes and restaurants for discounts or free items when you show the Tesla app or ownership proof.
If you’re looking for current deals, Steak ’n Shake’s social media or local stores are the most reliable place to check.

text:
A host: “the supreme court now shutting down a last ditch effort by the trump administration to force california to set aside thousands of ballots from alleged non-citizens. you may remember last month the d.o.j. sent a letter to state election officials that included a list of 20,000 registered voters. it claimed those folks are not u.s. citizens but still received a mail-in ballot. california contested and a federal judge sided with the state. yesterday the supreme court rejected the trump administration's appeal. with election day here the d.o.j. announced this morning that election monitors will be in all 50 states for the first time in u.s. history. so what does this mean? well, we've got cbs news election law expert david becker with us at the table. he's also executive director for the center for election innovation and research. that's a nonprofit focused on increasing trust in u.s. elections. so david, good morning. welcome. happy election day to you. the supreme court gave a very quick, almost single line ruling on avoiding the appeal from the trump administration. does that mean this case is over?”

David Becker: “this case is essentially over at this point. i mean, the d.o.j. had offered very flimsy evidence with regard to these 20,000 alleged non-citizens on the voter list. and in fact, a lawyer in a separate case yesterday for the d.o.j. stood up in court and basically admitted that there's a very high error rate on those, on that list. the supreme court rejected this. no notable dissents, didn't even invite briefing, which is very, very rare. and i think in doing so, they sent a clear signal. stop with all of this. let the election continue under the constitution. the states get to run elections. let the states continue to do their work to run this election. i think that's going to bode very well for future litigation as well. it's the same thing you have repeated. states run their own elections and they're pretty good at it.”

A host: “but despite that message from the supreme court, the d.o.j. yesterday announced dozens of arrests involving alleged voter fraud. fact check that for us. how common is voter fraud in the first place?”

David Becker: “we know how much voter fraud there is in the united states, and it's not zero, but it's really close to zero. it's very, very rare. we have a really good sense of how many non-citizens are on voter lists. sometimes they get on and as a result of an administrative error, but it's extremely rare. the numbers are very small. and over the course of nearly two years trying to investigate voter fraud, non-citizens voting, et cetera, this department of justice has only arrested several dozen people out of well over 200 million registered voters in the united states. it's also important to note the d.o.j. is violating its own rules here. the d.o.j. has very clear rules. i'm a former d.o.j. voting section attorney myself that say you do not, do not bring investigations or litigation that could influence or interfere with the election close to an election. and by even making these arrests, which could have been made tomorrow, they're clearly violating their own rules.”

A host: “so our viewers should keep that in mind as we watch poll results come in today. we don't know if they'll come in quickly or trickle in. if some states we can call tonight or tomorrow, what should people keep in mind as they perhaps hear different things from different government entities?”

David Becker: “yeah, it's almost certain that we're gonna hear losing candidates or losing parties claim the election was rigged and bring up false and debunked claims about the election in the aftermath. they're likely to try to leverage the period of time where we're still waiting for the winner to be announced by the media, by us here at cbs, because elections are gonna be really close around the nation today. and as margins get smaller, as the elections get closer, including in places we're not used to seeing close elections. we just heard about texas, for instance, and other places we might be waiting for more ballots to be reported in, and it could take hours or even days until we have enough information in those really, really close races. tune out the noise. be patient, as hard as it is. i'm also impatient, but just wait for the election officials, your neighbors, who are working in their county offices to count all those ballots. they're gonna be working through the night to get those out to all of us.”

A host: “and the results may change as they come in because different locations will be submitted.”

David Becker: “that's exactly right.”

A host: “the point you made there, your neighbors are the ones helping tally this in your local office and there's republicans and democrats there.”

David Becker: “that's exactly right. those observers from the parties are watching the entire process. the entire process process is transparent.”

A host: “all right, david becker with the message we need today. thank you so much.”

David Becker: “thank you.”

text:
A school in Dallas, Texas, asked for 50 men to show up for its students.

Nearly 600 answered the call.

In December 2017, Billy Earl Dade Middle School organized a special event called “Breakfast with Dads.”

The school expected around 150 boys to attend, but organizers worried that some students without fathers or male role models might feel left out.

So they reached out to the community, asking for 50 male volunteers to spend time with the children.

What happened next was extraordinary.

Nearly 600 men showed up.

They gathered with the students over breakfast, shared advice, offered encouragement, and talked about life. Some even helped the boys learn how to tie neckties.

The school gym filled with men who had one simple purpose: to make children feel supported, valued, and cared for.

They weren’t all fathers. They weren’t all relatives. Many were simply members of the community who wanted to make a difference.

The school asked for 50 men.

Nearly 600 showed up.

Sometimes, changing a child’s life doesn’t require grand gestures or extraordinary powers.

Sometimes, it simply means showing up when someone needs you.

And that morning, hundreds of men showed those boys that they mattered.

text:
❤️ CHRISTIAN MEN, THE NEXT GENERATION NEEDS YOU TO SHOW UP!

In December 2017, something truly heartwarming happened at Dr. Billy Earl Dade Middle School in Dallas, Texas.

The school organised an event called Breakfast with Dads for its students. Knowing that some children did not have fathers or father figures available, the organisers requested about 50 men to volunteer and spend time encouraging the boys.

But something extraordinary happened.

Nearly 600 men showed up!

Six hundred men decided that these children deserved to feel loved, supported and encouraged. They gave their time, shared wisdom, offered guidance and demonstrated what positive male presence looks like.

Now, let me speak to Christian men.

The next generation needs more than men who can preach, quote Scripture, lead worship or occupy positions in church. They need men who are willing to be present, mentor young boys, encourage young girls, support struggling families and demonstrate the love of Christ through their actions.

Christian men, we have a responsibility beyond providing for our own families. We must also be concerned about the children growing up around us.

There are boys growing up without fathers. There are young men desperately looking for direction. There are children who have never experienced a father's encouragement. Some are making life decisions without anyone to guide them.

Can we rise and become that generation of men who intentionally mentor, encourage and guide the next generation?

You don't have to be a biological father to make a father's impact in someone's life.

You don't have to be wealthy to mentor a young boy. You don't have to be a pastor to provide godly counsel. Sometimes, all you need is a willing heart, time and a genuine desire to see another person become better.

Paul said in 1 Corinthians 11:1, "Imitate me, just as I also imitate Christ."

Christian men, let us become examples worth following.

Let us raise sons, even those we did not biologically father. Let us protect, encourage, correct in love and point the next generation towards Jesus Christ.

The church must not only be a place where children are taught about God; it must also be a place where they encounter godly men who demonstrate His character.

Fifty men were requested. Nearly 600 showed up.

Imagine what would happen if Christian men everywhere decided to show up for the next generation.

May God raise men who are not only present in church but also present in the lives of those who need them.

MEN, THE NEXT GENERATION IS WATCHING. LET US GIVE THEM SOMETHING WORTH IMITATING. ❤️

text:
Virginia Woman Indicted in $49 Million Medicaid Mental Health Fraud Scheme | Matt Vespa, Townhall

A federal grand jury in the Eastern District of Virginia returned an indictment on October 20 against Mikia Antoneice Noble, 37, of North Chesterfield, Virginia, for a $49 million mental health crisis services fraud scheme targeting Virginia Medicaid.

Noble was arrested earlier this week.

Court documents say that Noble was the co-owner and chief operating officer of Advancing Communities Everywhere LLC (ACE), a mental health provider in the Richmond, Virginia area. In addition to her ownership role, Noble claimed to also work as a mental health professional for ACE. ACE purported to provide mental health services to individuals experiencing acute or significant behavioral health crises but did not provide those services as billed.

As alleged in the indictment, Noble conspired with her co-owner to:

- Bill Virginia Medicaid for crisis services purportedly provided by teams of mental health professionals including a trained and licensed professional, which were instead provided only by a single low-level, less qualified mental health professional;

- Pay over $2 million for hotel room rentals that were offered to Medicaid beneficiaries to illegally induce them to allow ACE to bill for services purportedly provided to them that they did not actually need;

- Falsify medical records by adding signatures of licensed professionals who had not actually participated in providing crisis services;

- Falsify medical records by adding Noble’s own signature falsely representing that she had participated in providing crisis services, when in fact Noble was out of the country; and

- Lie to Medicaid Managed Care Organizations conducting audits of ACE’s crisis services.

From January 2022 through April of 2026, Noble allegedly participated in submitting over $49 million in false and fraudulent claims to Virginia Medicaid.

Noble is charged with conspiracy to commit healthcare fraud and three counts of healthcare fraud. If convicted, she faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison on each count.

Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; First Assistant U.S. Attorney Theophani K. Stamos for the Eastern District of Virginia; and Special Agent in Charge Ian Kaufmann of the FBI Richmond Field Office made the announcement.

The FBI Richmond Field Office and the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit of the Virginia Office of the Attorney General are investigating the case.

Trial Attorneys Lauren Randell and Zachary H. Ray of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Robert S. Day for the Eastern District of Virginia are prosecuting the case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal healthcare programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, is taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in healthcare fraud schemes. More information is available at https://t.co/Lx0gR2qD3f.

An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

text:
The year is 180. You are a gladiator in Ephesus, and the films will give you a body like a bronze statue. You are fed barley porridge and beans, and the crowd calls you a barley man to your face. The porridge puts a layer of fat over your muscle so the cuts bleed instead of killing, which is good for the show. The man who owns you dines on dormice rolled in honey and poppy seed. When your bones are dug up eighteen centuries later they are full of barley and almost nothing else, and a man at a university will call your diet plant-forward.

The year is 1300. You are a villein on a Hampshire manor, living, as the brochure will one day put it, in harmony with the land. The land gives you pottage: peas, beans and oats in the one pot, every day, until you die of it at forty. The hall above you smells of venison from the lord's own park, roast pork, eel, swan, butter from cows you milked before dawn. Take one deer from his wood and you lose a hand. The court that decides it sits in his hall, after dinner.

The year is 1755. You are a Highland tenant eating oatmeal three times a day, and in London Dr Johnson has just printed his dictionary. Oats: a grain which in England is generally given to horses, but in Scotland supports the people. The laird at the head of your glen finds this very funny over his beef. The beef was driven to market past your door.

The year is 1795. You are a Berkshire farm labourer and a clergyman is at your table with a notebook, writing down what your children eat. Bread. Tea. A little cheese. Bacon on Sunday if the pig did well. He prints it as a national disgrace. The squire you work for has a joint every day of the year and is told from the pulpit that your trouble is thrift.

The year is 1847. You are in County Clare and the potatoes have gone black in the ground for the second year running. Your family lived on them, ten pounds a day for a working man, and you are sitting in a cabin with nothing. At the harbour the ships are loading cattle, pigs, butter and bacon for England, under armed guard. The agent on the quay looks well. So does the bullock walking up the gangplank past the people who raised it.

The year is 1933. You are in a village outside Kharkiv. The grain quota has been collected, then collected again, then the brigades have come with iron rods to probe the floors for anything buried. Your children are eating boiled bark, and the dog next door has stopped barking. In the district town there is a shop for Party members with a curtain over the window. Behind the curtain there is sausage.

The year is 1997. You are in North Pyongan and the rations stopped months ago. You are stripping the inner bark from pines and boiling grass, and the famine will take hundreds of thousands before it ends. The Dear Leader's personal chef is flying to Japan for tuna, to Denmark for pork and to Iran for caviar, and will write a book about it.

The year is 2026. You are in a supermarket in England. The posters say eat less meat for the planet. The spread is plant-based, the cereal has a heart on the box, and the beef carries a warning about its footprint. You take the lentils, because you are a responsible person, and you pay more for them than the villein's pottage ever cost anyone.

The people who put the posters up flew to the climate conference, and the menu had beef on it. They eat what the lord ate, what the laird ate, what the agent on the quay ate, what the man behind the curtain ate.

Two thousand years, and the diet of grain and beans was always what the powerful handed down to the people beneath them. Everyone at both ends of the table knew what it meant.

Now it has a name, a logo and a moral, and for the first time in history the peasant is paying extra for it.

It was nothing like the comfortable life she had known.

She had to wake up early, clean animal shelters, feed livestock, carry supplies, and learn how to care for animals.

Nick also began questioning her decisions.

Karina had no easy answer.

But a man named Andrew offered her help.

He had also suffered because of Dimma and Valentina's schemes, and he understood how dangerous they could be.

With his support, Karina slowly learned to survive on the ranch.

She began earning money, rebuilding her confidence, and gaining the respect of the villagers.

Most importantly, she started repairing her relationship with Nick.

But while Karina was learning to rebuild her life, Dimma and Valentina were making another mistake.

They believed she was too weak and poor to ever challenge them again.

They were wrong.

text:
The Catholic Church bases its teaching on Purgatory, a state of final purification for souls who die in God's grace and friendship, but are still imperfectly purified, on a combination of Scripture, Sacred Tradition, and early Christian practice:
1. Scriptural Evidence
While the exact word "purgatory" does not appear in the Bible, Catholic theology points to several passages:
1 Corinthians 3:11–15: St. Paul describes believers whose works are tested by fire on the day of judgment. Some will suffer the loss of their bad works ("wood, hay, stubble"), yet they themselves will be saved, "but only as through fire". This points to an intermediate state of purification distinct from heaven (where no imperfection exists) and hell (where there is no salvation).
2 Maccabees 12:39–46: Judas Maccabeus offers prayers and atonement sacrifices for fallen Jewish soldiers who died wearing pagan amulets. This demonstrates an ancient Jewish belief, predating Christianity, that the living can assist the dead through prayer.
Matthew 12:32: Jesus speaks of sin that will not be forgiven "either in this age or in the age to come," which implies that certain lesser sins or consequences can be cleansed or forgiven in the afterlife.
Matthew 5:25–26: Christ uses the imagery of being thrown into prison and not getting out "until you have paid the last penny," which early Church Fathers frequently interpreted as a metaphor for a purifying or penal state after death.
2. Sacred Tradition and the Early Church
Prayers for the Dead in the Catacombs: Early Christian inscriptions and graffiti in the Roman catacombs from the first three centuries consistently show Christians praying for the deceased so they may find peace and rest.
Early Church Fathers: Second-century writings, such as the Acts of Paul and Thecla and the Martyrdom of Perpetua and Felicity, alongside later writings by figures like St. Cyprian and St. Augustine, explicitly reference the practice of offering prayers, suffrages, and the Eucharist for the departed.
The Logic of Holiness: Revelation 21:27 states that "nothing unclean shall enter" heaven. Because many people die in a state of God's grace but still carry venial sins, attachment to self-love, or the temporal consequences of past sins, a post-mortem process of cleansing is necessary to achieve the absolute holiness required for the presence of God.

China, South China Sea, 1807. A woman took command of a pirate fleet.

Her name was Zheng Yi Sao. Within three years, she commanded tens of thousands of men and hundreds of ships — more than Blackbeard, Kidd, and Morgan combined.

She ran it like a state. Her rules were written down: any pirate who raped a captive was beheaded. Any pirate who stole from a village that supplied them was beheaded. Even captains were bound by them.

In 1810, the Qing navy could not defeat her fleet. The government offered amnesty instead.

She negotiated. Her men kept their lives. She kept her loot. The fleet disbanded.

She retired to Guangzhou, ran a gambling house, and died at home in 1844.

Zheng Yi Sao was one of history's most successful pirates, and she negotiated the terms of her surrender herself.

text:
East Texas A&M went into Norman on Monday night, beat Oklahoma 68 to 64 in Oklahoma's opener and it was the first time in the history of that school that the Lions had beaten a team from a power conference. A prediction model had their odds of winning at 1.2% prior to the game even starting.

Bo Aldridge scored 22 points on 8 of 12 shooting, had 5 assists and 2 steals. He did it in a building where Oklahoma had every reason to expect a comfortable night and three years ago Oklahoma was one of the schools that was recruiting him out of high school.

His name is Ketraleus Aldridge, everyone just calls him Bo. He's from Topeka, Kansas and played at Highland Park High School where 24/7 Sports had him as the 34th best shooting guard in the country for the class of 2024.

In June 2023 he made an unofficial visit to Kansas and in November of that year he committed to Arizona State on a list that also included Mississippi State, Ole Miss, Wichita State, Northern Illinois and Oklahoma. He then spent the next season playing prep ball in the Overtime Elite.

Then in June 2024 he asked ASU to release him from his LOI and re-opened his recruiting. No one has ever said why.

Texas A&M rang him, so did Old Dominion, so did Detroit and Indiana State and he ended up at East Texas A&M in Commerce, Texas. They used to call it Texas A&M Commerce (hence the scoreboard still says TAMC) and they were a Division II school until July of 2022 (that's four years ago).

Be absolutely straight about the size of Monday night. This is a game that gets scheduled so the bigger school can have a comfortable night in front of its own crowd prior to anything serious really starting. Oklahoma are in the SEC and East Texas A&M had never beaten a team at that level in the history of the school. The Lions came in on the road to open the season and won it by four.

Mohamed Diakite scored 15, Alonzo Dodd 15 and Aldridge (the one who had the Oklahoma offer in his pocket three years back and went off to somewhere else with it) scored 22 of his team's 68.

text:
This is what Higgins got.

This is page 136 of volume 30 of the county's deed records: an agreement between "Anthony F. Lucas of the City of Washington D.C. and Patillo Higgins of Jefferson County Texas," dated June 20, 1899, the same day as the lease. Read why Lucas made it: "Whereas the said Patillo Higgins by the use of his efforts and influence has secured for the said Anthony F. Lucas a contract of lease and purchase." And what he gave: "the said Anthony F. Lucas agree herewith to give to the said Higgins one tenth interest in said option or lease." If Lucas bought the land and sold it, Higgins was to have "ten per cent of the profits of said purchase and sale." If anyone offered Higgins money for his tenth, Lucas had thirty days to match the offer.

They signed it on July 24, 1899, both men, in duplicate. It was filed with the county clerk on October 14 and copied into the books on October 24.

Read the words carefully, because in 1901 he would sue on them. A tenth of the option or lease. That is a share of a contract: a tenth of Lucas's right to explore that land for a year, and to buy it for $33,150. It is not a royalty, a share of the oil. It is not a tenth of the company. If Lucas bought the land and sold it on, Higgins got ten percent of the profit. If Lucas kept the contract and found oil under it, Higgins had a tenth of Lucas's side of the deal.

And it was on record. From October 1899, anyone who took over any part of that contract did so on notice that Higgins claimed a tenth of it.

Everything now depended on the contract staying alive.

🧵11/24

Credit: Jefferson County Clerk, Deed Records Vol. 30, pp. 136–137; the clerk's free online images; public record.

text:
Celsius Faces Health‑Washing Lawsuit Over Energy Drink Claims

Annabelle Nielsen filed a federal lawsuit in Washington last week against Celsius, the Boca Raton, Fla. company that sells the nation’s second‑largest energy‑drink line. The suit seeks class‑action status and accuses Celsius of a “health‑washing” scheme that misled her into buying its products.

Nielsen says she would have chosen a cheaper alternative if she knew the company’s health claims were false. The complaint alleges she purchased the drinks believing they offered real metabolic benefits.

The lawsuit points to a can of Astro Vibe‑flavored Celsius that carries the phrases “accelerates metabolism” and “burns body fat.” Three small cartoon images of a runner, a biker, and a meditator flank the claims. On the back of the can, tiny print states, “Celsius alone does not produce weight loss in absence of a healthy diet and moderate exercise.”

“Health‑washing” is defined in the complaint as vague claims such as “organic” and “high protein.” The suit argues that Celsius puts health statements front‑and‑center while relegating caveats to small print.

According to the complaint, Celsius markets ingredients like ginger root and green tea extract as evidence of health benefits. The company also touts thermogenic properties, noting that caffeine—present in 200 to 270 milligrams per can—is a mild thermogenic agent.

In a 2025 statement, CEO John Fieldly said, “First, we’re better for you but don’t sacrifice flavor; second, Celsius delivers on more function with clinically proven fat‑burning and metabolism acceleration and third, Celsius is all about fitness.” The complaint cites this as part of the company’s marketing narrative.

Celsius claims it backs its product claims with peer‑reviewed studies approved by the Better Business Bureau’s National Advertising Division. A spokesperson told the Post that the company’s labeling meets or exceeds FDA requirements.

The lawsuit also alleges that Celsius published and funded studies that were misleading to consumers. The company’s website recommends consulting a doctor before use and limits consumption to two cans per day.

Earlier this year, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton opened an investigation into Celsius over the packaging and marketing of Alani Nu, a product with 200 milligrams of caffeine in a 12‑ounce can marketed to teens. Celsius said it would cooperate with the probe but disagreed with Paxton’s characterization.

Whether the court will grant class‑action status remains to be seen. The suit could force Celsius to rethink how it presents health claims on its labels and marketing materials.

#Celsius #HealthWashing #EnergyDrinks #Lawsuit

text:
A System That Can’t Restrain Its Own Power

Today’s election is a public judgment on a government Americans see as corrupt and unrestrained.

But this is a midterm election. Voters cannot remove the president today. They can change who controls Congress, impose a political cost, and signal that the country will not accept the government’s conduct as normal… how did our system give one president so much power, and why has it failed to restrain him?

The failure has two levels.

The first is the concentration of power itself. Decisions made in Washington change the lives of people around the world who had no part in making them. People in every country on earth are paying nearly double to eat, to heat, or to move because of the impulsive behavior of one old man.

Now consider the possibility of a nuclear strike. Tucker Carlson reported that the option of using nuclear weapons against Iran had been floated and that a decision could come by this Saturday.

The Associated Press has independently reported that officials warned regional allies to prepare for possible renewed U.S. strikes after the election, while saying the president had not made a final decision. Even the prospect of such a decision reveals the scale of power concentrated in the presidency—and the danger of leaving it there without effective restraint. And the implicit end of any form of constitutional republic.

The second failure is the political system that can put such power in one person’s hands, then offer voters such limited ways to respond.

That is how the public can look at a government and see corruption, yet still be told that the solution is simply to elect the other party. A new majority may block some abuses or investigate others. But changing who runs the machinery is not the same as changing how the machinery works.

A credible beginning requires comprehensive campaign-finance reform, radical transparency, independent redistricting and term limits. These reforms will not make every official honest or resolve every political conflict. They would make it harder for officeholders to protect themselves from voters and easier for the public to see who is influencing government decisions.

The people who benefit from the current rules have little reason to change them voluntarily.

Today’s vote can show that the public has had enough. It can change the balance of power in Congress. But its meaning will depend on what follows: whether the winners treat the result as permission to take their turn, or as a demand to change the rules that made this crisis possible.

A government capable of imposing immense costs on people at home and abroad must face limits that do not depend on the character of the person in charge. If those limits are absent, the next election may change the names in Washington while leaving the danger intact.

Reform is what would make the vote count as more than a warning.

**The US decision is based on its assessment of the ANC-led South African government’s policies and actions (or inactions), not AfriForum as the primary actor.**[](<https://t.co/EtYfOpnn69…>)

### Official US reasons
President Trump notified President Ramaphosa in a 28 October 2026 letter (with the formal announcement by USTR Jamieson Greer on 2 November) of the intention to terminate South Africa’s AGOA eligibility from 1 January 2027. The stated grounds under AGOA Section 104 include:

- Failure to establish or make continual progress on systems to combat corruption and bribery.
- Significant tariff and non-tariff barriers to US trade and investment (agricultural market access, regulatory requirements, investment protections, intellectual property).
- Actions on international security and cooperation with governments of concern to the US that risk undermining US national security and foreign policy interests.[](<https://t.co/seVk8fxxjF…>)

US Ambassador Brent Bozell described the outcome as “predictable and preventable” due to the South African government’s rejection of concerns raised by Washington. Broader reporting links the tensions to SA policies on land/expropriation, Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (BEE), foreign policy (including the ICJ case against Israel and ties with Russia, China, and others), and related issues. These are policy choices of the ANC-led government.[](<https://t.co/NBpvl4CNOq…>)

AGOA is a unilateral US preference program. The US President determines eligibility annually against the statutory criteria; the decision-maker is the US executive.

### AfriForum’s role
AfriForum and Solidarity have long lobbied in the US on property rights, the Expropriation Act (which allows for expropriation without compensation), farm security/crime, and what they describe as race-based discrimination under BEE and related laws. They have met US officials and raised these issues, which align with some of the concerns the Trump administration has voiced.[](<https://t.co/XJxFUIU6Jj…>)

AfriForum publicly blames President Ramaphosa and ANC leaders for the policies that triggered the outcome, noting they had warned about risks (including from the Expropriation Act) and that ordinary South Africans will bear the costs. Critics, including COSATU, counter that AfriForum’s lobbying and framing of issues (including around farm murders and “persecution” narratives, which the SA government rejects) damaged bilateral relations and contributed to the political climate that led to the termination.[](<https://t.co/B5CMLFzQJ9…>)

AfriForum has stated it does not support measures that punish ordinary citizens and previously argued against a full AGOA exit while acknowledging that SA government policies conflicted with the eligibility criteria.

### Bottom line
- **Primary responsibility for the policies cited by the US** rests with the ANC government, which sets trade, anti-corruption, land, transformation, and foreign policy.
- **AfriForum** is a private advocacy group whose lobbying amplified certain domestic concerns in Washington and helped shape perceptions (especially under an administration already critical of SA). It did not enact the policies or make the US decision.
- The SA government says it offered concessions in negotiations and that the US raised new issues; it is preparing support for affected sectors. AGOA covered a relatively small share of SA’s total exports (around 10% of exports to the US and ~1% of global exports in 2025).

Ashley Dupré was a 22-year-old escort charging $1,000 an hour when "Client 9" paid $4,300 for a night with her at a Washington hotel. Client 9 was the Governor of New York. Two days after the story broke, he resigned. Today she's the stepmom of TikTok star Alix Earle.

Eliot Spitzer built his career as the "Sheriff of Wall Street." As New York's attorney general he went after crooked bankers and busted prostitution rings. In 2006 he won the governor's race in a landslide. People called him a future president.

What nobody knew: he was a client of the Emperors Club VIP, a high-end escort service charging up to thousands of dollars an hour. His bank flagged a series of strange cash transfers. The feds thought it might be bribery. It turned out to be escorts.

On February 13, 2008, a young woman known to the agency as "Kristen" took a train to Washington and met him at the Mayflower Hotel. FBI wiretaps caught the booking. In the court papers he was just "Client 9."

On March 10, 2008, The New York Times broke the story. Within hours, reporters had a name for "Kristen": Ashley Dupré, an aspiring singer from New Jersey. Her MySpace music page got more than 9 million views in a week. Larry Flynt publicly offered her $1 million to pose for Hustler.

Spitzer stood at a podium with his wife Silda beside him and apologized. On March 12 he announced his resignation. He was never charged with a crime.

She was 22, and her face was on every front page in America. "I just don't want to be thought of as a monster," she told the New York Times. Years later she married, became a stepmother, and her stepdaughter Alix Earle became one of the biggest influencers on TikTok.

He walked away a former governor. She walked away as "the Spitzer call girl" forever.

Who paid the bigger price: the governor who hired her, or the 22-year-old whose name went around the world?

GFY News: Wisconsin History, Elections 

On this most important election of our lifetime, which has been repeated for over 100 yrs, you're still gonna lose, picking your favorite tyrant isn't setting you fee. 

November 3, 1914. Wisconsin voters went to the polls and were handed ten proposed amendments to the state constitution. They rejected every single one.

Among the pile: a measure to give the people the initiative and referendum, so citizens could put laws on the ballot themselves or force a vote to kill ones the legislature passed. Another to create the right of recall for elected officials other than judges, so if a bad one took office you could throw him out before his term ended. Home rule for cities and villages. A couple of state insurance schemes. Changes to how constitutional amendments get referred. All of it went down hard. The closest ones barely scraped 36 percent yes. Most sat in the mid-to-low 20s or low 30s.

Voters looked at the chance to stop being pure subjects of whatever the legislature and the parties served up, and they shrugged. They didn’t want the tools to bypass a crooked or useless official. They didn’t want the ability to recall him when he proved to be a thief or a fool. They preferred the existing arrangement: elect the man, hope he isn’t a disaster, and if he is, wait out the term while he does the damage. Representative government, they were told by the Republicans of the day, is sacred. Direct power in the hands of the voters is dangerous and has been discredited elsewhere. The Progressives had been running things, taxes had gone up, and the voters had grown tired of the reformers and their gadgets. So they voted no on the whole slate and went home.

They chose to remain sheep under whatever bad official came along. No initiative. No referendum. No recall. The herd stayed the herd. The shepherds kept the crook. Wisconsin kept the system it already had, the one that required nothing more of the citizen than showing up every couple of years and picking between the two brands of wool already on offer.

One thing you can't fail to admire about the NUP foot soldiers is their consistency in showing up, even when the political environment becomes difficult, uncomfortable and discouraging.

They have endured the heat, the dust, the frustrations and the uncertainties of political struggle. Yet one thing that stands out is their continued commitment to mobilisation, solidarity and peaceful political resistance rather than an announced resort to armed rebellion.

Look at what happens whenever a comrade falls. They gather. They stand with grieving families. They participate in burial ceremonies. Whenever there is a social cause they believe speaks to the struggles of ordinary and oppressed people, they make their presence felt.

That is the power of collective identity. People find belonging, purpose and a sense of responsibility in standing together for something they believe is bigger than themselves.

You do not have to agree with every political position of NUP to recognise the human commitment demonstrated by its foot soldiers.

Today, as we send off Kapere, let us also appreciate the people who have repeatedly shown up in moments of grief, difficulty and collective responsibility.

To Vardi, the boys of the Red Army and all NUP foot soldiers, congratulations.

There is something admirable about people who refuse to abandon one another when solidarity matters most.

text:
Since this video is generating a lot of interest I will also add a post about the historic context of this battle and how accurate this movie scene is, so that you can learn more about the tactics that were employed.

This post will answer the most frequently asked questions about this scene.

First of all, the scene is not meant to depict the entire Battle of Rocroi but only depicts the final moments of the battle, during which the last remaining Spanish tercio infantry squares performed a heroic last stand against the victorious French army.

One of the obvious criticisms of this scene is that the number of soldiers is very low. This is indeed true and is a result of the limitations of the production of this movie, but it's only partly a problem since the scene is not meant to depict the entire battle, in which both armies numbered around 25,000 men each, but only the last stages of the battle.

The number of participants should have still been higher, but not by that much, and it's unrealistic to have such expectation for a movie like this.

The more important point is that because these are the final stages of the battle, this is not a complete representation of pike and shot tactics and certain things might leave viewers confused. So I will go through all of important details one by one.

1) What happened in the actual historic Battle of Rocroi prior to this scene?

To give a short summary, the Spanish were besieging the French fortress of Rocroi. They brought a formidable army consisting of many veteran tercios who were elite infantry troops and considered the best in Europe at the time. However the entire campaign was poorly organized and led by inexperienced commander Francisco de Melo. The Spanish did not have enough heavy artillery to finish the siege quickly, enabling the large French relief army commanded by the Duke of Enghien to arrive and force a battle.

This led to the Battle of Rocroi in which the two army faced.

The Spanish army did not consist only of pike and shot infantry, as depicted in the scene, but had its own cavalry and artillery as well in the beginning of the battle.

At this point of evolution of pike and shot warfare (mid-17th century), cavalry was becoming the crucial part, which was one of the main reasons why the Spanish tercios were losing their superiority. The French gained the upper hand in this battle by a brilliant flanking manoeuvre with their cavalry led by Enghien personally. They managed to defeat the Spanish cavalry, outflank the tercios and destroy many infantry regiments of the Spanish Army of Flanders, including the German, Italian, Walloon and Burgundian regiments which fought for this international army.

This was largely a result of poor communication between troops in the Army of Flanders, a result of poor leadership and organization.

At the end only the elite Spanish infantry tercios remained which formed pike squares to defend themselves against the cavalry onslaught. The Spanish cavalry had fled the battle, following their defeat to French cavalry, and the Spanish artillery was captured by the French, meaning that the tercios were getting fired at by their own cannons!

They were left to defend themselves against the overwhelmingly larger French army.

And this is where this scene begins...

2) Why didn't the tercio infantry simply try to retreat in order instead of facing such superior army?

At the time there was much confusion and the Spanish tercios still hoped that a relief army, led by commander Jean de Beck, would arrive.

Had Beck arrived, he could have probably forced the French, who had sustained loses as well, to retreat.

However Beck was not coming, leaving the tercios on their own. They couldn't know this, of course. The French surrounded them and fired at them with cannons they had captured.

3) Why did the Spanish tercios just stand in formation instead of attacking?

Without their own cavalry and with a limited number of musketeers, the Spanish had little to offer offensively. By marching forward and attacking the French artillery, they would have exposed themselves to a cavalry attack. Their best bet to survive was to keep the defensive formation and commit to forming an impregnable pike square.

4) Why did the French stop firing with the cannons, given how successful this tactic was for which the tercios had no answer?

Cannons overheated. There was also limited ammunition. The French needed to finish the battle quick as they were nervous about the Spanish receiving possible reinforcements.

5) The French cavalry tactics in the scene. How accurate?

Largely accurate. While some mentioned that the French could have performed a "caracole" tactic, successively firing at the tercio infantry in a disciplined formation without engaging them, the caracole was already out of fashion at that time since muskets were more powerful and pistol-armed cavalry did not want to risk getting into fire fights with musketeers. Instead they tried something like shown here, trying to pressure the tercio from all sides and hoping it would break.

The problem with cavalry in this scene is that they start firing their pistols way too early, from way too far. These pistols had very short range and firing them from so far would be completely useless. In reality they would have fired them much much closer, as close that "they could see the white in the eyes of their enemies", as the saying was at the time.

6) French infantry tactics.

Mostly accurate, as far as the push of pike is concerned. It was a brutal type of fighting which must have looked pretty much like depicted in the scene.

As cavalry was unable to break the pike square on its own, and with ammunition being very limited in those times, there was no other choice from the French but to send infantry.

However the one thing that's missing in this scene were the French musketeers. They were also crucial for the victory as they were able to shoot at Spanish tercios pretty much unopposed after the Spanish lost their cavalry, as there was no offensive threat from the Spanish left. To break up the remaining Spanish tercios, the French would also use their own musketeers to skirmish and shoot at the large infantry blocks, for as long as they had ammunition left.

7) Conclusion.

The scene is very accurate in terms of depicting a specific segment of pike and shot warfare, such as it unfolded in the last stages of the Battle of Rocroi. There are some inaccuracies, and more importantly, it does not depict how an entire pike and shot battle would look like at the time.

A typical pike and shot battle would start with artillery duel, fights between cavalry regiments, and maybe some skirmishing between musketeers. None of this is shown here. This scene primarily shows how a pike square would fight under pressure, and in this particular aspect of pike and shot warfare it's quite accurate.

Overall, we should be really really grateful for this scene, they did amazing with the limited resources they had.
