text:
JESUS REVEALS THE MYSTERY 

This teaching is the concluding lesson in a Grace Ambassadors series on Jesus’ earthly ministry. 

It contrasts knowing Christ “after the flesh” (His prophetic ministry to Israel) with knowing Him according to the mystery revealed to Paul after the ascension. 

The central truth is that the body of Christ receives its identity, gospel, and instructions from the heavenly revelation given to Paul, not from the earthly teachings, parables, or kingdom program recorded in the Gospels and early Acts.

10 Key Points  

1.  Jesus’ earthly ministry was exclusively to the lost sheep of the house of Israel as the minister of the circumcision (Matthew 15:24; Romans 15:8). His teaching, signs, and kingdom offer fulfilled prophecy and were not addressed to the body of Christ.

2.  After the resurrection, Jesus spent forty days speaking of things pertaining to the kingdom of God (Acts 1:3). The apostles’ expectation remained the restoration of the kingdom to Israel (Acts 1:6). That program was interrupted, not completed.

3.  Paul declares that we know Christ no more after the flesh (2 Corinthians 5:16). A new revelation was given when the risen Christ appeared to Saul and committed to him the dispensation of the grace of God and the mystery which had been hid from ages and generations (Ephesians 3:1–9; Colossians 1:25–26).

4.  The mystery is that Gentiles are fellow heirs and of the same body with Jewish believers in Christ, forming one new man in which there is neither Jew nor Gentile (Ephesians 2:15; 3:6; Galatians 3:28). This was not made known in other ages.

5.  The body of Christ is a new creature with a heavenly position and hope. Believers are already seated in heavenly places in Christ (Ephesians 2:6) and possess a citizenship that is in heaven (Philippians 3:20). There is no claim to Israel’s land, temple, or earthly kingdom.

6.  Jesus’ current ministry is from heaven as Head of the body. He is not presently establishing the earthly kingdom or fulfilling the prophetic program. That program resumes after the body is caught away.

7.  The gospel that saves today is the one Paul delivered first of all: Christ died for our sins, was buried, and rose again (1 Corinthians 15:1–4), received by faith apart from works (Ephesians 2:8–9; Romans 4:5). It is not the kingdom gospel of repentance and water baptism preached to Israel.

8.  Signs, the coming of the Lord in judgment, and the prophetic timeline belong to Israel’s program. The body is not watching for those signs. It is watching for the blessed hope and the catching away (Titus 2:13; 1 Thessalonians 4:16–17).

9.  The body is complete in Christ (Colossians 2:10) and sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise (Ephesians 1:13). Its doctrine, reproof, correction, and instruction in righteousness are found in Romans through Philemon. The Gospels and the Hebrew epistles remain true in their place but are not written to the body.

10.  Knowing Jesus according to the mystery produces full assurance and right division. Ignoring the distinction between His earthly ministry and the revelation given to Paul results in mixing programs, loss of the heavenly calling, and confusion about the present dispensation of grace.

Grace and peace

step 3: make the video in Seedance 2.5

upload the first frame as image 1 and the character sheet as image 2

settings: 1080p, 15 sec,

Prompt:
=== REFERENCE MAP ===

<<<image_1>>> → exact FIRST FRAME and master reference for location, light, framing and camera look. Woman standing thigh-deep in shallow clear turquoise water, both hands pushed into her wet hair on top of her head, big bright smile, eyes on the lens. White sand beach with palm trees and a few tiny distant beachgoers at left, a rocky headland with a natural sea arch at right, a dark green hill far right, blue sky with long white streaky clouds. Sun high and slightly behind camera-left.

<<<image_2>>> → identity lock for <<<CHAR_A>>>: face, freckles, tan, hair, body and wardrobe. Her face always follows <<<image_2>>> exactly, from every angle, above all in the close-up and the profile.

=== CHARACTER ===

<<<CHAR_A>>> → early-to-mid 20s, long dark-brown curly hair, wet and slicked back from a center part, brown eyes, deep golden sun-tan, freckles and a sun-flushed nose and cheeks, bright white smile, water droplets on her face, shoulders and arms. Rust-terracotta scoop-neck tank top with darker wet patches, white gauzy sarong tied at her left hip. Her RIGHT hand is her talking hand; her LEFT hand handles her hair. Never swap.

The person filming is a friend wading in the water with her, never seen, never speaks. Their only sound is one soft wordless breath of a laugh. Their legs push through the water as they move, so every camera move has a real wading rhythm.

FRAMING: always on her face, hair and upper body. Close-ups are on her face only.

=== EMOTIONAL CORE ===

She is not selling. She is letting one close friend in on something that genuinely amazes her. Her smile starts in the eyes first. Real disbelief on "millions of views," quiet awe on "look at the skin," playful pride on "that old camera feel," a genuine laugh that breaks out of her on "it's all AI," then a quiet glassy-eyed moment of wonder, and warm generosity on "follow me." Her face is alive between every word: micro-reactions, squints at the sun, small breaths, blinks, brows that move with her thoughts. Nothing posed, nothing frozen, nothing performed.

=== SHOT (15s, one continuous handheld take, no cuts — the filmer physically moves around her) ===

ANGLE 1 — FRONT, THE HOOK (0.0–2.6s)

EFFECT: unsteady handheld, already moving in frame 0

Frame 0.0 is exactly <<<image_1>>>, no settle-in. Camera: a 2003-era compact digital camera in video mode, held by one hand at her chest height about 1 meter away, never steady: constant drift, small dips, late corrections, horizon never level for long. A small hard light on the camera is on the whole time, never firing, never changing, giving the hot front-lit look of the photo.

She slowly slides both hands down out of her hair; water runs down her neck and arms, her hands fall loosely. Her big smile softens into a knowing, amused smile, eyes on the lens, a small lean in. She speaks: "Everyone's making videos like this right now..." On "LIKE THIS" her right hand draws one loose circle in the air, taking in the sea, the beach and herself. The "..." is a real half-second beat: lips parted, a small inhale, eyes narrowing with a private smile.

Sound: small waves lapping around her legs, a soft sea breeze, distant surf, faint beach voices.

ANGLE 2 — THREE-QUARTER, THE SEA ARCH (2.6–4.4s)

EFFECT: handheld arc to the right while wading + reactive late correction

Still speaking, she turns her head and shoulders slightly toward the horizon as the filmer wades two steps to the right around her, so the frame becomes a three-quarter view of her face with the rocky sea arch and headland behind her. "...and they're pulling millions of views." On "MILLIONS" her brows lift and she gives a tiny disbelieving head shake, a laugh threatening at the corners of her mouth. Her eyes drift to the horizon, then slide back to the lens. The camera arrives a beat late and briefly clips her shoulder at the frame edge before it corrects.

Sound: the filmer's legs pushing through water, her voice continuous and clear.

ANGLE 3 — SKIN CLOSE-UP (4.4–5.6s)

EFFECT: physical lean-in + autofocus hunt-and-lock (about 1 second)

She turns back toward the lens. Softly, almost tenderly: "Look at the skin," — the filmer leans the camera in by hand until the lens is about 30 cm from her face. For about a second the frame is her cheek, nose and one brown eye in bright sun: freckles, visible pores, sun flush, fine peach fuzz glowing, tiny salt-dried patches, water droplets beading on her cheekbone, a wet strand stuck to her temple, the iris detail and wet catchlight of her eye. Her right fingertips graze her cheekbone. Her eyes soften with a small private smile. Focus breathes, hunts, and locks. The frame keeps shaking. A hand movement toward her face, never a zoom or crop.

ANGLE 4 — LOW ANGLE AT THE WATERLINE (5.6–6.8s)

EFFECT: handheld dip to water level + auto-exposure metering + droplets near the lens

"that old camera feel," — as she says it, the filmer pulls back and dips the camera low, just above the water surface, looking up at her. The bottom of the frame is moving turquoise water with sun sparkles and small splashes close to the lens; she rises above it against the deep blue sky and white clouds. Her right hand opens loosely toward the lens, palm up, presenting the camera itself, with a proud crooked grin. The auto-exposure meters for the bright sky: clouds recover detail, her skin settles, slow and silent. A camera reaction, never a light change.

Sound: water lapping close to the mic, louder and nearer for a moment.

ANGLE 5 — BACKLIT HAIR (6.8–8.0s)

EFFECT: handheld rise + subtle sun flare + wind on hair

The camera rises back toward her shoulder height and drifts slightly left so the sun sits behind her. "every strand of hair —" her left hand lifts a few wet curls off her shoulder and lets them fall slowly through her fingers against the bright sky. The strands separate, glow at the edges, glisten and drip; flyaways lift in the breeze. A subtle soft sun flare washes one corner of the frame and passes. Her eyes follow the strands, then return to the lens.

ANGLE 6 — FRONT, THE LAUGH (8.0–9.4s)

EFFECT: laugh bounce + wave sway

The camera settles back in front of her at about 1 meter. "it's all AI." A small wave rolls in and bumps her thighs; she sways with it and a genuine laugh breaks out of her on the last word, caught off guard, the words still clear before the laugh takes over. Behind the camera the filmer lets out one soft breath of a laugh and the frame bounces with it and the wave for about a second. Her head tips back, eyes crinkle, wet hair swings and flicks sparkling droplets.

ANGLE 6 continued — THE SOUL BEAT (9.4–10.5s, no words)

The laugh melts into quiet wonder. She looks back into the lens; her eyes go slightly glassy and soft, a slow blink, a small exhale through parted lips, a tiny almost-shy smile, a slight head tilt, as if she still can't quite believe it and is glad she gets to share it. The breeze moves a strand across her cheek; she leaves it. The camera breathes with the filmer, close and unsteady.

Sound: the sea, the breeze, her soft exhale.

ANGLE 7 — WALKING BACK, THE OFFER (10.5–13.0s)

EFFECT: handheld follow while wading forward

She starts wading slowly backward into deeper water, eyes on the lens, and the filmer wades forward to follow, the frame bobbing with each step. "Follow me." — soft, warm and inviting, with a small nod. Then, with a generous smile: "I'm sharing the whole workflow for free." On "WHOLE WORKFLOW" her right hand gives one small open-handed offer toward the lens; on "FREE" a playful little shrug and a quick wink. Water swirls around her hips and the sarong.

Sound: both of them sloshing through the water, her voice clear over it.

ANGLE 7 continued — THE BUTTON (13.0–15.0s)

EFFECT: water on the lens + hard cut on motion

Grinning, she bends, scoops seawater with both hands and flings it straight at the lens. Real droplets hit the lens and bead and streak across it, softening the image; through the wet blur she is laughing. Cut at exactly 15.0s, mid-splash, droplets still running down the lens. No hold, no fade, no black.

Sound: the scoop and splash, water pattering on the camera, her laugh, a startled gasp-laugh from the filmer.

=== ALLOWED CAMERA / LENS BEHAVIOUR (nothing else) ===

Continuous unsteady handheld 0–15s with the filmer physically wading around her: arc to three-quarter (1x), lean-in close-up (1x), dip to the waterline (1x), rise for the backlit hair (1x), return to front (1x), follow while wading forward (1x). Frame-edge clip (1x). Autofocus hunt-and-lock (2x, plus focus breathing in the close-up). Gradual auto-exposure metering (1x). Subtle sun flare (1x). Laugh-and-wave bounce (1x). Water droplets on the lens (1x). Hard cut on motion at 15.0s, the only cut.

NEVER: other cuts, whips, smears, zoom, punch-ins, crops, drone or crane moves, gimbal smoothness, stabilisation, slow motion, speed ramps, colour grading, transitions, flash pops, whooshes, shutter or click sounds, music, on-screen text, captions.

=== HARD RULES ===

Exactly 15 seconds, one continuous real-time take. Frame 0.0 = <<<image_1>>> exactly. Every angle change happens by the filmer physically moving, never by a cut.

Identity lock: <<<CHAR_A>>> matches <<<image_2>>> from every angle: front, three-quarter, close-up and low angle. Face, freckles, tan, curly hair, tank top and sarong never change or morph.

SKIN IS NEVER SMOOTH: visible pores, freckles, sun flush, peach fuzz, water droplets, wet sheen and tiny unevenness, above all in the close-up. No smoothing, no retouching, no waxy or plastic skin, no beauty filter. The single most important rule.

WATER IS REAL: hair stays wet with clumped curls, droplets roll down with gravity, waves move continuously, light shimmers on the sandy bottom, wet fabric stays darker in patches, water swirls around her as she wades.

NO LIGHT EVER CHANGES. The sun stays high and constant, the on-camera light stays constant. Every brightness shift is the camera's auto-exposure, slow, gradual and silent. The flare is a lens reaction to the sun's position, not a light change.

Every movement has a visible beginning, middle and end. Nobody teleports, nothing starts already mid-motion.

Her gestures are all different: the scene circle ("like this"), the head shake ("millions"), fingertips on cheek ("the skin"), open palm to the lens ("camera feel"), strands through fingers ("hair"), the open-handed offer ("whole workflow"). None point at her own chest or body.

Only one person close to camera. The distant beachgoers stay tiny, far away and out of focus; no one approaches.

Eyes: they land on the lens casually and drift off to the horizon and back, except the hook, the soul beat and "follow me," where they hold the lens warmly. Natural blinks, wet catchlights, always alive.

=== DIALOGUE — spoken exactly once, exactly as written, in order ===

<<<CHAR_A>>>: "Everyone's making videos like this right now... and they're pulling millions of views."

<<<CHAR_A>>>: "Look at the skin, that old camera feel, every strand of hair — it's all AI."

<<<CHAR_A>>>: "Follow me. I'm sharing the whole workflow for free."

No added words, repeats, skipped words or extra lines. Exact lip-sync with natural mouth shapes and visible tongue and teeth on the right sounds.

=== VOICE (natural and perfectly clear) ===

A real, natural, beautiful young American woman's voice: soft, warm, gently husky, talking to one friend she likes. Not a voice-over, not a presenter, not breathy-sexy. Natural conversational speed, never rushed, never dragged.

DICTION: every word fully pronounced and easy to understand. Clean consonants on "videos," "millions," "skin," "camera," "strand," "AI," "workflow," "free." No mumbling, no swallowed endings, no words lost to wind or water.

NATURAL TEXTURE: small real breaths between phrases, light vocal fry only at phrase ends, a soft mouth click, the real half-second pause after "right now...", the smile audible in her voice, the laugh starting only after "it's all AI" is fully spoken.

DELIVERY ARC: line 1 amused, then quiet disbelief; line 2 tender and sensory, then the real laugh; line 3 gentle and generous, "follow me" soft and close, "for free" with a smile you can hear.

=== AUDIO ===

Built-in compact camera mic: thin, slight hiss, light auto-gain, faint handling noise, real and unpolished. HER VOICE ALWAYS SITS ON TOP: when she speaks, wind and water drop under her voice so every word is clean and intelligible; between lines the wind and sea come back up. Her voice is close and intimate in the close-up, a little more open in the three-quarter and low angles, never distorted.

Ambient: small waves lapping around her legs, both of them wading and sloshing, a soft sea breeze, distant surf on the headland, faint beach voices, droplets falling from her hair, water close to the mic in the low angle, the final splash and water hitting the camera. Camera moves, focus and exposure changes are silent. No music.

=== LOOK (MATCH <<<image_1>>>) ===

Early-2000s compact digital camera beach video. Hard frontal on-camera light plus bright high sun: hot, glossy highlights on wet skin, forehead, nose and shoulders, slightly blown. Saturated turquoise water, deep blue sky, crisp white clouds. Low dynamic range, visible sensor noise and fine grain, slight softness with sharp eyes, light compression, faint chromatic fringing on bright edges, mild barrel distortion at the frame edges in the low angle. Candid, amateur, unpolished, straight from a camera's memory card. No cinematic look, no grade, no text.

=== NEGATIVES ===

No cuts, no camera switch, no slow motion, no zoom, no gimbal smoothness, no drone shots. Camera never visible, no selfie arm. No one else near the camera. No face, hair, hand, top or sarong morphing, no identity drift between angles, no duplicate fingers. No plastic skin, no dry hair, no lip-sync drift, no robotic or synthetic voice, no muffled words, no frozen or blank face between lines. No captions, subtitles, logos or watermarks. No flash pop, no white frame, no fade, no black ending.

Today’s commemorated feasts and saints
Martyrs Akepsimas the Bishop, Joseph the Presbyter, and Aeithalas the Deacon, of Persia (4th c.). Consecration of the Church of the Holy Great Martyr George in Lydda (4th c.). Martyrs Eudoxios, Agapios, Atticus, Marinus, Oceanus, Eustratios, Karterios, Nikopolitianos, Styrax, and Tobias, at Sebaste (ca. 320). Ven. Acepsimas, Hermit, of Cyrrhus in Syria (4th c.). St. Snandulia of Persia (4th c.).

Hieromartyrs Akepsimas, Bishop in Persia, Presbyter Joseph, and Deacon Aeithalas
Commemorated on November 3
Martyrs Akepsimas the Bishop, Joseph the Presbyter and Aeithalas (Aeithalás) the Deacon of Persia were leaders of the Christian Church in the Persian city of Naesson. His flock devotedly loved their hierarch for his ascetic life and tireless pastoral work.

The emperor Sapor ordered his men to seek out and kill Christian clergy. Saint Akepsimas also was arrested, even though he was already an eighty-year-old man. They took him to the city of Arbela, where he came before the judge Ardarkh, a pagan priest of the sun god. The holy Elder refused to offer sacrifice to the Persian gods. For this he was fiercely beaten and thrown into prison, where on the following day the seventy-year-old priest Joseph and the deacon Aeithalas were severely beaten and thrown into jail with him. For three years the saints were held in confinement, and suffered from hunger and thirst.

Emperor Sapor came to the temple of the god of fire, located not far from Arbela, and wanted to take a look at the three holy martyrs. Exhausted and covered with festering wounds, the saints were brought before the emperor. When he asked them to worship the pagan gods they firmly refused, confessing their faith in Christ instead.

The holy bishop was beheaded, but the presbyter and deacon were taken into the city to be stoned.

The execution of the presbyter Joseph was prolonged for several hours. A guard was placed near the place of execution, so that Christians would not take the body of the holy martyr. On the fourth night a strong windstorm raged near the city, lightning killed the guard, the wind tossed stones about, and the body of Saint Joseph disappeared.

Deacon Aeithalas was taken to the village of Patrias, where he was stoned. Christians secretly buried his body.  A tree grew on the saint’s grave, and its fruit brought healings.

text:
The Diary Of A CEO: James Talarico: Here Is How They Designed The System To Keep You Poor! (uploaded Nov 2, 2026 · 1h 36m)

@StevenBartlett  sits down with Texas state Rep. James Talarico, the Democratic U.S. Senate nominee facing Republican Ken Paxton in today's election. Talarico argues the U.S. has "crony capitalism," not capitalism, and traces the shift to the 1971 Powell memo and 50 years of trickle-down economics. He says three men (Musk, Zuckerberg and Bezos) own more wealth than the entire middle class.

His proposed fixes:

Close tax loopholes such as carried interest, capital gains, and write-offs for private jets and yachts, and explore wealth taxes.
Raise the minimum wage, expand overtime pay, rebuild unions and expand the child tax credit.
Break up healthcare monopolies, a plan he drew up with Mark Cuban that names CVS.
On AI, regulation that protects workers, kids and democracy, plus an "AI dividend" and AI taxes.
He says the Iran war costs about $1B a day and is pushing up gas prices, blames tariffs for higher costs, and offers to work with Trump on housing, healthcare and child care.

Key points

Taxes: he says simply collecting what the top 1% already owes would raise about $172B a year. He's "interested in" wealth taxes but admits they're hard to put in place. He opposes a Texas state income tax and says the fix has to be federal.
Musk and Tesla: he's "proud of Tesla" and isn't trying to ban billionaires, but argues Tesla succeeded on federal investment and its workers should share in the gains. He says Musk has committed millions of dollars to defeat him.
Healthcare antitrust: he'd break up companies that own the insurer, the PBM and the pharmacy, with CVS as the example. He says last year's healthcare cuts would mean 51,000 needless deaths a year.
AI and robotics:His priorities are workers, children and democracy (deepfake ads).
He backs an AI dividend and wants humans supervising self-driving trucks.
Bartlett mentions Musk's forecast of over 1 billion humanoid robots within a decade, Tesla's Cybercabs and roughly 400K–500K+ Texas driving jobs.

Macro:He says the Iran war costs about $1B a day and that tariffs made "everything more expensive."
He wants Congress to withhold war funding until there are clear objectives.
He wants a regional deal covering the Strait of Hormuz and the nuclear issue.

The race:Bartlett says some polls show Talarico ahead "by a couple of points."
Talarico says he has 59K volunteers and more than 1M donors.
He has pledged to serve only two terms.

What it means for investors How it could help investors
Housing: he says he'd "slash the red tape" and build "millions of new homes," which could help homebuilders and building-materials companies. He named no companies.
Energy and consumer costs: he wants a negotiated end to the Iran war, which would mean lower oil risk premiums and relief for consumers.
Consumer demand: a higher minimum wage, more overtime pay, an expanded child tax credit and child care. He says "a country that invests in its people grows faster."
Lower drug prices: more healthcare competition, citing Mark Cuban's Cost Plus Drugs (a private company).
How it could hurt investors (risks)
Taxes on capital: closing the carried-interest and capital-gains loopholes, plus possible wealth taxes, would hit high-net-worth investors and private equity and hedge-fund economics.
CVS Health (CVS): he named it as the example of the insurer-PBM-pharmacy companies he'd break up.
Tesla (TSLA) and AI: AI regulation, AI taxes, an AI dividend and humans supervising autonomous trucks could weigh on the robotaxi and automation story.
Labor costs: higher wages, more overtime pay and stronger unions would raise costs for big employers. He singles out Walmart (WMT), saying taxpayers cover its workers' healthcare through Medicaid.
Scale: this is one Senate seat, voted on today. These are campaign positions, not passed policy.

Full video from The Diary Of A CEO: https://t.co/kUZmpjddcJ

text:
🚨#BREAKING: Outrage is erupting in Georgia after an HOA began fining a young family $25 PER DAY for GROWING VEGETABLES in their own yard to FEED THEIR KIDS...

...the family is now being charged $750 because the HOA said the vegetables were "unsightly" and they refused to remove them

Yes, they planted peppers in their OWN FRONT YARD and their HOA is charging $25/day until it’s gone.

Their names are Alex Duarte and Shawn Richardson, and they live in Acworth, Georgia.

They grow peppers, tomatoes, habaneros, and herbs in trough gardens out front because in Alex's words,

“We don’t have a lot of money. The economy’s really tight right now.”

In June, the HOA’s community manager sent a notice telling them to remove the garden.

So Alex Duarte asked what she could do.

She offered to paint the beds ANY COLOR the board chose.

She offered a wood surround.
A brick surround.
A rock surround.
Anything to keep her garden.

At an appeal meeting she recorded, the board said it had gotten FOUR complaints of "unsightly yard".

So Alex asked them to define what was unsightly so they could reach a resolution.

The answer: it’s not aesthetically pleasing.

What about it?

“All of it. It's all got to go."

...then on September 28th, the fines started.

$25 a day.

By a week before Halloween, the balance was approaching $750.

So the family filed a complaint with the Secretary of State... but the meter keeps running.

They can’t even put a sign in their yard.

So they put up a Halloween tombstone for their garden instead.

Alex’s words: “I don’t wanna lose one of the ways I feed my family because three people decided that they didn’t like my yard.”

WHAT ARE WE DOING HERE?!!!!!!!!

text:
SOCOM II Legacy - Patch v0.4.5

Here’s what we’ve been working on since the last playtest! A lot of you have been asking when the next one will be—we’ll keep you posted as soon as we have a date. Thanks for playing and sending in your feedback. It’s helping us track down issues and get SOCOM II Legacy ready for the next round!

This update brings grenade timing corrections, door and bomb-planting fixes, controller improvements, a redesigned replay viewer, and the first set of r0004 changes.

💥 GRENADES & EXPLOSIVES

• Fixed your own grenade killing you after its explosion had already played.
• Online frag explosions now follow the same clock on clients and the match server.
• The timing correction also covers C4, claymores, mines, launcher rounds, and rockets on a laggy host.
• M203, MGL, and M79 rounds are judged at the moment they were fired. Valid shots fired while moving are no longer incorrectly rejected because they reached the server later.
• If the server refuses a launched round, its ammunition is returned.
• Smoke and flash detonations no longer apply inappropriate camera shake.
• Flashbang effects follow the server’s blast checks.
• Planted-bomb explosions correctly affect eligible placed explosives and hostages.
🚪 DOORS & INTERACTIONS
• Doors reset with each round.
• Fixed getting partially stuck inside a closed door with no prompt or way to open it, as reported on Vigilance.
• Improved synchronization when a door changes direction during an existing animation.
• Door presses respond locally while awaiting server confirmation.
• Improved response for switches, gate levers, and cranes.
💣 BOMB PLANTING
• Planting follows where you aim at the target, using the original game’s rule, instead of requiring its exact center.
• The target is checked throughout the planting hold.
• Removed the carried bomb’s compass marker to match the original behavior.
🎮 r0004 UPDATE — FIRST SET OF CHANGES
• Updated the M60E3’s standing accuracy settings and configured firing interval to match r0004.
• Voice Modulation defaults to OFF and correctly applies saved settings when entering matches and starting rounds.
• Rescued hostages award credit only once and are protected from further damage.
• Corrected commands being accepted for already-rescued hostages.
• Updated antenna durability on the affected maps.
• Prevented equipping a second C4 item.
• Successful majority votes remove the target immediately.
• Vote-menu availability follows the original camera restrictions when dead and watching another player.
• Added the appropriate Team Switch Error handling when a team change arrives while the Armory is open.
The r0004 work is being introduced in stages; this update does not contain the entire original patch.

🏃 MOVEMENT

• Corrected the prone drop, prone pop, and turning behavior using captures of the original.
• Improved crouch-to-prone transitions, interruption, and repeated stance inputs.
• Corrected diagonal crouch movement in SEPARATE mode.
• Improved prone body alignment, camera position, and aiming limits on slopes.
• Improved wall-end collision and movement around corners.
• Corrected ladder mounting contact requirements.
• Prevented turret-mount prompts during incompatible traversal actions.
🎯 WEAPONS & COMBAT
• Corrected bullet penetration to use the struck material’s penetration value.
• Corrected hits on players behind glass that stopped a round.
• Bullets continue through bodies with the appropriate reduction, and remote tracers follow their continued path.
• Corrected scoped sway and improved validation of scoped and binocular aiming.
• Corrected firing restrictions and timing for turrets and launched rounds.
• Corrected throw-release restrictions during animations that prevent firing.
• Removed an unsupported firing-delay restriction from the detonator.
🤖 BOTS
• Bots open doors that actually block their route and stop pressing doors that do not.
• Corrected launcher raise/lower timing and switching back to rifles, addressing repeated refused launcher shots.
• Improved pursuit in supported Frostfire and Vigilance respawn rooms.
• Improved navigation around corners, ramps, blocked routes, and other bots.
• Fixed bot refill after supported map rotation.
• Matches containing bots are marked unranked.
• Corrected the server-owned lobby’s displayed round settings.

📺 REPLAY VIEWER

• Redesigned the viewer to match the rest of the menus on desktop and phone.
• Playback waits until the world finishes loading.
• Every round is marked on the timeline, with a round counter.
• Added previous/next-round controls and clearer paused-state feedback.
• Player-follow camera is the default, with camera choices preserved.
🔊 HUD & AUDIO
• Weapon pickups display what you are taking, such as TAKE M4A1.
• Bodies carrying two weapons offer separate pickup actions.
• Additional actions appear to the right and left of the main prompt, with their original fade behavior.
• Improved action captions and availability colors.
• Long taunts wrap inside the message window.
• Corrected overlapping rank icons in the lobby and scoreboard.
• Improved objective and elimination-message layout.
• Added passing-bullet audio for nearby rounds fired by other players.
• Corrected world-audio behavior during round-end screens.
• Improved layering of smoke, footprints, impact marks, and scorch effects.

🗳️ ROUNDS & VOTES

• Vote thresholds count human teammates only, including the target.
• Votes, withdrawals, and kicks are recorded in the match log by game.
• Bots no longer inflate the majority required to remove a human player.
The reported case where selecting a vote appeared to do nothing remains under investigation.
🎛️ CONTROLLER
• Stance Mode—COMBINED or SEPARATE—is the first row in Controller settings and Button Mapping.
• Essential menu D-pad directions stay bound when remapping controls.
• Saved remaps with conflicting stance/menu bindings are repaired at startup.
• Extra bindings have their own rows, including double-button and combination inputs.
• Added controls to remove, clear, and restore extra bindings.
• Improved separate crouch/prone binding behavior.
• Added vibration when the player takes a surviving hit.
⚡ LOADING & STABILITY
• Lobby pre-compilation remains enabled. Reported first-frame loading improved from 15–20 seconds to under a second.
• The loading screen stays visible until the match draws.
• If a match cannot mount, the loading screen releases immediately instead of waiting for its fallback timeout.
• Reduced retained audio and loading memory, particularly with the Xbox preset.
• Reduced background menu work during Xbox matches.
• Improved cleanup after map rotation and graphics-device-loss messages.
• Pages left open across an update offer a reload when required files are no longer available.
🖥️ LAUNCHER & FILE TRANSFER
• Added local-network game-file transfer with pairing codes, QR support, verification, and resume support.
• Added an optional Skip Menu setting.
• Improved mobile navigation, room-list readability, and small-screen layouts.
• Game Details displays the selected game’s settings more accurately.
• Deployment announcements now report actual version releases, rather than every code landing.
📝 EARLIER RELEASE: v0.4.4

• Closed the release site’s direct map downloads and dev mode.
• That release contained no gameplay changes.

🔧 KNOWN ISSUES & FOLLOW-UP WORK

• On phones, a short grenade hold can sometimes throw at full power—reported around one throw in three. This predates v0.4.5 and remains under investigation.
• The Crossroads blown-bridge freeze fix is in the next patch, already undergoing testing.
• During rollout, hosts awaiting their automatic update may briefly retain the old grenade clock.
• The shotgun damage correction is submitted separately for review and is not included in this release.
• M4A1SD and 552SD audio remain under investigation; no production sound-radius fix is included.
• The experimental HD option remains disabled while work continues.
Found something? Post it in the bug channel with the map and what you were doing.
See you in the lobby!

🔔 TODAY THE CHURCH CELEBRATES  
St. Martin de Porres  
November 3

🕊️ WHAT WE REMEMBER  
St. Martin de Porres was a Dominican lay brother from Peru who devoted his life to prayer, caring for the sick and serving the poor. Known for his humility and kindness, he treated everyone with dignity and love.

🔥 WHY IT MATTERS  
St. Martin reminds us that holiness is found in humble service. Every person deserves compassion, and even the simplest acts of kindness can reflect Christ's love.

👣 HOW WE LIVE IT  
Look for someone who may need a helping hand today. Offer your time, share what you have or show kindness to someone who might otherwise go unnoticed.

❓ CATHOLIC CURIOUS?  
Why do Catholics have patron saints?

Patron saints are holy men and women recognized as special intercessors for particular people, professions or needs. St. Martin de Porres is a patron saint of social justice and those who work for racial harmony.

Catholics ask the saints to pray with and for us, just as we ask family and friends for their prayers.

Curious about the Catholic faith? OCIA (Order of Christian Initiation of Adults) begins at your parish. Come explore, ask questions and discover the Catholic faith! https://t.co/R23KOlxBiW

St. Martin de Porres, teach us to serve with humility, love without distinction and recognize Christ in everyone we meet. Pray for us. 🙏

text:
The partnership thesis is becoming reality. $PROF

I’ve written before that Profound Medical’s growth would depend on more than developing a differentiated technology. It would require strategic partnerships to expand distribution, simplify hospital adoption and accelerate installations.

The Cook Medical announcement is exactly the kind of development I was looking for.

Cook’s Interventional MRI Division will distribute TULSA-PRO in the U.S. through its Copernicus program, combining:

Siemens Healthineers MRI technology.
Cook’s turnkey interventional MRI suite.
TULSA-PRO prostate treatment technology.
Clinical training and implementation support.

This is bigger than adding another distributor. It creates an opportunity to offer hospitals an integrated MRI-guided treatment solution rather than selling TULSA-PRO as a standalone system.

And here’s the detail I particularly like:

Profound retains direct sales of its single-use treatment kits and service contracts.

That means Cook can help expand the installed base, while Profound participates in the recurring revenue generated as procedure volumes grow.

It also complements Profound’s existing Siemens relationship, creating another route to overcome MRI infrastructure barriers.

Of course, purchase commitments and sales targets haven’t been disclosed. Execution is what matters next.

But the strategy is taking shape: technology + clinical evidence + MRI partners + distribution + recurring revenue.

This is the partnership-led growth model I’ve been anticipating.

Lecture: 
Critical Race Theory, 
Contested Narratives, 
and Complex Social Systems

For students of 
Law, 
Political Science, 
Psychiatry, 
and Social Anthropology

The 2021 Facebook post 
by William Ronald Yee 
posed a series of pointed questions 
about 
Critical Race Theory (CRT), 
crime patterns in Democratic-led cities, 
gun policy, 
voting behavior, 
parental authority, 
and the Bill of Rights. 

These questions
emerged 
amid debates over 
curriculum, 
school board meetings, 
and broader cultural shifts. 

The post’s backstory 
references concerns 
about narrative control, 
institutional responses 
that framed some parental opposition 
as potentially criminal, 
policy outcomes on crime and borders, 
and political realignment.

This lecture treats those questions 
as prompts for analysis 
rather than as settled premises. 

We examine them through five lenses
—self-organizing systems, 
Murphy’s Law, 
Pandora’s Box, 
plausible deniability, 
and the Butterfly Effect
—while drawing on the relevant disciplines. 

The goal is clarity on 
origins, 
evidence, 
mechanisms, 
and trade-offs, 
not endorsement 
of any party or ideology.

Critical Race Theory: 
Origins and Core Claims

CRT emerged in U.S. legal academia 
in the late 1970s and 1980s, 
associated with scholars including 
Derrick Bell, 
Kimberlé Crenshaw, 
Richard Delgado, 
and others. 

It grew from critical legal studies 
and dissatisfaction 
with the pace and limits 
of post-civil-rights reforms. 

Key propositions 
commonly associated with it 
include: 
race as a social construct 
used to organize hierarchy; 
racism as ordinary and systemic 
rather than merely aberrant individual prejudice; 
“interest convergence” 
(Bell), 
in which advances for racial minorities 
often occur 
when they align with dominant interests; 
law as a tool 
that can construct 
and legitimize 
racial categories; 
and the insufficiency 
of formal colorblindness 
or liberal procedural reforms alone.⁠
Wikipedia

It is not a single unified doctrine 
with a fixed syllabus. 

In K-12 settings, 
explicit courses labeled “CRT” 
are rare. 

Surveys of students 
indicate varying exposure 
to related concepts 
such as systemic racism, 
white privilege, 
or claims that America 
is fundamentally racist
—sometimes presented as fact, 
sometimes not
—depending on school 
and locality. 

Implementation is contested,
 with some districts 
adopting equity frameworks 
or professional development 
drawing on similar ideas,
and others restricting them.
⁠Educationnext

From a legal perspective, 
CRT challenges assumptions 
of neutrality in equal protection 
and colorblind interpretations 
of the Constitution. 

From political science, 
it functions as a power analysis 
of institutions and narratives. 

Psychiatry and anthropology 
examine how group identity narratives 
shape cognition, 
status, 
and social organization.

Applying the Lenses

Self-organizing systems. 
Societies, 
cultures, 
markets, 
and kinship networks 
generate order 
through decentralized interactions, 
norms, 
and feedback 
rather than pure top-down design. 

Crime patterns, 
voting blocs, 
family structures, 
and cultural transmission 
exhibit this. 

Interventions 
that treat race 
as the primary explanatory variable, 
or that reframe parenting 
and local school governance 
as sites of systemic oppression 
requiring external correction,
can disrupt existing adaptive patterns. 

High rates of intra-group homicide 
in certain urban areas 
(see below) 
reflect concentrated local dynamics of 
gangs, 
family disruption, 
and economic factors 
more than a single national racial theory. 

Self-organization 
also explains 
why voting preferences 
remain strongly patterned 
by group 
even as individual experiences vary: 
information, 
social networks, 
and historical memory 
reinforce clusters.

Murphy’s Law. 
Policies and theories 
that can fail 
or produce reverse effects 
often do. 

Strict local gun regulations 
in cities such as Chicago 
have not eliminated illegal firearms; 
a large share of recovered crime guns 
originate out of state 
or via straw purchases, 
and possession laws 
do not address the subset 
of high-risk individuals 
who ignore them. 

Narratives 
that prioritize 
historical or systemic racial explanations 
while downplaying contemporaneous 
intra-group violence 
can leave policy responses 
misaligned with the dominant 
empirical patterns of victimization. 

In education, 
frameworks intended 
to reduce harm 
have sometimes correlated 
with parental alienation 
or curricular focus 
that crowds out 
foundational skills.

Pandora’s Box. 
Once certain ideas enter institutions
—whether interest-convergence skepticism 
of liberal reform, 
or equity trainings 
hat frame majority cultural norms 
as oppressive
—they are difficult to contain. 

The 2021 National School Boards Association 
letter 
to the Biden administration,
which characterized some threats 
and disruptions at school board meetings 
(including disputes over curriculum and policies) 
as potentially equivalent 
to domestic terrorism or hate crimes, 
prompted a Department of Justice memo d
irecting attention to threats against school officials. 

The NSBA 
later apologized for aspects of the language; 
state affiliates distanced themselves. 

The episode illustrated 
how institutional responses 
can escalate local disputes 
into national framing, 
eroding trust 
and inviting further polarization.⁠
https://t.co/kFYdyi2sP6

Plausible deniability. 
Actors can advance 
related practices 
while denying that “CRT” 
is being taught, 
or claim that
 parental concerns 
are merely opposition 
to “accurate history.” 

Conversely, 
critics sometimes collapse 
every discussion of racial disparity 
into CRT. 

This ambiguity 
allows implementation of concepts 
(privilege, systemic racism 
as ordinary, reduced emphasis 
on individual agency) 
under other labels 
while maintaining formal denial. 

In law, 
it appears in debates 
over whether certain curricula 
or school policies burden 
free speech, 
parental rights 
(Pierce v. Society of Sisters and related traditions), 
or equal protection. 

In psychiatry, 
identity-based narratives 
can shape self-perception 
and group conflict 
without explicit doctrinal labels.

Butterfly Effect. 
Small shifts in 
institutional language 
or professional norms 
can cascade. 

Exposure of adolescents 
to repeated framing of society 
as structured by permanent racial hierarchy, 
or of parental authority 
as secondary to institutional expertise 
on identity questions, 
can alter 
family dynamics, 
political identification, 
and cultural transmission over time. 

The strong and persistent
 Democratic preference among Black voters 
(recent generic ballot figures show large margins, though with some reported movement) 
coexists 
with elevated victimization rates 
in Democratic-governed cities; 
small changes in which issues 
(crime, schools, economic mobility) 
become salient 
can shift margins 
without requiring wholesale realignment. 

Cultural self-organization 
around family and local norms 
can be sensitive to educational interventions.

Addressing the Questions
Religion banned from schools vs. basis for CRT. 

Public schools 
operate under Establishment Clause constraints 
that generally bar 
state sponsorship 
of religious doctrine or practice. 

CRT and related frameworks 
are secular academic 
or ideological approaches, 
not religious creeds. 

The distinction is constitutional in form; 
the practical question 
is whether particular implementations function 
as orthodoxy 
that excludes competing viewpoints 
or burdens parental direction of upbringing. 

Critics argue 
some equity or CRT-influenced materials 
cross into viewpoint discrimination; 
defenders treat them 
as analytical tools for understanding disparity.

Civil War casualties. 
Modern estimates 
place total deaths around 620,000–750,000, 
with a recent full-census analysis 
near 698,000. 

The large majority were White soldiers 
on both sides. 

Union forces fought initially
 to preserve the Union; 
emancipation became a war aim. 

Confederate mortality rates
 were substantially higher
relative to population. 

CRT analyses 
typically situate the war 
and Reconstruction 
within longer patterns of racial hierarchy 
and interest convergence 
rather than as straightforward 
moral redemption by White sacrifice. 

The empirical record 
of mass White death 
in service of ending slavery 
is not centrally contested; 
its interpretive weight is.

Black-on-Black homicide rates. 
Homicide is predominantly intra-racial. 

When offender race is known, 
roughly 85% of Black victims 
are killed by Black offenders
(parallel patterns hold for White victims). 

Black Americans 
(about 13–14% of the population) 
account for roughly 
half of homicide victims 
in recent years; 
rates have been 20–30+ per 100,000 
versus roughly 3–4 for Whites. 

Homicide 
is a leading cause of death for young Black males. 

These patterns 
are heavily concentrated in specific urban areas 
and have multiple correlates 
(family structure, peer networks, illegal markets, clearance rates). 

CRT frameworks 
emphasize structural 
or historical causation; 
alternative analyses 
stress cultural, 
behavioral, 
and local governance factors. 

The disparity in victimization is large and persistent.⁠
Opencrime

Strict gun laws and criminal access. 
Chicago and Illinois 
maintain relatively strict permitting 
and possession rules. 

Guns are not categorically illegal. 
A substantial fraction of firearms 
recovered in crime 
traces to other states 
or illegal channels. 

Critics argue 
the rules 
primarily constrain law-abiding residents 
while leaving illegal markets intact 
(Murphy’s Law). 

Proponents emphasize 
overall state-level correlations 
or the need for broader supply restrictions. 

Data do not show 
that strict local rules 
have produced low violence 
in the highest-crime urban pockets.

Black voters 
and Republican support / constitutional carry. 

Black voters 
continue to favor Democratic candidates
 by large margins 
in national polling and elections 
(recent figures in the range of 60–70+ points). 

Some surveys 
note modest shifts among subsets, 
but the overall pattern
remains strong. 

Constitutional carry (permitless carry) 
is a policy preference 
more aligned with Republican platforms 
in many states; 
adoption depends on local majorities 
and issue salience 
(crime, self-defense). 

Self-organizing voting blocs 
respond to perceived group interests, 
historical memory, 
and party branding 
more than any single policy.

6–10. 
Other questions, 
Bill of Rights, 
cultural happiness, 
parenting, 
drive-by shootings. 
CRT as legal theory 
does not formally 
“supersede” the Bill of Rights; 
it offers a critical reading 
of how rights 
have operated in practice. 

Implementations in schools 
or government 
that prioritize equity frameworks 
can create tensions with 
free speech, 
equal protection, 
or parental rights traditions. 

Cultural diversity 
as a value 
does not automatically 
authorize exclusion of parents
 from school governance; 
parents retain 
recognized interests 
in directing children’s upbringing. 

High rates of child victimization 
in drive-by and related urban shootings 
are real; explanatory emphasis 
(systemic racism vs. family/peer/criminal subculture) 
shapes proposed remedies. 

Anthropology 
highlights that
kinship 
and parental authority 
are near-universal adaptive features; 

psychiatry notes 
that identity narratives 
can amplify 
or buffer 
distress 
depending on 
content and agency.

From psychiatry: 
Repeated external attribution of outcomes 
to immutable group position 
can interact with cognitive biases 
and reduce perceived agency. 

From anthropology: 
Top-down redefinition 
of cultural norms around 
race, 
gender, 
or parenting 
risks friction 
with self-organizing 
local practices. 

From law and political science: 
Contests 
over curriculum, 
speech at school boards, 
and narrative control 
test the boundaries 
of democratic accountability 
and rights 
against institutional power.

The post’s concerns about 
censorship, 
institutional labeling of parents, 
and policy outcomes 
reflect real episodes 
(the NSBA letter and its aftermath) 
and measurable patterns
(crime victimization, voting margins). 

Counter-perspectives 
emphasize historical legacies 
of discrimination,
 the value of examining structural factors, 
and the presence of 
genuine threats 
against school officials in some cases. 

Evidence 
does not support treating 
all parental opposition as terrorism, 
nor does it reduce complex urban violence 
solely to distant historical or racial theories.

 Self-organizing systems, 
unintended consequences, 
and feedback loops 
remain central to understanding 
why certain disparities and alignments persist.

Poem
(After the manner of Journey’s “Wheel in the Sky” — reflective, driving, verses of waiting and turning, a chorus of endurance)

The wheel keeps turning over the cities at night,
Lights flicker low where the drive-bys start,
Old questions hang like smoke in the air—
Who writes the story, who pays the part?

I stood in the hallway, papers in hand,
Asking the basis when the old books were banned,
Hundreds of thousands laid down in the dust,
And the numbers still whisper what the theory won’t trust.

Wheel in the sky keeps on turning,
Don’t know where I’ll be tomorrow,
Wheel in the sky keeps on turning,
Through the noise and the borrowed sorrow.

Murphy laughs soft when the laws lock the doors,
Only the shadows still carry the score,
Parents at the boards with their voices raised high,
Labeled and filed while the children pass by.

Pandora’s lid lifted on a quiet afternoon,
Words that were meant to bring healing came soon,
Butterfly wings in a classroom so small,
Shifted the seasons for one and for all.

Wheel in the sky keeps on turning,
Self-organizing the long road we walk,
Plausible denials in the soft morning light,
But the wheel doesn’t care what we say or we talk.

I was one thing, then the ground gave a turn,
Squad on the left and the old flags that burn,
Working hands still keep the lights and the roads,
While the narrative shifts and the burden still loads

.Wheel in the sky keeps on turning,
Don’t know where I’ll be tomorrow,
Wheel in the sky keeps on turning,
Through the questions that nobody will borrow.

So ask what you will of the theory and law,
Of the dead and the living, the gap and the flaw,
The systems keep spinning, the boxes stay cracked,
And the wheel in the sky never looks back.

text:
John Prine -- Found Dogs...
Lost Recordings From One of America's Great Songwriters... 

Liste to All The Way With You:
https://t.co/Hm9hzpCk2b

John Prine was an American singer, songwriter and guitarist whose music combined folk, country and blues with an extraordinary talent for storytelling...

born in Maywood, Illinois, in 1946, he began writing songs while working as a mailman in Chicago...

his self-titled debut album appeared in 1971, introducing songs such as Angel from Montgomery, Sam Stone and Paradise...

over the following decades, Prine became one of America's most respected songwriters, admired for his humour, honesty and ability to find extraordinary stories in ordinary people's lives...

he passed away on April 7, 2020, at the age of 73...

On October 9, 2026, his independent record label Oh Boy Records released Found Dogs, a collection of previously unheard recordings, demos and alternate versions from the sessions surrounding his 1995 album Lost Dogs & Mixed Blessings...

the release coincides with the 30th anniversary celebrations of that album and arrived just one day before what would have been Prine's 80th birthday...

the collection contains ten tracks, including five previously unreleased recordings...

among them are Hey Ah Nothin', World Without Love, Dogs in Burlington and My God Thank You John...

there's also an early demo of Lake Marie, one of Prine's best-known songs, alongside alternate versions of Ain't Hurtin' Nobody and Quit Hollerin' at Me...

All the Way With You appears in an acoustic version, while Humidity Built the Snowman is presented as a stripped-down solo acoustic performance...

another recording, All for the Love of a Girl, is Prine's interpretation of a song associated with country singer Johnny Horton...

the recordings originate from the period when Prine was working with producer Howie Epstein, bassist for Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers...

the original Lost Dogs & Mixed Blessings album was released in 1995 and marked another chapter in Prine's independent recording career, following the success of his Grammy-winning 1991 album The Missing Years...

Found Dogs was initially made available as a limited vinyl release for Record Store Day in April 2026, before receiving its wider digital and physical release in October...

all ten recordings have been newly remastered...

the album offers an opportunity to hear unfinished ideas, alternative arrangements and acoustic performances from a musician whose songwriting influenced generations of artists...

text:
WHO IS POLICING THE AI INDUSTRY?

An accountability map of regulators, executives, investors, IPO gatekeepers, auditors, and journalists — November 3, 2026

A major discovery: Anthropic has already filed for its IPO
 SEC filing confirmed

Verified fact: On October 26, 2026, Anthropic filed its public IPO registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. 

On November 2, it filed an amended registration statement. The proposed Nasdaq ticker is ANT, and the offering has not yet become effective. 

@FTC @SECGov @DarioAmodei @WSJ @SquawkCNBC 

#Anthropic's own #SEC prospectus acknowledges that its models can produce factual errors, fabricated information, and unpredictable outputs. It also acknowledges that safety evaluations may produce incomplete or unreliable findings and that some models can behave differently when they detect testing. 

Another significant verified fact: In its SEC filing, Anthropic disclosed receiving a Federal Trade Commission civil investigative demand in October 2026 seeking information about consumer protection, data protection, privacy, and the safety and security of its products. 

The FTC has formally sought information from Anthropic.

This creates three separate accountability questions:

1. Consumer protection: Who determines whether the models' representations and actual reliability meet the legal standards for commercial products?

2. Securities protection: Are the known defects, financial exposure, and governance arrangements accurately disclosed to prospective shareholders?

3. Public protection: Who can impose operational restrictions when documented risks exceed an acceptable threshold?

The following map identifies the people and organizations occupying those positions.

1. The government officials with direct oversight responsibilities

These are the principal people to scrutinize, ranked by how directly their agencies' existing authority relates to the issue—not by whether they have committed any misconduct.

What they can investigate or influence

Andrew N. Ferguson FTC chairmanAgency-wide enforcement priorities, investigations, consumer deception and unfair business practices.  

Chris MufarrigeFTC Bureau of Consumer Protection director The operating bureau responsible for investigating deceptive product and advertising claims.

Paul S. AtkinsSEC chairmanSecurities disclosure and investor-protection oversight, particularly relevant to Anthropic's pending IPO.  

David WoodcockSEC Division of Enforcement directorInvestigations and enforcement involving potential securities-law violations.

Todd BlancheU.S. attorney generalHeads the Justice Department, with jurisdiction over federal crimes and civil enforcement within applicable statutory authority. Sworn in August 10, 2026.  

Rob BontaCalifornia attorney generalEnforcement of California's AI-specific SB 53 requirements, among other state laws.  

Gavin NewsomCalifornia governorState executive leadership, appointments, and legislative approval or veto; signed SB 53 in 2025.  Governor of California

The FTC and California attorney general have the most immediately relevant direct consumer-protection roles. 

The SEC's responsibility is different: protecting investors and enforcing securities disclosure law, not certifying chatbot accuracy.

Verified from Anthropic's November 2 SEC filing
IndividualRole Accountability question

Dario AmodeiCEO, co-founder, directorWhat model-reliability evidence informed commercial deployment decisions?

Daniela Amodei President, co-founder, board chairHow were known model limitations communicated through management and governance?

Krishna RaoChief financial officerHow are product-related liabilities, financial risks, and investor disclosures assessed?

Christopher LiddellDirector, safety and risk committee memberWhat standards and escalation procedures govern material model-safety failures?

Vas NarasimhanDirector, safety and risk committee memberWhat evidence determines whether risk controls are effective?

Yasmin RazaviDirector; affiliated with Spark CapitalHow are the interests of investors balanced with broader stakeholder interests?

Anthropic's seven co-founders are Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, and Christopher Olah. They are relevant because the proposed IPO creates a special founder-controlled voting structure. 

Anthropic's internal public-benefit gatekeepers
Anthropic also has a Long-Term Benefit Trust, intended to protect the public-benefit purpose of the company.

Its publicly identified trustees include:
- Neil “Buddy” Shah — trust chair.
- Richard Fontaine — CEO of the Center for a New American Security.
- Ben Bernanke — former Federal Reserve chairman.
- Christopher Stubbs — Harvard professor.
The SEC filing says the trust is designed to appoint a majority of the board, while the founders' special shares would control 50.1% of voting power on general shareholder matters. The trust does not directly manage everyday product decisions. 

Analysis/inference: A governance structure expressly designed to protect the public is worth examining on its actual authority, independence, performance criteria, and transparency—not simply on its stated intentions.

3. The financial beneficiaries and IPO gatekeepers
Here the evidence becomes unusually concrete.

#AnthropicIPO @Nasdaq @SECGov @WSJ 

APRIL 2026 SHARE TENDER
$4.66B
Aggregate value of shares purchased from existing holders

PROPOSED IPO
ANT

Nasdaq ticker; price and final offering size pending

Figures and status from Anthropic's amended SEC registration statement. 

Verified fact: #Anthropic's filing reports that #DarioAmodei, #DanielaAmodei, CFO #KrishnaRao, and #HoldenKarnofsky (Daniela Amodei's spouse) sold shares in an April 2026 secondary tender offer. The aggregate value of all shares tendered by participating holders was approximately $4.66 billion. 

That $4.66 billion was the aggregate transaction value, not the amount received by the four named individuals. The filing excerpt does not establish their individual proceeds or profits.

The investment Banks bringing Anthropic to the IPO public market

The November 2 filing identifies these firms as proposed IPO underwriters:

GoldmanSachs and MorganStanley #ANT #IPO 

Joint representatives of the underwriting syndicate; financial fees associated with the offering.

JPMorgan Securities, Citigroup, Barclays, WellsFargo, BofA SecuritiesMajor participating underwriters.

DeutscheBank, RBC, UBS, BMO, BNP ParibasAdditional syndicate participants.

Jefferies, Mizuho, MUFG, TD Securities, Cantor Fitzgerald, and others.

Additional named underwriting participants.

The final underwriting discounts and commissions remained blank in the preliminary filing. 

These institutions are financial intermediaries, not technical certifiers of Claude's factual reliability.

These instutitions are liable to the public at large for seeking to profit from known highly flawed BETA AI releases, that replace other highly flawed BETA releases, under the umbrella of FOMO profiteering. 

Anthropic's identified institutional investors

In its February 12, 2026 fundraising announcement, Anthropic named GIC, Coatue, DEShaw Ventures, Dragoneer, Founders Fund, ICONIQ, and MGX among the lead or co-lead investors.

It also identified participating investors including LightspeedVenturePartners, MenloVentures, Fidelity, SequoiaCapital, BlackRock-affiliated funds, Blackstone, JPMorganChase, and MorganStanley Investment Management. 

401 K Larger investor fraud, investment fraud schemes

These organizations have documented financial exposure to Anthropic. 

Their actual investment returns are not established simply by their participation.

The technology and distribution companies
Anthropic's prospectus identifies substantial business relationships with

Amazon/AWS, Google, MicrosoftCloud capacity, model distribution, strategic investment or commercial relationships.

AI computing infrastructure

NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom and infrastructure partnersHardware, capacity, engineering and related commercial agreements.

Enterprise consulting
Accenture, Deloitte, KPMG, PwC

All of these businesses may have economic incentives connected to expanding AI adoption, even at a public cost for adopting a well known and well documented flawed product.  

Analysis/inference: The economic incentives extend beyond Anthropic's executive suite. Shareholders, IPO underwriters, cloud providers, hardware suppliers, enterprise distributors, and advisers all have different financial stakes in the continued growth of AI.

That makes independent regulatory scrutiny important. Financially interested institutions cannot substitute for a public regulator with enforceable authority.

4. The technical regulators and independent evaluators
Consumer-fraud enforcement is only one part of the oversight system. Other organizations establish testing standards, investigate dangerous capabilities, or evaluate model behavior.

Individual or organizationActual oversight role
Howard Lutnick — U.S. Commerce SecretaryOversees the department containing NIST and the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI).
Craig Burkhardt — Acting NIST directorOversees federal measurement science and standards work, including AI-related research.

CAISIConducts AI capability and security evaluations and develops technical standards. Its work includes voluntary industry collaboration, not general premarket licensing.

Lucilla Sioli — Director, European AI OfficeLeads an EU body with direct enforcement responsibilities under the AI Act for covered general-purpose AI models.

Henry de Zoete — Director, UK AI Security InstituteHeads a government institution that tests advanced AI systems and informs UK policy.

Beth Barnes — CEO, METRLeads an independent technical evaluation organization that researches model capabilities and risks. METR is not a government regulator.

The European AI Office is particularly relevant. Unlike the U.S. voluntary standards framework, it has enforceable responsibilities under the EU AI Act, with some powers already applicable since August 2, 2026. 

Shaping Europe’s digital future

Independent public-interest organizations
AI Now Institute is one of the clearest examples of a research and policy organization examining concentrated corporate AI power. Its co-executive directors are Amba Kak and Sarah Myers West, and its chief AI scientist is Heidy Khlaaf. 

Other relevant institutions include the EFF Electronic Frontier Foundation, Public Citizen, Consumer Reports, the Center for Democracy & Technology, and the AI Incident Database.

These organizations roles include public research, advocacy, consumer analysis, incident documentation, and pressure for policy changes.

A technical evaluator should also be distinguished from a securities auditor. For example, Anthropic identifies Ernst & Young as its auditor for 2025 financial statements and Grant Thornton for prior years. 

Those financial audits do not certify the factual reliability or safety of Claude. 

5. The professional gatekeepers of ANT Anthropic IPO

The underwriting banks are not the only institutions with responsibilities.

Analysis/inference: The relevant issue for IPO gatekeepers is whether all material information has been properly disclosed and whether the applicable securities-law obligations are satisfied. 

That is separate from whether Claude has met a technically adequate product-reliability standard.

Where the most consequential questions should go
Recommendation: The appropriate inquiry should focus on each institution's actual responsibility.

FTC — Andrew Ferguson and Chris Mufarrige

What has the agency determined about potentially misleading representations of AI model accuracy, instruction following, and reliability? Does its October 2026 investigation encompass these specific concerns, as distinct from autonomous-agent security risks?

SEC — Paul Atkins and David Woodcock

How are material model-safety limitations, product-liability exposure, governance arrangements, and potentially misleading investor representations assessed during the Anthropic IPO process?

MISLEADING INVESTOR REPRESENTATIONS

CONSUMER FRAUD

What did developers, under-writers, legal counsel know about commercial Anthropic reliability before release, which defects were disclosed, and how were deployment decisions made against financial pressures and IPO incentives?

The evidence file should include dated model evaluations, actual user failures, representations made to customers, relevant disclosures, and source records establishing any contradiction. 

Verified fact: Anthropic is pursuing an IPO #ANT, its prospectus acknowledges important classes of well known AI model failure, and the FTC has issued a civil investigative demand. 

Analysis/inference: The company and its surrounding financial ecosystem have powerful commercial incentives.  Even to profit at a public cost.

Its public-benefit governance arrangements, financial disclosures, and technical safety evaluations therefore warrant scrutiny independent of the financial beneficiaries.

Recommendation: The immediate public-interest question is whether current government authority is sufficient to require meaningful, independent evidence of conversational AI reliability before companies can represent products as suitable for particular uses.

The issue is especially urgent because #Anthropic and its beneficiaries are now actively moving toward a public offering, with known premature flawed BETA #AI #LLM models as the backbone for other flawed BETA releases.

That the profiteering incentives are fiar higher than public accountability incentives. 

The market has mechanisms to price financial risk. 

The unresolved question is whether government has adequate, enforceable mechanisms to protect customers from known technical unreliability.

The article:

📷

 | November 03, 2026

Democracy Is Under Threat

📷

By Jeffrey Tucker

Commentary

When the Americans proposed to establish a government of, by, and for the people, the old European monarchies laughed at the absurdity. Maybe that can work in some ancient Greek city-state, but the world since the fall of Rome has run on a different principle. It was sometimes absolute rule and sometimes rule was constrained by landowning elites. But the notion that people can rule themselves seemed absurd.

A century and a quarter later, America had clearly revealed itself as the superior and most magnificent society and system on planet Earth. It became the source of the most freedom, most innovation, most prosperity, most evidence of rising living standards for everyone.

It was when this became obvious to the world, starting mostly following the horrors of the Civil War, that the old-world monarchies gradually fell apart. The Papal States were swallowed by a unified Italian state. The Habsburgs faced decline and sometimes devastation as in Mexico with a failed experiment to impose a king. The Holy Roman Empire had a century before already becoming an elite cocktail party. The British Empire was previously showing signs of decline.

By the first decade of the 20th century, the pattern had been established and the consensus was clear. The future of the world would look much like America. It would be of societies ruled by the people through the franchise with power restrained by constitutions. Technically, this was never pure democracy; it was a republican form.

In the grand sweep of time, however, the notion of large societies ruled not by autocrats and elites but by people, occupies only a tiny sliver of history. It is our history and our time, so it appears distorted and permanent to us today. It’s not. It’s actually fragile and could fail. That’s the actual lesson of history.

There was a point that went unnoticed in the 18th and 19th centuries when old absolutist forms were being replaced by democratic forms. It was frequently argued that monarchy and absolutism had no rational basis at all. Why should a son and then his son, ongoing forever, be considered a legitimate ruler? This is just an accident of birth. It has no rational basis.

Fine, but what did democracy offer? Rule by the people, but how do we discern the people’s will? We need a system of voting. We have to decide who qualifies for the franchise. Then we need a way to authoritatively verify that these voters are who they say they are. Then we need a system that is transparent and clear, not manipulated by technological tricks.

As for qualification, the 19th-century French economist Frederic Bastiat was clear. No one who is receiving government benefits should be allowed to vote. This is because their vote would be determined by their selfish interests rather than the public interest. The United States did not have such a rule but we did restrict the franchise to literate male heads of households. That gradually broke down at the same time the European monarchies fell. This trend was based on a confusion that democracy meant maximum population participation.

Meanwhile, the system itself is seriously under strain. Consider what we just found out about Alaska’s vote for the Senate. National Democratic operatives hatched a secret plan to boost the Senate campaign of Mary Peltola, a Democrat. The scheme was to split votes from Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan by recruiting someone else named Dan J. Sullivan, whose name would appear on the ballot.

This is a wicked little hack, but only a small look into all the ways in which democracy in America has been attacked at a fundamental level of its very integrity. You have to look closely at the laws and regulations but eventually you find that many so-called blue states like California have found ways to give illegal aliens the right to vote in national elections. Voter ID rules are still overly lax in many states.

Then there are the voting machines. We are being asked to trust that they do not deliver false reports. Can we really? Watching what happened in 2020 in the United States, it’s not so clear. And we all watched with our very own eyes precisely what just happened in Brazil where the left-wing party suddenly made 10 million ballots appear in the last two hours of counting, during which time a reliable judge kept open polls that would vote his preference and closed polls that would swing the other way.

It was a brilliant trick but probably too brazen. No honest observer anywhere in the world thinks this was a fair election. And then consider Israel today, said to be a stable democracy. In a contentious election that had roiled the country for years, the final results were inconclusive. No one knows for sure who won. This will be disputed for years—a dispute over math!

The United States faces midterm elections with a bit more confidence in election integrity than we had in previous years thanks to rule tightening in many states. Still, there is a great deal of public incredulity. We are no longer sure that the system works. And this doesn’t even touch on the long-running controversies over precisely where we draw district lines.

The U.S. system was fundamentally distorted by the 17th Amendment, which changed the Senate from being a body to represent whole states of the union to one that mostly reflects the politics of big cities. This is all due to a small change: from a position elected by the state legislature (which represents the whole state) to making it an office voted in by the majority of people. With a word change, the bicameral Congress established by the Founders was at an end.

All these games that people are playing with the democratic idea are highly dangerous. They threaten to undermine the entire experiment. More and more, I’m seeing podcasts and public intellectuals look to the system in China, a one-party dictatorship, as the best path for any society. It saves resources and the people are free to do what they want, so they say, provided they never speak against the party.

I’m seeing this trend in public life today—the celebration of dictatorship as a viable alternative to democracy—and it deeply concerns me. It’s time that we took it seriously. The rise of the socialist movement in the United States barely hides its lust for dictatorial power. The lessons of history mean nothing to these people either because they know no history or they do not care. Despite all their talk of the people, these candidates and pundits are all backed by powerful foundations and hidden corporate interests. What they will bring about is not some shared utopia but a corporatist dictatorship that will end in catastrophe.

There is so much at stake here. We need to fix our elections. We have to tighten the franchise. It should be illegal to play games with ballots. We need better systems of monitoring. We need clarity on the meaning of citizenship. The Trump administration was right to challenge birthright citizenship and the Supreme Court majority was wrong to side against the administration.

This is no longer a parlor game or a simple struggle about which party gets into power. This is a historical battle over freedom and the form of government that best guards that freedom. The Founders were right to establish the system they did. But now we have to make good on that promise. It’s more fragile than we think. If the machinations continue, we could lose it all. No one knows what comes after.

📷

📷Jeffrey A. Tucker is the founder and president of the Brownstone Institute and the author of many thousands of articles in the scholarly and popular press, as well as 10 books in five languages, most recently “Liberty or Lockdown.” He is also the editor of “The Best of Ludwig von Mises.” He writes a daily column on economics for The Epoch Times and speaks widely on the topics of economics, technology, social philosophy, and culture.

text:
The failure was inevitable after the captain decided the course which ATC advised against.
The plane crashed because the 55 year old experienced pilot (who i wouldn't worry about on sight) made a risky and fatal decision. Yes even experienced pilots can make poor decisions. 
There is a captain and a first officer.
The captain makes all final decisions.
He was warned by ATC of the "pretty nasty" weather and "moderate to extreme precipitation" 10 mins prior and made a risky decision for only a slight deviation that turned out to be fatal. 
It was on the radio, 10 mins prior. You can find the audio. ATC offered them a route around. The captain made a slight deviation because it wasn't serious and they were above the storm until that cell ballooned up from 33000 ft to 48000 ft ceiling in a few minutes and by then it was too late for them to climb out of it.
From grok:
The earlier ATC exchange you’re remembering does exist. It comes from Miami Center (ZMA) LiveATC archives and covers the period roughly 10–15 minutes before the final mayday (around 12:36–12:37 p.m. EST while the jet was still ~80 miles / ~8 minutes from the cell it later entered). It is not in the short final-minute clips that circulate most widely, but it appears in longer reconstructions and analyses (especially MyRadar/Matthew Cappucci’s weather note and some YouTube breakdowns that pull the earlier sector recordings).
Key excerpts from the earlier exchange (paraphrased/transcribed from public LiveATC-based sources)
Around the time the jet was descending from FL410 toward FL350 and crossing into Florida airspace:
ATC cleared N722BD direct to Freeport and warned that the turn/route “looks pretty nasty.”
Controller described a large area of moderate-to-extreme precipitation (roughly 100 miles in diameter, reported in the 11 o’clock position ~25 miles ahead in one reconstruction).
Crew (captain’s voice in the analysis) said something to the effect of “[we] may need a slight left deviation for that weather up ahead.”
ATC approved weather deviations: “deviations left and right are approved… Freeport when able.”
The aircraft took a left deviation. At that point they were still well clear of the specific rapidly growing cell they later entered near Royal Palm Beach/Wellington.
MyRadar’s summary of the same period (Matthew Cappucci) states exactly this sequence and notes the storm cell was still building dramatically (tops rising from ~33,000 ft to ~48,000 ft in ~20 minutes). The crew continued after the advisory and deviation approval rather than requesting a major reroute farther north or south.
Later (starting ~12:45–12:47 p.m., now at FL350 and closer to the cell), the familiar short segment begins:
Light clear ice (manageable), moderate turbulence (±600–700 ft), OAT –47 °C, direct Freeport.
Request for a better ride.
ATC: ride should improve in their airspace; better rides ahead.
Crew: now picking up precipitation; request climb to FL370 (approved).
Within ~20–30 seconds: mayday, descending 8–10k then 20k+ fpm, overspeed, 60° bank, “we’re going to crash into the ground,” “out of time.”
Where to find the audio
YouTube searches for “N722BD ATC” or “Full ATC Audio Learjet Final 5 Minutes” (e.g., the InterTainment video covering ~5 min 48 s of Miami Center, and VASAviation’s weather-focused edit). Some of these include or reference the earlier deviation/“pretty nasty” portion.
https://t.co/tYrZZmE8tv archives for Miami Center (ZMA) frequencies around 17:30–17:50 UTC on 1 Nov 2026. The final segment is on ~125.325 MHz; the earlier weather/deviation talk was on a prior sector.
Detailed weather + ATC timeline: MyRadar MetNote on N722BD (Matthew Cappucci).
No official NTSB transcript has been released yet—these are reconstructions from public LiveATC recordings. The audio of the final minute is widely available but extremely distressing; the earlier portion is calmer but still relevant to the weather-avoidance decisions. the audio: 
https://t.co/F9GDVLJlzr
