text:
Advisor to Prime Minister, Official Spokesperson for Ministry of Foreign Affairs @majedalansari : Qatar Continues Its Efforts to Bridge Gap between Washington, Tehran

Doha | November 3, 2026

Advisor to the Prime Minister and Official Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Dr. Majed bin Mohammed Al Ansari confirmed Tuesday that the State of Qatar continues its efforts to bridge the gap between the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran by facilitating the exchange of proposals.

He noted that both sides have demonstrated a commitment to the negotiation process and to reviewing the proposals put forward, despite the escalation currently unfolding in the region.

During the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' weekly media briefing, Al Ansari said that the Qatari delegation that traveled to Tehran on Monday arrived as planned and held an extensive meeting with their counterparts there, which lasted for about three hours. During the meeting, they exchanged views on various proposals currently under consideration to bridge the gap between the two sides, before the delegation departed and returned to Doha Monday evening.

He added that communications between the parties are ongoing, and mediators continue to exchange proposals in real time, while both sides are currently reviewing the ideas and suggestions presented by the mediators within various contexts.

He pointed out that the continuation of negotiations, the parties' commitment to engaging in them, and their examination of the proposals on the table offer a "glimmer of hope" for reaching an agreement. In this regard, he said that a mediator cannot lose hope; there are developments in the communication between the parties, though it is not possible at this moment to speak of any specific breakthrough.

The Advisor to the Prime Minister and Official Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs indicated that these efforts are being carried out in full coordination with regional partners, particularly the GCC member states, reflecting a strong consensus among these nations on the need to spare the region from escalation and to work toward de-escalation, thereby preventing its peoples from being subjected to any future tensions.

He reaffirmed that the Qatari-Pakistani mediation remains a priority for the State of Qatar, stressing that any escalation in the coming period would not be in the interest of any party.

He highlighted the ongoing communication and coordination between Qatari officials and their counterparts in the region, as well as with partners across the globe, aimed at achieving a de-escalation and resolving this crisis through diplomatic means.

Regarding the targeting of the Qatari gas carrier "Al Mayeda," Al Ansari affirmed that the State of Qatar has condemned this act. He emphasized that freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and the Arabian Gulf is non-negotiable, noting that Qatar rejects any threat to such freedom, whether directed at a Qatari vessel or any other ship in the waters of the Gulf.

He said that any escalation in the region, whether through military attacks or the targeting of vessels in the waters of the Gulf, poses a threat to the entire region and its peoples, and impacts negotiations. He further emphasized that efforts are currently underway to halt this escalation and reach a diplomatic agreement to end the crisis.

Regarding regional coordination, the Advisor to the Prime Minister and Official Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs emphasized that there is a "very high level" of regional coordination with various countries in the region, noting that these efforts are entirely aimed at supporting mediation initiatives and resolving the crisis through diplomatic means.

He said that there is ongoing, daily coordination among Their Highnesses and Excellencies leaders of the countries in the region, with each state playing its part in coordination with the others as part of a joint regional effort to spare the region the ravages of escalation. He further expressed the State of Qatar's welcome for all steps taken by fraternal nations in the region, noting that coordination continues at the highest levels to ensure an end to the escalation and the establishment of a new regional security framework that guarantees security and stability for the peoples of the region.

Regarding the situation in Yemen, Al Ansari reiterated the State of Qatar's support for the legitimate Yemeni government and the Yemeni people in realizing their aspirations and overcoming the crisis. He noted that Qatar has clearly condemned the attacks carried out by the Houthi group against the sisterly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and affirmed its continued support for the Kingdom, as well as its commitment to the implementation of agreements reached under the GCC umbrella.

On the visit of HH the Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani to the Russian Federation, and Moscow's role in the current regional crisis, Al Ansari said that Qatari-Russian relations encompass numerous areas of joint cooperation, particularly in the energy sector. The participation of HH the Amir in the 8th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) underscores the State of Qatar's commitment to this role and to coordination within this vital market, with a view toward global energy security.

He added that the Russian Federation is a state with significant influence on the international stage and a permanent member of the UN Security Council. He noted that the discussions between HH the Amir and HE the President of the Russian Federation addressed the crisis in the region, as well as the role that Russia could play, in coordination with other international partners and fellow permanent members of the Security Council, toward resolving this crisis.

Regarding the meeting between HH the Amir and the Iranian President, the Advisor to the Prime Minister and Official Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs indicated that the meeting is part of ongoing bilateral engagements with officials from the Islamic Republic of Iran. He emphasized that the State of Qatar consistently believes in communication and dialogue, and values Iran's positive engagement in the negotiations and mediation efforts led by Qatar.

He noted that Qatari officials at the highest levels continue to engage with their Iranian counterparts, with the aim of reaching a solution that enhances regional security and leads to a regional security framework that ensures security, stability, and prosperity for the peoples of the region.

In a separate context, Al Ansari condemned Israeli allegations regarding the State of Qatar's interference in the Israeli elections and its influence on their outcome, pointing to a statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs last week in which it expressed its strong denunciation of these claims.

He described these allegations as "absurd and baseless," asserting that the State of Qatar categorically rejects them and will not accept being used as a "scapegoat" within the context of the internal political polarization currently unfolding in Israel, or in any other country.

The Advisor to the Prime Minister and Official Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs urged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to address his internal challenges rather than attempting to export his political crises abroad. He emphasized that such campaigns would not deter the State of Qatar from continuing its mediation role regarding Gaza or Iran, nor would they prevent it from fulfilling its role as a "mediator for peace" on the global stage.

#MOFAQatar

text:
October 7, 1950. Somewhere in Korea, a Catholic priest set up his altar on the hood of a jeep and said Mass for the men of the 1st Cavalry Division.

Chaplain Emil Kapaun of the 8th Cavalry Regiment would be a prisoner less than a month later.

He was a Kansas farm boy, born in 1916, ordained in 1940, and he had already served as an Army chaplain in Burma and India during World War II. In Korea he often rode a bicycle from position to position along the line to reach his soldiers. In August 1950 he earned the Bronze Star near Kumchon for pulling a wounded soldier out under heavy fire.

At Unsan, on November 1 and 2, the Chinese encircled the 3rd Battalion. Kapaun was captured once and got free when allied soldiers shot his captors. Then he volunteered to remain with the wounded and was captured again.

In the camps at Sambukol and Pyoktong he kept ministering. When the guards ran a mandatory reeducation program, he politely rejected every theory the instructors offered. Once he was punished by being made to sit outside in subzero weather without clothes.

Army Chief of Staff Gen. Raymond Odierno said that near the end Kapaun gave last rites to a dying prisoner and wrote the Our Father and Hail Mary on a scrap of paper for another man.

He died at Pyoktong on May 23, 1951. In 1993 the Catholic Church named him a Servant of God, the second of four steps toward sainthood.

What would you have said to him at that jeep?

Who is Zelensky? 

For 7 years, Volodymyr Zelensky has been the wests darling, a khaki clad symbol of defiance, pleading for billions in aid and NATO’s embrace amid Ukraine’s self inflicted war. 

To many well meaning, but willfully ignorant  Americans and Europeans , he’s a hero battling overwhelming odds. But behind the curated image lies a far uglier truth, a stooge comedian turned president, propped up by a criminal oligarch, surrounded by cronies, and presiding over a regime of corruption, repression, and broken promises.

An actor playing a role he’s woefully unfit for.  

As Ukraine spirals deeper into chaos and its brutally harvested conscript army dwindles, it's important that decent Americans and Europeans understand who and what this man really represents.

Let's start with Kvartal 95, The Oligarch’s Launchpad, Zelensky’s story starts not in politics but comedy. Born in 1978 in Kryvyi Rih, he co-founded Studio Kvartal 95 in the 1990s with a group of friends that had hit it big by the 2000s, ironically their big breaks were made in Russia, performing in Russian and focusing on Russian and Ukrainian political and cultural life. The key to all this success? Ihor Kolomoisky, a billionaire ukrainian oligarch with a laundry list of crimes, including fraud, money laundering, and brutal violence. Kolomoisky then owned 1+1, the TV network that handed Zelenskys Kvartal 95 a national platform starting in 2012. He didn’t just offer airtime. He bankrolled Zelensky with cash, security, and legal and criminal muscle. This wasn’t mentorship. It was a transaction. Kolomoisky, later sanctioned by the U.S. for “significant corruption,” saw Zelensky as a pawn in his game. By 2019, when Zelensky ran for president, Kolomoisky’s DNA was all over the campaign providing vehicles, lawyers, bodyguards, and a media blitz. Zelensky was never an outsider; he was a "made man"

This is where it gets almost unbelievably bizzare. In 2015, Zelensky starred in "Servant of the People," a hit satire aired on  Kolomoisky’s 1+1 channel, where he played a teacher turned president railing against corruption. 

Ukrainians, tired of the endemic corruption in the post Soviet state, lapped it up. Then, in 2018, his Kvartal 95 crew decided to turn fiction into reality, registering a political party called, you guessed it,  "Servant of the People." It had absolutely no manifesto, no policies, and no plan of action, just a TV title and Zelensky’s face. 

Running in 2019, Zelensky promised to end corruption and the Donbas civil war, which had erupted after the CIA backed Maidan Coup, winning in a landslide thanks to Kolomoisky’s media machine. An actor who played a president on TV was now remarkably in the real job.

Zelensky didn’t waste any time handing power to his showbiz pals. Ivan Bakanov, a Kvartal 95 co-founder, became head of the SBU security service with no experience. Serhiy Shefir, another comedy crony, took a top aide role, no experience. And then there’s Andriy Yermak, a now disgraced former film producer turned Zelensky’s right-hand man, who headed the Presidential Office, dubbed Ukraine’s “shadow president.” Yermak, physically and intellectualy towered over Zelensky, controled policy and access, a fixer running the show while the president flounders. 

These weren’t appointments based on merit. They were placements, a Kvartal 95 clique utterly unfit for a grossly dysfunctional war-torn nation.

Zelensky’s laughable anti-corruption pledge met reality in 2021 with the Pandora Papers. The leak revealed he and his inner circle,including Bakanov, were funnelling cash to Kolomoisky with Zelensky stashing millions offshore. 

Zelensky swore to end corruption and the Donbas war. Instead, he’s delivered more of both, a million plus lie Dead, the free Media crushed, billions stolen, languages and religion banned. This criminal is no hero. No Churchill. And no friend of Europecor America. He should be treated accordingly.

text:
Yes. Peter Thiel is the central figure—often called the “don”—of the PayPal Mafia.⁠Wikipedia

The PayPal Mafia is the informal name for the group of PayPal founders and early employees who, after eBay’s 2002 acquisition of the company, founded, funded, or helped scale many major tech companies (LinkedIn, YouTube, Yelp, Palantir, SpaceX, Affirm, and others). The label stuck after a 2007 Fortune magazine article and a staged photo of members in mafia-style attire at a San Francisco bar.⁠Wikipedia

Key members (commonly listed)
Here are the best-known ones, drawn from Wikipedia and contemporary reporting (lists vary slightly and have expanded over time; not every early employee is always included):

Peter Thiel — Co-founder and former CEO of Confinity/PayPal. Later co-founded Palantir (data analytics widely used by government and intelligence clients), founded Founders Fund (venture firm), and was the first major outside investor in Facebook. Also involved with Clarium Capital and other funds.
Elon Musk — Founded https://t.co/SlJQFQgwEP, which merged with Thiel’s Confinity to form PayPal. Later founded SpaceX (including Starlink), Neuralink, The Boring Company; took control of Tesla; acquired Twitter (now X). He also founded xAI, the company behind Grok.
Max Levchin — Co-founder and CTO. Later founded Affirm (buy-now-pay-later) and Slide; sometimes called the “consigliere.”
Reid Hoffman — Early executive. Founded LinkedIn; early investor in Facebook and other companies; more Democratic-leaning politically than some of the others.
David Sacks — Former COO. Founded Yammer (acquired by Microsoft) and https://t.co/cddPyVi0zb. Later served as a Trump administration advisor on AI and crypto.
Luke Nosek — Co-founder. Partner at Founders Fund.
Ken Howery — Early CFO. Partner at Founders Fund; served as U.S. ambassador (Sweden, then Denmark).
Roelof Botha — CFO. Later partner at Sequoia Capital.
Keith Rabois — Executive. Later at LinkedIn, Square, and various VC firms.
YouTube founders — Steve Chen, Chad Hurley, and Jawed Karim (PayPal engineers/designers).
Yelp co-founders — Jeremy Stoppelman and Russel Simmons.
Others sometimes included: Premal Shah (Kiva), Nathan Gettings (Palantir/Affirm), Jack Selby, Scott Banister, and more. Joe Lonsdale (Palantir co-founder, 8VC) is sometimes noted as a junior associate/intern-era figure.
The group is credited with seeding a large portion of modern Silicon Valley consumer internet, fintech, and later hard-tech/defense companies through mutual investment, board seats, and advice. Founders Fund (Thiel and others) was an early institutional investor in SpaceX.

Thiel, Vance, and government-related companies
Thiel has been a significant backer of J.D. Vance: he mentored him, helped fund his venture efforts, gave roughly $15 million to support Vance’s 2022 Senate campaign (via a super PAC), and helped facilitate introductions that aided Vance’s rise, including with Trump. Vance later became Trump’s vice president.⁠Forbes

On the “spy accessory / data” side: Thiel co-founded and chairs Palantir, whose software is used by U.S. intelligence, military, and other government clients for data analysis and integration. He is a major investor (via Founders Fund) in Anduril, a defense technology company focused on autonomous systems, drones, surveillance towers, and related military hardware/software. Founders Fund has also been a major early investor in SpaceX/Starlink. These companies have secured substantial government contracts; critics on both the left (surveillance/power concentration concerns) and parts of the right (unelected influence, certain foreign-policy or cultural positions) have expressed resentment or skepticism toward the concentration of power and political activity.⁠Strobofactory

Starlink is part of SpaceX (Musk). Grok is developed by xAI (Musk). Thiel is not a direct founder or controller of those, but the overlapping network (PayPal alumni, Founders Fund investments, personal and political ties) is real and frequently noted.

In short: Thiel is the central “don” of the PayPal Mafia, which includes Musk (SpaceX/Starlink/xAI/Grok) and others who built or backed many of the companies you mentioned. The political and institutional influence is well-documented; so is the resulting criticism from multiple directions.The PayPal Mafia is not uniformly left or right. Public political activity splits clearly among the best-known members.

Right-leaning / conservative / libertarian / Trump-aligned
These are the most publicly active on the right:

Peter Thiel — The clearest case. Self-described libertarian, major early Trump supporter (2016), key backer and mentor of J.D. Vance (including large donations to his Senate campaign), and long associated with conservative political efforts in tech and government. Frequently described as a Republican kingmaker.
Elon Musk — Shifted strongly right. Major 2024 Trump campaign supporter and donor, led the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), and has been vocal against progressive cultural and regulatory positions. SpaceX/Starlink and xAI (Grok) are his companies.
David Sacks — Conservative/libertarian. Trump administration AI and crypto czar, pro-Trump fundraiser and All-In podcast co-host, and consistently aligned with the right in recent years.
Keith Rabois — Openly conservative and self-described contrarian. Supported Trump in 2024, has criticized progressive policies, and is active in right-leaning tech and political circles.
Ken Howery — Served as U.S. ambassador under Trump (Sweden, later Denmark) and has supported pro-Trump efforts.
Left-leaning / Democratic
Reid Hoffman (LinkedIn co-founder) — The main clear Democratic figure. Long-time major donor to Democratic candidates and causes (tens of millions across cycles to Biden/Harris-aligned efforts and other Dems). He has occasionally given to moderate or anti-Trump Republicans (e.g., Nikki Haley), but his overall record is strongly Democratic. He has preferred the term “PayPal Network” over “Mafia.”
More centrist or less partisan
Max Levchin (Affirm CEO, PayPal co-founder/CTO) — Avoids strong party affiliation. Anti-socialist (citing his Soviet upbringing), pro-capitalist, critical of heavy redistribution, supportive of skilled immigration, and has called January 6 a “disgrace.” He has engaged with both sides on policy but is not a reliable left or right partisan.
Most other members (YouTube founders like Steve Chen/Chad Hurley/Jawed Karim, Yelp’s Jeremy Stoppelman and Russel Simmons, etc.) are not as prominently political in public donations or statements.

Summary: The publicly political core is right-leaning (Thiel, Musk, Sacks, Rabois, Howery) with Reid Hoffman as the clear left/Democratic counterweight. This mix is widely noted in coverage of the group’s later influence.⁠Wikipedia

Political views can evolve, and private preferences aren’t always public, but the above is based on donations, appointments, statements, and consistent reporting.Peter Thiel’s political influence is substantial but distinctive: it runs more through people, institutions, and long-term networks than through pure check-writing volume in any single cycle. He is best known as a kingmaker who helped elevate J.D. Vance, a major early Trump supporter who has since been more selective, and the co-founder/chairman of Palantir, whose government contracts give him structural influence in national security and data systems.

The Vance relationship (his clearest political success)
Thiel met Vance in 2011 after a talk at Yale Law School that Vance later called one of the most significant moments of his time there. Vance joined Thiel’s Mithril Capital, co-founded Narya Capital (Tolkien-themed, in the Thiel style), and received heavy support for his 2022 Ohio Senate race—roughly $15 million from Thiel to a pro-Vance super PAC, the largest amount then given to a single Senate candidate. Thiel also helped facilitate Vance’s introduction to Trump at Mar-a-Lago and later privately urged Trump to pick Vance as running mate.⁠Forbes

With Vance now Vice President and widely viewed as a leading 2028 Republican contender, this is Thiel’s highest-profile political outcome. Thiel has described himself as a “Vance partisan” while expressing caution about 2028 electoral prospects in general.⁠Benzinga

Trump and Republican politics
Thiel was one of the earliest prominent Silicon Valley figures to back Trump in 2016 (speaking at the RNC and donating roughly $1.25 million). He largely sat out or was cooler on the 2024 race (at one point saying he would vote for Trump “if you hold a gun to my head”). After Vance’s selection he warmed somewhat but remained relatively restrained in public donations compared with figures like Elon Musk.⁠NYTimes

In 2025–2026 he has resumed selective giving (e.g., $1.5 million to Club for Growth Action, $3 million opposing a proposed California wealth tax, and smaller amounts to GOP committees and candidates). He has also offered public or semi-public criticisms of aspects of the second Trump administration—calling some officials “not very smart,” expressing skepticism of the Iran war (“we should not have done it”), and warning of risks from a democratic-socialist Democratic nominee in 2028.⁠Politico

His overall pattern is that of a selective, high-leverage donor rather than a constant megadonor.

Institutional and defense-tech influence
Thiel chairs Palantir, whose data-analytics software has long-term contracts with U.S. intelligence, military, and other agencies. Under the second Trump administration, Palantir has won or expanded significant work (including large Army consolidations that could reach into the billions, ICE-related systems, and other federal deals). The company has a well-documented revolving door with government.⁠FT

Through Founders Fund, Thiel is a major backer of Anduril (autonomous systems, border surveillance towers, and other defense tech). Anduril has secured substantial contracts and partnered with Palantir and others on government work. These companies benefit from broader defense modernization and border-security spending priorities.⁠FT

This creates influence that is structural (contracts, alumni networks, policy relevance) rather than purely electoral.

Ideology and broader network
Thiel is commonly described as a techno-libertarian or libertarian nationalist. He has long argued that technology can be an alternative to conventional politics and has written critically about aspects of democracy and stagnation. He has connections to figures associated with “neoreactionary” thought (including Curtis Yarvin) and has recently given lectures warning about AI regulation, “Antichrist”-style risks, and the appeal of socialism to younger generations facing debt and housing costs. He has also developed ties in Argentina under President Javier Milei and explored ideas around autonomous or low-regulation jurisdictions.⁠DW

His network includes the Thiel Fellowship (which has backed many young founders), Founders Fund partners and portfolio companies, and a wider “Thielverse” of investors and operators who have entered government roles or political activity.

Criticisms and limits
Critics on the left focus on Palantir’s surveillance and targeting applications, the concentration of unelected tech power, and the scale of defense contracts. Some on the right or within MAGA circles have noted his occasional criticisms of Trump-era decisions or his preference for certain policy directions over pure loyalty. Thiel himself has sometimes expressed skepticism about the efficacy of large political spending.

Bottom line: Thiel’s influence is real and durable—most visibly through Vance’s rise, Palantir’s and Anduril’s government roles, and a long-running network of tech talent and capital—but it is selective, ideological, and more institutional than the high-volume campaign spending of some other billionaires. It is frequently resented from multiple political directions precisely because of that combination of money, ideas, and operational access.

Ken Howery — Served as U.S. ambassador under Trump (Sweden, later Denmark) and has supported pro-Trump efforts.
Left-leaning / Democratic
Reid Hoffman (LinkedIn co-founder) — The main clear Democratic figure. Long-time major donor to Democratic candidates and causes (tens of millions across cycles to Biden/Harris-aligned efforts and other Dems). He has occasionally given to moderate or anti-Trump Republicans (e.g., Nikki Haley), but his overall record is strongly Democratic. He has preferred the term “PayPal Network” over “Mafia.”
More centrist or less partisan
Max Levchin (Affirm CEO, PayPal co-founder/CTO) — Avoids strong party affiliation. Anti-socialist (citing his Soviet upbringing), pro-capitalist, critical of heavy redistribution, supportive of skilled immigration, and has called January 6 a “disgrace.” He has engaged with both sides on policy but is not a reliable left or right partisan.
Most other members (YouTube founders like Steve Chen/Chad Hurley/Jawed Karim, Yelp’s Jeremy Stoppelman and Russel Simmons, etc.) are not as prominently political in public donations or statements.

Summary: The publicly political core is right-leaning (Thiel, Musk, Sacks, Rabois, Howery) with Reid Hoffman as the clear left/Democratic counterweight. This mix is widely noted in coverage of the group’s later influence.⁠Wikipedia

Political views can evolve, and private preferences aren’t always public, but the above is based on donations, appointments, statements, and consistent reporting.Peter Thiel’s political influence is substantial but distinctive: it runs more through people, institutions, and long-term networks than through pure check-writing volume in any single cycle. He is best known as a kingmaker who helped elevate J.D. Vance, a major early Trump supporter who has since been more selective, and the co-founder/chairman of Palantir, whose government contracts give him structural influence in national security and data systems.

The Vance relationship (his clearest political success)
Thiel met Vance in 2011 after a talk at Yale Law School that Vance later called one of the most significant moments of his time there. Vance joined Thiel’s Mithril Capital, co-founded Narya Capital (Tolkien-themed, in the Thiel style), and received heavy support for his 2022 Ohio Senate race—roughly $15 million from Thiel to a pro-Vance super PAC, the largest amount then given to a single Senate candidate. Thiel also helped facilitate Vance’s introduction to Trump at Mar-a-Lago and later privately urged Trump to pick Vance as running mate.⁠Forbes

With Vance now Vice President and widely viewed as a leading 2028 Republican contender, this is Thiel’s highest-profile political outcome. Thiel has described himself as a “Vance partisan” while expressing caution about 2028 electoral prospects in general.⁠Benzinga

Trump and Republican politics
Thiel was one of the earliest prominent Silicon Valley figures to back Trump in 2016 (speaking at the RNC and donating roughly $1.25 million). He largely sat out or was cooler on the 2024 race (at one point saying he would vote for Trump “if you hold a gun to my head”). After Vance’s selection he warmed somewhat but remained relatively restrained in public donations compared with figures like Elon Musk.⁠NYTimes

In 2025–2026 he has resumed selective giving (e.g., $1.5 million to Club for Growth Action, $3 million opposing a proposed California wealth tax, and smaller amounts to GOP committees and candidates). He has also offered public or semi-public criticisms of aspects of the second Trump administration—calling some officials “not very smart,” expressing skepticism of the Iran war (“we should not have done it”), and warning of risks from a democratic-socialist Democratic nominee in 2028.⁠Politico

His overall pattern is that of a selective, high-leverage donor rather than a constant megadonor.

Institutional and defense-tech influence
Thiel chairs Palantir, whose data-analytics software has long-term contracts with U.S. intelligence, military, and other agencies. Under the second Trump administration, Palantir has won or expanded significant work (including large Army consolidations that could reach into the billions, ICE-related systems, and other federal deals). The company has a well-documented revolving door with government.⁠FT

Through Founders Fund, Thiel is a major backer of Anduril (autonomous systems, border surveillance towers, and other defense tech). Anduril has secured substantial contracts and partnered with Palantir and others on government work. These companies benefit from broader defense modernization and border-security spending priorities.⁠FT

This creates influence that is structural (contracts, alumni networks, policy relevance) rather than purely electoral.

Ideology and broader network
Thiel is commonly described as a techno-libertarian or libertarian nationalist. He has long argued that technology can be an alternative to conventional politics and has written critically about aspects of democracy and stagnation. He has connections to figures associated with “neoreactionary” thought (including Curtis Yarvin) and has recently given lectures warning about AI regulation, “Antichrist”-style risks, and the appeal of socialism to younger generations facing debt and housing costs. He has also developed ties in Argentina under President Javier Milei and explored ideas around autonomous or low-regulation jurisdictions.⁠DW

His network includes the Thiel Fellowship (which has backed many young founders), Founders Fund partners and portfolio companies, and a wider “Thielverse” of investors and operators who have entered government roles or political activity.

Criticisms and limits
Critics on the left focus on Palantir’s surveillance and targeting applications, the concentration of unelected tech power, and the scale of defense contracts. Some on the right or within MAGA circles have noted his occasional criticisms of Trump-era decisions or his preference for certain policy directions over pure loyalty. Thiel himself has sometimes expressed skepticism about the efficacy of large political spending.

Bottom line: Thiel’s influence is real and durable—most visibly through Vance’s rise, Palantir’s and Anduril’s government roles, and a long-running network of tech talent and capital—but it is selective, ideological, and more institutional than the high-volume campaign spending of some other billionaires. It is frequently resented from multiple political directions precisely because of that combination of money, ideas, and operational access.

text:
🇺🇸 Tonight’s midterm elections’ results will be about more than determining which party controls Congress. They will provide the first nationwide electoral assessment of Donald Trump’s presidency and offer important clues about the future direction of both parties as they begin positioning themselves for the 2028 presidential election.

I would follow the results on three levels: control of Congress, the most competitive Senate races, and the internal struggle shaping the Democratic Party.

The real story, however, will go beyond which party wins. It will be found in what the results reveal about changes in the electorate, particularly among independent voters, suburban communities and constituencies that have traditionally formed the Democratic Party’s electoral base.

With that in mind, here is my election-night watchlist.

➡️ Senate races

• Alaska – Dan Sullivan (R) vs Mary Peltola (D)

• Michigan – Abdul El-Sayed (D) vs Mike Rogers (R)

• Maine – Susan Collins (R) vs Troy Jackson (D)

• Ohio – Sherrod Brown (D) vs Jon Husted (R)

• Texas – James Talarico (D) vs Ken Paxton (R)

• Georgia – Jon Ossoff (D) vs Mike Collins (R)

• Kansas – Roger Marshall (R) vs Adam Hamilton (D)

• Iowa – Ashley Hinson (R) vs Josh Turek (D)

• New Hampshire – Chris Pappas (D) vs John Sununu (R)

➡️ House races

MI-07, TX-15, OH-07, NY-17, PA-07, PA-08 and WI-03

➡️ Governor races

GA, FL, TX, OH, WI, AK and IO

➡️ DSA and progressive movement tests

• Michigan Senate: Does El-Sayed consolidate Democratic support after Stevens's endorsement of Rogers?

• Michigan-07: Does progressive William Lawrence translate his primary success into a general-election victory?

• California: Watch the intra-Democratic contests involving progressive challengers and established Democratic incumbents.

The results will help distinguish between the ability of progressive organisations to win primaries and their ability to build broader electoral coalitions.

➡️ My election-night dashboard

• Early evening: Exit polls, turnout composition and initial results in Georgia and the eastern states.

• As results accumulate: Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Pennsylvania.

• Later evening: Texas, Kansas, Iowa and Alaska.

• Throughout the night: House seat projections and whether the Senate map is expanding or contracting for either party.

➡️ Three big questions

• Can Republicans retain both chambers despite the national polling environment?

• Can Democrats convert their advantage among independents into actual congressional seats?

• Can DSA-backed progressives win general elections without alienating the broader Democratic electorate?

🧐 Ultimately, I would pay as much attention to the composition of the electorate as to the winners. The independent vote, suburban turnout, Hispanic voters and the participation of younger progressives could tell us more about the future direction of American politics than the final national vote margin alone.

text:
Barron's view on $LITE $MRVL 

Marvell Technology's planned acquisition of Lumentum has helped erase more than $91 billion in their combined market value. But the selloff alone may not derail the deal.

Investors haven't been shy about their discontent with Marvell Technology's planned acquisition of Lumentum, and even Barron's argued that the valuation of the deal coupled with the artificial-intelligence trade coming under significant pressure were serious concerns.

Lumentum stock tumbled nearly 19% on Monday and logged its largest daily percentage decline since April 3, 2025. It wasn't much better for shares of Marvell, which fell 13% to $171.41, marking their lowest closing price level since July 29.

Between Oct. 28, the day before Bloomberg reported the two companies were discussing a merger, and the closing bell on Monday, Lumentum lost $20.80 billion in market value while $70.36 billion was wiped out from Marvell.

Put it together and the two stocks have shed more than $91 billion in market capitalization since Oct. 28. That's quite a signal that Wall Street isn't too pleased.

The selloff has also called into question the valuation of Marvell's all-stock offer. At Oct. 28 prices, the acquisition implied an enterprise value of $115 billion for Lumentum and consideration of roughly $1,132 per share — a 24% premium to Lumentum's closing price of $913.95 that day.

Lumentum shareholders will receive a fixed 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share.

That raises the question: Could one of the companies decide to pull the plug on the deal? It still requires approval from both companies' shareholders and regulatory clearances, and is expected to close in the first half of 2028.

A Morgan Stanley analyst team led by Joseph Moore and Meta Marshall noted Tuesday that another concern is that the deal also needs Chinese approval, and that China-based module makers, which buy Marvell's digital signal processors and compete with Lumentum, account for most transceiver supply.

There were murmurs even before Monday that maybe the deal could fall through.

Gordon Haskett analyst Don Bilson said in a research note that if Marvell and Lumentum hadn't announced their merger news Monday "it would have led to some head-scratching in these parts."

"More specifically, it would have had us wondering whether MRVL got cold feet over the weekend after seeing its stock fall 13% on Thursday and another 10% on Friday," Bilson said.

For now, it looks unlikely that either company will walk away from the deal even with significant market value being wiped out.

Lumentum would owe a $2.9 billion termination fee if, among other things, it accepts a superior proposal, according to regulatory filings. Marvell would owe Lumentum $5.8 billion in specified circumstances, including terminating the agreement to accept a superior proposal. A separate $3.2 billion fee would apply in certain regulatory-related terminations, according to regulatory filings.

B. Riley analyst Dave Kang said these termination fees both make a "competing bid unlikely" and partly cushions Lumentum shareholders if the deal falls apart. Kang downgraded Lumentum to Neutral from Buy on the acquisition and cut his price target to $770 from $1,142.

"Because the exchange ratio is fixed, LITE holders now carry MRVL share-price risk until close," Kang said.

After the sharp share price declines on Monday, stock market sentiment appeared to be turning somewhat on Tuesday.

Lumentum rose 0.4% to $687.30 on Tuesday while Marvell declined 0.5% to $170.86.

Some analysts argue that the merger, even with the risks, makes strategic sense for AI infrastructure.

"We like the strategic combination," Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer said in a research note in which he reiterated his Outperform rating on Marvell with a price target of $425.

Schafer said the merger "creates the leading AI connectivity pure-play" and brings Marvell's broad platform that includes digital signal processors together with Lumentum's high-power and high-speed lasers.

That would make the combined company a formidable force in the optical-networking sector, which has become integral to both the AI trade and the data-center buildout.

Marvell and Lumentum have said the combined company's total addressable market is likely to expand to around $550 billion as the merger brings together two of the largest players in optical networking.

But that too makes it an implicit bet on the data-center buildout continuing. Ever-larger data centers require optical transceivers to efficiently transfer data by converting electrical signals into light. Marvell makes the digital signal processors within those transceivers, while Lumentum produces lasers and other components.

"We believe core customers and partners also like the combination as integration and co-design become increasingly critical," Schafer added.

StoneX analyst Cody Acree agreed with this analysis. Acree reiterated Buy ratings on both Lumentum and Marvell along with price targets of $1,200 and $375, respectively.

"The industrial logic is sound," Acree said in the research note.

The analyst outlined how Lumentum makes indium phosphide lasers that generate the light in AI optical links, describing that capability as the "scarcest element in the chain."

"Together they come closest to Broadcom's integrated optics position, and co-design matters most as optics move inside the rack for scale-up," Acree added.

Raymond James analyst Simon Leopold also sounded an optimistic tone, upgrading Lumentum to Strong Buy from Outperform following the merger announcement. The analyst also raised his price target to $1,328 from $1,036 as he called the stock market's response to the merger an "overreaction."

Still, Wall Street is divided, caught between the significant potential that the combined company could have and the inherent risks.

"The strategic logic is sound, but the price leaves little room for error," Morgan Stanley analysts Moore and Marshall said.

text:
People outside of education don’t understand how much tunnel-vision there is among many of the higher ups inside of education.

Just yesterday an admin from outside my school was in the building for a meeting. Don’t know her but she seems like one of the well intentioned ones.

When she saw me she mentioned she saw my name on the list for the free SOR class being offered to middle school teachers. We chatted for a bit about how nice it was to see these changes happening in the district. (It’s also now the law in Massachusetts, btw.)

To emphasize how much of a difference several years can make, I pointed out that when I first started at my school, my classroom was used by the Reading Recovery teacher.

Her response was, “Oh wow! That’s great!”

And I was like, “No. Not great at all. Reading Recovery was a bad program.”

Many people in ed are under the impression that what we’ve been doing for the past couple of decades is fine and that we’re just tweaking it a little bit now with SOR & SOL.

We need to require some sort of 12 step-like program where in step 1 people have to actually admit that what we’ve were doing before was wrong and that things have to change substantially.

text:
OTD in 1755, Massachusetts Lieutenant Governor Spencer Phips issued a proclamation declaring the Penobscot Nation “Enemies, Rebels and Traitors” to King George II.

On July 2, during the French and Indian War, a scalp-hunting party led by James Cargill killed and scalped twelve Penobscot people, including nine attacked near Owl’s Head while returning from a peace conference at Fort St. George.

The Penobscot had been explicitly exempted from a Massachusetts scalp-bounty proclamation issued that June. Phips condemned the killings, expressed his grief to Penobscot leaders, and had Cargill arrested.

Following a September attack at Fort St. George that killed livestock, Captain Jabez Bradbury told Phips he suspected Penobscot involvement. On October 31, the House accused the Penobscot of recent hostilities and of violating treaty obligations by refusing to fight other Native nations.

At the House’s request, Phips directed the province’s subjects to pursue, capture, kill, and destroy Penobscot people.

The proclamation offered frontier troops £50 for capturing a male over twelve and £40 for his scalp. For a female of any age or a boy under twelve, the payments were £25 for a captive and £20 for a scalp.

The legislature voted to pay the bounties from the public treasury.

Veterans Day ceremony: Amarillo College will host a ceremony honoring veterans at 10:15 a.m. on Nov. 10 at the Washington Street Campus Clock Tower. 
Healthcare expansion: Cardiology Center of Amarillo has joined BSA Health System, aiming to strengthen cardiovascular care access across the Panhandle. 
Blood donation campaign: Coffee Memorial Blood Center's “Magic of Giving” promotion offers a limited-edition long-sleeve shirt to successful donors through Dec. 23, with extra rewards for O-negative donors. 
Drought improvement: The Texas Panhandle continues to see improving drought conditions for the fourth straight week. 
Game warden recruitment: Texas Parks and Wildlife is accepting applications for its 70th Law Enforcement Cadet Class through Dec. 31. 
Road work on FM 2590: Overlay work is beginning between Canyon and Amarillo. Drivers should expect periodic lane closures and pilot-car escorts through work zones. 
Biggest community takeaways: improving drought conditions, road construction on FM 2590, the Parks and Recreation tree giveaway, and the healthcare partnership are likely to have the broadest impact on Amarillo residents.

text:
Content warning: this post concerns the 1913 murder of a 13 year old girl and includes Leo Max Frank's own early statement to the detectives.

On Tuesday, November 3, 2026, we post State's Exhibit B from Leo Frank's Georgia Supreme Court appeal record. Slides 1286 and 1287 are Frank's unsigned statement made Monday morning, April 28, 1913, before Newport A. Lanford, Chief of Detectives.

Mary Anne Phagan, 13, was found murdered in the National Pencil Company basement early Sunday, April 27, 1913. Frank was the factory superintendent. Two days later he sat with Lanford and gave this account.

He said he was general superintendent and director of the company at 37 to 41 South Forsyth Street, with about 107 employees, and had held the place since August 10, 1908. He described Saturday, April 26, Memorial Day, at the factory, who came for pay, and when he said he left. He said he had told the night watchman Newt Lee on Friday night to come early Saturday "because I may go to the ball game," and that Lee got there at twenty minutes to four.

That ball-game plan was with Charles F. Ursenbach, husband of Lucille Selig Frank's sister Rosalind. Frank later called it off. Most of his accounting papers for that week were dated before Saturday. Saturday was a legal holiday.

The jury heard this statement and the rest of the evidence and convicted Frank on August 25, 1913. The Georgia Supreme Court affirmed on February 17, 1914. These two slides are one exhibit and are kept together.

Forever 13 and Never forgotten.

#MaryPhagan #LeoFrank

Appendix: Full slide transcripts

Slide 1286

STATE'S EXHIBIT B.

Frank's statement made before N. A. Lanford, Chief of Detectives, on Monday morning, April 28, 1913, this statement being unsigned:-
"I am general superintendent and director of the National Pencil Company, in Atlanta. I have held that position since August 10, 1908. My place of business is at 37 to 41 S Forsyth St. We have about 107 employees in that plant, male and female. I guess there are a few more girls than boys. Saturday, April 26th, was a holiday with our company and the factory was shut down. There were several people who came in during the morning. The office boy and the stenographer were in the office with me until noon. They left about 12 or a little after. We have a day watchman there. He left shortly before 12 o'clock. After the office boy and the stenographer left, this little girl, Mary Phagan, came in, but at the time I didn't know that was her name. She came in between 12:05 and 12:10, maybe 12:07, to get her pay envelope, her salary. I paid her and she went out of the office. I was in the inner office at my desk, the furthermost office to the left from the main office. It was impossible to see the direction she went in when she left. My impression was that she just walked away. I didn't pay any particular attention. I didn't keep the door locked downstairs that morning because the mail was coming in. I locked it at 1:10 when I went to dinner. Arthur White and Harry Denham were also in the building. They were working on the machinery, doing repair work, working on the top floor of the building, which is the fourth floor, towards the rear or about the middle of the building, but a little more to the rear. They were tightening up the belts; they are not machinists; one is a foreman in one department and the other is an assistant in another, and Denham was assisting White, and Mrs. White, the wife of Arthur White, was also in the building. She left about 1 o'clock. I went up there and told them I was going to dinner and they had to get out, and they said they had not finished and I said, 'How long will it take?' and they said until some time in the afternoon, and then I said, 'Mrs. White, you will have to go, for I am going to lock these boys in here.' Another boy came in and said he wanted to go out, but not the inside door, which I had locked. You can go in the basement from the front through the trap door. They, sir, they could get up the steps if I was out. I looked the outer door and the inner door. I got back at 3 o'clock, and maybe two or three minutes before, and I went to the office and took off my coat and then went upstairs to tell those boys I was back, and I couldn't find them at first, they were back in the dipping room in-the rear, and I said, 'Are you ready,' and they said, 'We are just ready,' and I said, 'All right, ring out when you go down to let me know when you go out,' and they rang out, and Arthur White came in the office and said, 'Mr. Frank, loan me $2.00,' and I said, 'What's the matter; we just paid off,' and he said, 'My wife robbed me,' and I gave him $2.00 and he walked away, and the two of them walked out. I locked the outer door behind them. When I am in there is no need of locking the inner door. There was only one person

Slide 1287

I was looking for to come in, and that was the night watchman. He got there at 20 minutes to four. I had previously arranged with him to get there. On Friday night I told him, after he got his money, to give him the keys and I said, 'You had better come around early to-morrow because I may go to the ball game,' and he came early because of that fact; I told him to come early and he came 20 minutes to 4. I figured that I could leave about 1 o'clock and would not come back, but it was so cold I didn't want to risk catching cold and I come back to the factory as I usually do. He come in and I said 'Newt, you are early,' and he said, 'Yes, sir,' and he had a bag of bananas with him and he offered me a banana; I didn't see them but he offered me one and I guess he had them. We have told him once he gets in that building never to go out; I told him he could go out; he got there so early and I was going to be there. He come back about 4 minutes to six; the reason I know that I was putting the clock slips in and the clock was right in front of me. I said, 'I will be ready in a minute,' and he went downstairs and I come to the office and put on my coat and hat and followed him and went out. When I went out, talking to Newt Lee was J. M. Gantt, a man I had fired about two weeks previous. Newt told me he wanted to go up to get-a-pair of shoes he left while he was working there, and Gantt said to me, 'Newt don't want me to go up,' and he said, 'You can go with me, Mr. Frank,' and I said 'That's all right, go with him, Newt,' and I went on home, and I got home about 6:25. Nothing else happened; that's all I know. I don't know what time Gantt came down after he went up. I saw him go in and I locked the door after him, but I didn't try them. I telephoned Newt. I tried to telephone him when I got home; he punches the clock at half hour intervals, and the clock and the phone is in the office, and I didn't get an answer and at 7 o'clock I called him and asked him if Gantt got his shoes and he said yes, he got them, and I said is everything all right and he said yes, and the next thing I knew they called me at 7:30 the next morning. I don't know that our watchman has been in the habit of letting people in the factory any time. I have never heard of it. I never had any trouble with the watchman about it. As to whether any of our employees go there at night, Gantt did, when he was working there; he had a key and sometimes he would have some work left over. I never have seen him go out until I go out. I go out and come back, but he has come back before I left, but that is part of his duty. I took a bath Saturday night at my home. I changed my clothes. The clothes that I changed are at home, and this is the suit of clothes I was wearing Saturday. After I left the shop I went to Jacob's Pharmacy and bought a box of candy for my wife and got home about 6:25."

STATE'S EXHIBIT C.

Piece of cord found around Mary Phagan's neck, about size of a heavy twine, with a knot in it.

text:
ELECTION DAY WATCH 2026 | REPORT 05
GEORGIA ABSENTEE BALLOT DELAYS: THREE COUNTIES, DISPUTED VOTER COUNTS AND EMERGENCY AGREEMENTS

UPDATE: NOVEMBER 3, 2026

Absentee-ballot delivery problems have affected voters in Cobb, Gwinnett and DeKalb counties, Georgia.

Election officials have acknowledged delays, lawsuits have challenged ballot handling, and counties have taken corrective action.

Here is what official records, court filings and election notices establish.

1. COBB COUNTY — VENDOR DELAYS CONFIRMED

On October 28, Cobb County acknowledged absentee-ballot mailing delays involving Fort Orange Press, its third-party ballot vendor.

The problems primarily affected ballots marked as issued between October 7 and October 15.

The county offered qualifying voters replacement ballots by USPS Priority Express Mail, with prepaid express return envelopes.

A lawsuit alleged that nearly 2,900 Cobb County voters had not received requested ballots.

The county disputed that number, describing the problem as affecting a limited group of voters.

On October 28, the plaintiff voluntarily dismissed the case after the county agreed to provide a replacement ballot.

2. GWINNETT COUNTY — EMERGENCY SETTLEMENT

On October 30, civil rights organizations filed an emergency lawsuit concerning delayed absentee ballots.

The complaint identified 1,820 registered voters whose requested ballots allegedly had not arrived on time.

On October 31, Gwinnett County reached a settlement agreeing to:

• Contact affected voters whose absentee ballots had not been returned.

• Inform them about replacement-ballot options.

• Send requested replacements overnight.

• Provide prepaid return envelopes.

The ACLU of Georgia announced the settlement on November 2.

The agreement provides corrective measures. It is not a court finding that all 1,820 voters were prevented from voting.

3. DEKALB COUNTY — SEPARATE AGREEMENT

DeKalb County also experienced reported absentee-ballot mailing delays involving Fort Orange Press.

On October 30, the county reached a separate agreement to contact affected voters and offer overnight replacement ballots with prepaid return postage.

The final number of affected DeKalb voters has not been established.

4. WERE 10,000 VOTERS AFFECTED?

Approximately 10,000 potentially affected voters across the three counties were cited in statements from Georgia Democratic Party leadership and voting-rights litigation.

That figure is not a verified count of ballots lost, rejected or never counted.

Some voters received replacement ballots. Others may have received their original ballots or voted in person.

The number ultimately unable to vote because of these delays remains unknown.

5. ELECTION DAY DEADLINE — 7 PM EASTERN

Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger reminded voters on October 29 that ordinary absentee ballots must be RECEIVED by county election officials by:

7:00 PM EASTERN
TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 3, 2026

A November 3 postmark alone does not meet that deadline.
Separate rules apply to qualifying military and overseas voters.

COBB COUNTY BALLOT RETURNS

Cobb County says completed absentee ballots may be hand-delivered to:

Cobb County Elections & Registration
995 Roswell Street NE
Marietta, GA 30060

Deadline: 7 PM today.

Cobb County also confirms that absentee ballots cannot be returned to Election Day polling locations and that its ballot drop boxes closed October 30.
6. WHAT IF A REQUESTED BALLOT NEVER ARRIVED?
Georgia election officials say requesting an absentee ballot does not automatically prevent an eligible voter from voting in person.

Voters who have not already voted may be able to cancel an outstanding absentee ballot and vote at their assigned Election Day precinct.

Election workers can assist with the cancellation process.

Cobb County Elections:
770-528-2581
ABM@cobbcounty.gov

Gwinnett County Elections:
678-226-7210
Absentee@GwinnettCounty.com

Official Georgia voter information:
https://t.co/qp2enCdmAj

Official Cobb County instructions:
https://t.co/YQU345eHXC

7. WHAT REMAINS UNKNOWN?
Officials have not yet established:
• The exact number of delayed or undelivered ballots across all three counties.

• How many affected voters successfully received replacement ballots.
• How many ultimately voted by another method.
• Whether any voters lost their opportunity to cast a ballot.

• Whether additional legal or administrative action will follow.
These questions require follow-up after Election Day.

THE BOTTOM LINE

Georgia's absentee-ballot mailing delays are documented problems, not simply social-media rumors.

Cobb County acknowledged vendor-related delays. Lawsuits raised additional concerns, and all three counties took or agreed to corrective action.

The failures deserve investigation and accountability.

However, disputed estimates and delayed ballots are not, by themselves, proof of intentional election interference or fraudulent votes.

The central questions are what caused the delays, how many voters were affected and whether eligible voters were able to cast their ballots.

• Gwinnett County absentee-ballot lawsuit
• ACLU of Georgia, November 2 settlement announcement

• FOX 5 Atlanta, November 3

text:
They are actually the most likely to get left out between them, Miami, and FSU.  They have a small, regional fan base, and minimal national following.  When you break out TV #s based on network, game time, and caliber of season, Clemson pales compared to FSU & Miami, especially when all have down seasons.  They really are a Texas Tech type of program that caught lightening in a bottle, and had a magical decade.  

Networks (and by default, conferences) want teams that deliver strong viewership even when they're having a bad season.  That's why a bad Penn St will be on Fox 5 times during a .500 season, but a ranked Illinois or ranked Northwestern is over on the BTN.  A bad PSU delivers more eyeballs than a good Illinois or NU.  

That's where Clemson is weak.  They don't have the national following to deliver strong #s when they're down.  Networks don't price what they offer conferences based on the odds a team is good or bad.  They can't, because all programs have down stretches:  Alabama, Texas, Michigan, USC, etc al.  So when push comes to shove, Clemson is going to have a hard time delivering the $90M+ in increased TV revenue that'd be required to solicit an offer of membership from the SEC or Big Ten.

FWIW, during the 2010s realignment I was as connected as you could get, and was a source for ESPN.  Even today, my roots run deep.  And, I have clients at ESPN, CBS, the SEC, and P4 athletics depth across the country.  I work in a different area of analytics, but my consultancy has overlap.  So, I understand the subject well.

text:
Something I keep telling Southern Indiana sellers right now: the headlines about a "cooling market" don't match what's actually happening on the ground in Jeffersonville and New Albany.

Well-priced homes in good condition are still moving fast — sometimes with multiple offers. The slowdown is mostly hitting homes that are overpriced or need work the seller hasn't accounted for.

If you're wondering what your specific situation looks like, that's a better question than "how's the market" — because the market isn't one thing right now. It depends on your price point, your condition, and your neighborhood.

Happy to run the numbers for your street specifically. (502) 379-2365

text:
National Geographic Names Five US Locations on 2027 Travel List

National Geographic named five destinations in the United States among its Best of the World travel list for 2027. The selected locations include Madison in Wisconsin, the Pacific Coast Highway in California, the Southern Ozarks across Missouri and Arkansas, Baltimore in Maryland, and Catalina Island off the California coast.

Madison received recognition for its outdoor spaces, food scene, and university culture. The city features over 200 miles of hiking trails and bikeways, including a 13-mile cycling loop around Lake Monona. The Pacific Coast Highway was highlighted for its coastal scenery, arts communities, and the reopening of sections in Big Sur. Laguna Beach will mark its centennial in 2027, while Lompoc features local murals and a wine region.

The Southern Ozarks earned recognition for outdoor recreation, such as mountain biking in Bella Vista and exploring the 10,000-acre Dogwood Canyon Nature Park in Missouri. Baltimore was noted for its railway history and waterfront attractions, including a planned upgrade for the National Museum of Railroad History and Innovation. Finally, Catalina Island offers coastal landscapes and the 38.5-mile Trans-Catalina Trail.

Georgia and Missouri may be spending smarter, but they also have the luxury of potentially being able to accomplish more with less. The bigger issue is that offers are going out in four to six weeks, and I would expect that $31–35 million range for the top half of the roster to increase to somewhere around $40–45 million. 
The real question is whether we're going to get ahead of that increase and position ourselves to compete, or whether we're going to fall into the same pattern we've seen under Hunter and end up somewhere around 10th–12th in spending.

text:
Yes. Peter Thiel is the central figure—often called the “don”—of the PayPal Mafia.⁠Wikipedia

The PayPal Mafia is the informal name for the group of PayPal founders and early employees who, after eBay’s 2002 acquisition of the company, founded, funded, or helped scale many major tech companies (LinkedIn, YouTube, Yelp, Palantir, SpaceX, Affirm, and others). The label stuck after a 2007 Fortune magazine article and a staged photo of members in mafia-style attire at a San Francisco bar.⁠Wikipedia

Key members (commonly listed)
Here are the best-known ones, drawn from Wikipedia and contemporary reporting (lists vary slightly and have expanded over time; not every early employee is always included):

Peter Thiel — Co-founder and former CEO of Confinity/PayPal. Later co-founded Palantir (data analytics widely used by government and intelligence clients), founded Founders Fund (venture firm), and was the first major outside investor in Facebook. Also involved with Clarium Capital and other funds.
Elon Musk — Founded https://t.co/SlJQFQgwEP, which merged with Thiel’s Confinity to form PayPal. Later founded SpaceX (including Starlink), Neuralink, The Boring Company; took control of Tesla; acquired Twitter (now X). He also founded xAI, the company behind Grok.
Max Levchin — Co-founder and CTO. Later founded Affirm (buy-now-pay-later) and Slide; sometimes called the “consigliere.”
Reid Hoffman — Early executive. Founded LinkedIn; early investor in Facebook and other companies; more Democratic-leaning politically than some of the others.
David Sacks — Former COO. Founded Yammer (acquired by Microsoft) and https://t.co/cddPyVi0zb. Later served as a Trump administration advisor on AI and crypto.
Luke Nosek — Co-founder. Partner at Founders Fund.
Ken Howery — Early CFO. Partner at Founders Fund; served as U.S. ambassador (Sweden, then Denmark).
Roelof Botha — CFO. Later partner at Sequoia Capital.
Keith Rabois — Executive. Later at LinkedIn, Square, and various VC firms.
YouTube founders — Steve Chen, Chad Hurley, and Jawed Karim (PayPal engineers/designers).
Yelp co-founders — Jeremy Stoppelman and Russel Simmons.
Others sometimes included: Premal Shah (Kiva), Nathan Gettings (Palantir/Affirm), Jack Selby, Scott Banister, and more. Joe Lonsdale (Palantir co-founder, 8VC) is sometimes noted as a junior associate/intern-era figure.
The group is credited with seeding a large portion of modern Silicon Valley consumer internet, fintech, and later hard-tech/defense companies through mutual investment, board seats, and advice. Founders Fund (Thiel and others) was an early institutional investor in SpaceX.

Thiel, Vance, and government-related companies
Thiel has been a significant backer of J.D. Vance: he mentored him, helped fund his venture efforts, gave roughly $15 million to support Vance’s 2022 Senate campaign (via a super PAC), and helped facilitate introductions that aided Vance’s rise, including with Trump. Vance later became Trump’s vice president.⁠Forbes

On the “spy accessory / data” side: Thiel co-founded and chairs Palantir, whose software is used by U.S. intelligence, military, and other government clients for data analysis and integration. He is a major investor (via Founders Fund) in Anduril, a defense technology company focused on autonomous systems, drones, surveillance towers, and related military hardware/software. Founders Fund has also been a major early investor in SpaceX/Starlink. These companies have secured substantial government contracts; critics on both the left (surveillance/power concentration concerns) and parts of the right (unelected influence, certain foreign-policy or cultural positions) have expressed resentment or skepticism toward the concentration of power and political activity.⁠Strobofactory

Starlink is part of SpaceX (Musk). Grok is developed by xAI (Musk). Thiel is not a direct founder or controller of those, but the overlapping network (PayPal alumni, Founders Fund investments, personal and political ties) is real and frequently noted.

In short: Thiel is the central “don” of the PayPal Mafia, which includes Musk (SpaceX/Starlink/xAI/Grok) and others who built or backed many of the companies you mentioned. The political and institutional influence is well-documented; so is the resulting criticism from multiple directions.The PayPal Mafia is not uniformly left or right. Public political activity splits clearly among the best-known members.

Right-leaning / conservative / libertarian / Trump-aligned
These are the most publicly active on the right:

Peter Thiel — The clearest case. Self-described libertarian, major early Trump supporter (2016), key backer and mentor of J.D. Vance (including large donations to his Senate campaign), and long associated with conservative political efforts in tech and government. Frequently described as a Republican kingmaker.
Elon Musk — Shifted strongly right. Major 2024 Trump campaign supporter and donor, led the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), and has been vocal against progressive cultural and regulatory positions. SpaceX/Starlink and xAI (Grok) are his companies.
David Sacks — Conservative/libertarian. Trump administration AI and crypto czar, pro-Trump fundraiser and All-In podcast co-host, and consistently aligned with the right in recent years.
Keith Rabois — Openly conservative and self-described contrarian. Supported Trump in 2024, has criticized progressive policies, and is active in right-leaning tech and political circles.
Ken Howery — Served as U.S. ambassador under Trump (Sweden, later Denmark) and has supported pro-Trump efforts.
Left-leaning / Democratic
Reid Hoffman (LinkedIn co-founder) — The main clear Democratic figure. Long-time major donor to Democratic candidates and causes (tens of millions across cycles to Biden/Harris-aligned efforts and other Dems). He has occasionally given to moderate or anti-Trump Republicans (e.g., Nikki Haley), but his overall record is strongly Democratic. He has preferred the term “PayPal Network” over “Mafia.”
More centrist or less partisan
Max Levchin (Affirm CEO, PayPal co-founder/CTO) — Avoids strong party affiliation. Anti-socialist (citing his Soviet upbringing), pro-capitalist, critical of heavy redistribution, supportive of skilled immigration, and has called January 6 a “disgrace.” He has engaged with both sides on policy but is not a reliable left or right partisan.
Most other members (YouTube founders like Steve Chen/Chad Hurley/Jawed Karim, Yelp’s Jeremy Stoppelman and Russel Simmons, etc.) are not as prominently political in public donations or statements.

Summary: The publicly political core is right-leaning (Thiel, Musk, Sacks, Rabois, Howery) with Reid Hoffman as the clear left/Democratic counterweight. This mix is widely noted in coverage of the group’s later influence.⁠Wikipedia

Political views can evolve, and private preferences aren’t always public, but the above is based on donations, appointments, statements, and consistent reporting.Peter Thiel’s political influence is substantial but distinctive: it runs more through people, institutions, and long-term networks than through pure check-writing volume in any single cycle. He is best known as a kingmaker who helped elevate J.D. Vance, a major early Trump supporter who has since been more selective, and the co-founder/chairman of Palantir, whose government contracts give him structural influence in national security and data systems.

The Vance relationship (his clearest political success)
Thiel met Vance in 2011 after a talk at Yale Law School that Vance later called one of the most significant moments of his time there. Vance joined Thiel’s Mithril Capital, co-founded Narya Capital (Tolkien-themed, in the Thiel style), and received heavy support for his 2022 Ohio Senate race—roughly $15 million from Thiel to a pro-Vance super PAC, the largest amount then given to a single Senate candidate. Thiel also helped facilitate Vance’s introduction to Trump at Mar-a-Lago and later privately urged Trump to pick Vance as running mate.⁠Forbes

With Vance now Vice President and widely viewed as a leading 2028 Republican contender, this is Thiel’s highest-profile political outcome. Thiel has described himself as a “Vance partisan” while expressing caution about 2028 electoral prospects in general.⁠Benzinga

Trump and Republican politics
Thiel was one of the earliest prominent Silicon Valley figures to back Trump in 2016 (speaking at the RNC and donating roughly $1.25 million). He largely sat out or was cooler on the 2024 race (at one point saying he would vote for Trump “if you hold a gun to my head”). After Vance’s selection he warmed somewhat but remained relatively restrained in public donations compared with figures like Elon Musk.⁠NYTimes

In 2025–2026 he has resumed selective giving (e.g., $1.5 million to Club for Growth Action, $3 million opposing a proposed California wealth tax, and smaller amounts to GOP committees and candidates). He has also offered public or semi-public criticisms of aspects of the second Trump administration—calling some officials “not very smart,” expressing skepticism of the Iran war (“we should not have done it”), and warning of risks from a democratic-socialist Democratic nominee in 2028.⁠Politico

His overall pattern is that of a selective, high-leverage donor rather than a constant megadonor.

Institutional and defense-tech influence
Thiel chairs Palantir, whose data-analytics software has long-term contracts with U.S. intelligence, military, and other agencies. Under the second Trump administration, Palantir has won or expanded significant work (including large Army consolidations that could reach into the billions, ICE-related systems, and other federal deals). The company has a well-documented revolving door with government.⁠FT

Through Founders Fund, Thiel is a major backer of Anduril (autonomous systems, border surveillance towers, and other defense tech). Anduril has secured substantial contracts and partnered with Palantir and others on government work. These companies benefit from broader defense modernization and border-security spending priorities.⁠FT

This creates influence that is structural (contracts, alumni networks, policy relevance) rather than purely electoral.

Ideology and broader network
Thiel is commonly described as a techno-libertarian or libertarian nationalist. He has long argued that technology can be an alternative to conventional politics and has written critically about aspects of democracy and stagnation. He has connections to figures associated with “neoreactionary” thought (including Curtis Yarvin) and has recently given lectures warning about AI regulation, “Antichrist”-style risks, and the appeal of socialism to younger generations facing debt and housing costs. He has also developed ties in Argentina under President Javier Milei and explored ideas around autonomous or low-regulation jurisdictions.⁠DW

His network includes the Thiel Fellowship (which has backed many young founders), Founders Fund partners and portfolio companies, and a wider “Thielverse” of investors and operators who have entered government roles or political activity.

Criticisms and limits
Critics on the left focus on Palantir’s surveillance and targeting applications, the concentration of unelected tech power, and the scale of defense contracts. Some on the right or within MAGA circles have noted his occasional criticisms of Trump-era decisions or his preference for certain policy directions over pure loyalty. Thiel himself has sometimes expressed skepticism about the efficacy of large political spending.

Bottom line: Thiel’s influence is real and durable—most visibly through Vance’s rise, Palantir’s and Anduril’s government roles, and a long-running network of tech talent and capital—but it is selective, ideological, and more institutional than the high-volume campaign spending of some other billionaires. It is frequently resented from multiple political directions precisely because of that combination of money, ideas, and operational access.

The meaning of this scene from Apocalypto is that, in the end, the white Christian man arrived to put an end to paganism and the widespread practice of human sacrifice among indigenous peoples—brown, black, and white—around the world.

In Maya and Aztec societies, captives and slaves were routinely dragged up temple pyramids, held down on stone altars, and had their chests cut open with obsidian knives so priests could rip out their still-beating hearts as offerings to the gods. Victims were also decapitated, thrown alive into sacred cenotes, or flayed; their skulls were displayed on racks, and in some cases parts of the bodies were eaten. These were not rare events—major temples could see thousands sacrificed in a single ceremony, and constant warfare was waged largely to capture more victims.

White pagan societies in Europe practiced their own aggressive forms of ritual violence. In the Roman world, human sacrifice was carried out in earlier periods and in moments of crisis, including the live burial of Gauls and Greeks after the Battle of Cannae, while the origins of the gladiatorial games lay in the ritual slaughter of captives as funeral offerings to the dead. Among Germanic tribes, archaeological evidence from bog bodies shows victims who were hanged, throat-cut, bludgeoned, or subjected to multiple forms of killing in overkill rituals; captives and slaves were offered as blood sacrifices to gods such as Odin, often drowned, stabbed, or left hanging from sacred trees, and prisoners taken in war were regularly killed to honor the gods and the dead.

Black pagan societies in Africa also practiced large-scale human sacrifice. In kingdoms such as Dahomey, Ashanti, Benin, and others, captives, slaves, and criminals were regularly killed as offerings to the gods and ancestors—often by beheading, throat-cutting, or live burial during annual festivals and royal ceremonies. Thousands could be sacrificed in a single custom; skulls and body parts were displayed, and warfare was frequently conducted to supply victims for these rituals.

Jews practiced paganism and human sacrifice. Kings Ahaz and Manasseh made their sons pass through the fire. People burned their children in the Valley of Hinnom. Solomon built high places for Chemosh and Molech. The Northern Kingdom set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan. Ahab and Jezebel promoted Baal worship. High places, Asherah poles, and foreign cults were repeatedly established and used. These acts are recorded in 2 Kings 16:3, 21:6, 1 Kings 11, 1 Kings 12, 1 Kings 16–18, Jeremiah 7 and 19, and elsewhere.

Across these cultures, the belief that the gods required human life and blood was widespread, and warfare often supplied the victims. With the coming of Jesus Christ, the New Testament, and the spread of Christianity, these sacrificial systems and the pagan practices that sustained them were nullified and destroyed. The New Testament declares that the death of Jesus is the final sacrifice that ends every blood offering, and Christian expansion suppressed and replaced these rites wherever it took hold. Christians themselves were also sacrificed and killed for refusing to participate in pagan rites and for working to stop them.

JESUS CHRIST IS KING.
