text:
The “Obey Your Father” Bhaal ending is actually the most biblically moral choice in Baldur’s Gate 3

Hear me out before you smash that reply button.

Bhaal isn’t some cartoon devil. He’s the Angel of Death with a better PR team. In the Old Testament the Angel of Death shows up, looks at a city full of corruption, and goes “yeah, no.” Sodom and Gomorrah didn’t get a second chance because the locals were “just vibing.” They were running the exact same playbook as Baldur’s Gate: open degeneracy, cultists on every corner, and people who looked at a literal mind-flayer and said “yeah, I’d hit that.”The Dark Urge isn’t “falling to his worst impulses.” He’s the guy who finally reads the room, sees the false prophets (every companion who wants you to “be better” while they’re actively sleeping with demons, bears, or each other), and does what the Angel of Death does: purge.

Let’s go down the list of Baldurian sins:

Tieflings are canonically people with infernal blood. Demons with good PR. The Grove plot is literally “outsiders (demons + cultists) force their way onto private property and the druids are the bad guys for complaining.” Kagha says it. Halsin later confirms in Act 3 that the woods get tainted by civilization. The only way you don’t have to fight the druids is if you let the demons stay. The druids were right.

The bear scene. I’m not elaborating. The Bible does not have a “druid turns into a bear and the party is cool with it” clause.

The Emperor is the founder of the city and also a squid that wants to romance you. The city is named after a mind-flayer. That’s not a plot twist. That’s a warning label.

Rampant homosexuality, the drow twins (incest), citizens who want to sleep with mind-flayers, gith who at least still treat humans as people instead of content… the whole place is one long Sodom & Gomorrah speedrun.

Alfira shows up as a lesbian bard, plays the lute, and immediately runs the soft emotional-manipulation routine so you’ll feel protective of a stranger. The Dark Urge kills her. Later Dad tells you to kill Isobel. Do that and she and Dame Aylin both die. Aylin and Isobel spent the campaign sticking it to Ketheric, the father who damned himself for his daughter, then treated the wreckage as a romantic victory lap. No partial credit.

Faerûn in general is a warlock convention. Ambitious wizards trying to sleep with pagan gods, Thayan Red Wizards, people making deals with demons so casually it started a blood war. A diabolist and a devil are allowed to operate inside the city. Bhaal looks at this and says “purge.” That’s not evil. That’s maintenance.

Even the “good” endings don’t escape it. Wyll either keeps the devil pact for the Peter Pan thrill or becomes duke by killing his father. Gale either teaches illusion tricks to kids or ascends to lust after a pagan goddess. Shadowheart either goes full travel girly or kills her parents. Karlach dies or goes back to the Hells for more wrath and war-lust. Astarion becomes a bigger monster or just more of the same. Minthara keeps killing. Halsin, lets not go there. The redemption is cosmetic. The underlying arrangements stay.

Withers gets sold as the calm, holy undead who just wants to help. He’s a pagan undead still serving Jergal, the god of death-and-knowledge who handed his portfolio to Bhaal, Myrkul, and Bane and then stuck around to keep the books. Knowledge of that kind is the apple: forbidden, recorded, and offered anyway. He raises the dead and hands you unwilling hirelings. Bhaal doesn’t do that. Bhaal doesn’t resurrect, doesn’t staff your party with corpses, and doesn’t keep a ledger so the next chosen can shop. He just wants the false prophet and the city that enabled her removed.

On the Absolute itself: Bhaal sends the butler, calls Orin a false prophet and usurper, and notes she killed the previous butler. Her own grandfather agrees with the assessment until he flips. Gortash himself says he prefers you to Orin because you’re more reasonable and supports your birthright. The Emperor confirms Gortash is being sincere. Bhaal isn’t the one who started the cult that ate the Sword Coast. He’s the one who wants the usurper removed.

The “everyone lives and you get the happy romance” ending is the reform-Sodom option. They live and then have to deal with a Gith–illithid war, the same arrangements continue, Nine-Fingers is treated as an acceptable power broker, the Blood War is still running, warlocks are still making deals, and a diabolist is still allowed to operate in the city. “Everyone lives” just means the problems are still on the board.Even the name is doing work. 

“Bhaal” is one letter away from Baal, the Canaanite god the Old Testament spent entire books telling people to stop worshipping. The Dark Urge obeying Bhaal is the same energy as the Israelites finally deciding the Baal poles had to go. False prophets everywhere, the city is rotten, and one guy with a very direct instruction from Dad finally does something about it. The dark urge even gets baptized to become formally recognized after purging the abomination that is Valeria a gold flying gender ambiguous elephant monster.

So yes. The “Obey Your Father” ending is the closest thing BG3 has to an Old Testament morality play. Everyone else is trying to reform Sodom. The Dark Urge is just the Angel of Death who got tired of the paperwork.

text:
Ron Goldman was off work. He brought glasses to O.J. Simpson's ex-wife's house, and both were stabbed to death. A jury held O.J. responsible and told him to pay $33,500,000. He barely paid. He did 9 years, but over old footballs. He died owing Ron's father $58,000,000.

Brentwood, Los Angeles, June 12, 1994. Nicole Brown Simpson's mother had dinner at Mezzaluna and left her glasses behind. Ron worked there, but he wasn't even their waiter. He was 25, twenty days from his birthday, and also taught tennis and picked up modeling jobs. After his shift he offered to drop the glasses off at Nicole's place.

Shortly after midnight, Ron and Nicole were found stabbed to death outside her home.

Nicole was O.J. Simpson's ex-wife. Within days he was charged with both murders. The trial ran for eight months. On October 3, 1995, the jury took less than four hours to find him not guilty.

Ron's father, Fred, didn't stop. He sued. In 1997 a civil jury, with a lower bar of proof, found O.J. responsible for both deaths and ordered him to pay $33,500,000.

O.J. moved to Florida, where the law protects your home from creditors.
His NFL and actors' union pensions were protected too.
The Goldmans took his Heisman Trophy and sold it for $255,500.
They took the rights to his book, "If I Did It," and published it themselves.
By their own count, they collected about 1% of what he owed.

In 2007 O.J. walked into a Las Vegas hotel room with armed men to take back sports memorabilia he said was his. "I didn't want to steal anything from anyone," he later told the judge. On October 3, 2008, exactly 13 years after his murder acquittal, a jury convicted him. He got up to 33 years and served 9.

In 2009, while he sat in prison, a judge handed him back the 3 ties he wore at his murder trial.

In the video below, O.J. sits in a prison uniform and tells the court why he thought all of it was legal.

O.J. died in April 2024, at 76. That same month, his expired credit card sold at auction for $10,675. His longtime lawyer, now running the estate, said he hoped the Goldmans would get "zero." In November 2025 the estate finally accepted that it owes Ron's father $58,000,000. By the lawyer's own estimate, the whole estate is worth under $1,000,000.

His Vegas lawyer suggested the sentence was payback: "It's very difficult to separate the California case from the Nevada case." The judge said it wasn't: "I'm not here to try and cause any retribution or any payback." Fred Goldman said it was "satisfying seeing him in shackles like he belongs."

The jury took less than four hours to let O.J. go. Ron's father has been chasing the money for almost 30 years.

So was O.J. an innocent man the courts kept punishing, or a man who got away with it and never paid?

text:
$DRH Q3 2026 earnings: DiamondRock raises its full-year plan, as luxury resorts lift margins

DiamondRock Hospitality Company, the owner of 35 upscale US hotels and resorts, filled more rooms at higher prices while keeping property costs in check. Revenue from hotels owned a year ago rose 6%, and hotel cash profit grew twice as fast because housekeeping and front-desk labor costs stayed flat. Chief executive Jeffrey J. Donnelly raised the full-year outlook for a third time, though by our math the plan still leaves fourth-quarter operating cash profit down 1%.

• Comparable room revenue per available room: $𝟐𝟐𝟔.𝟎𝟏 (+6.6% from a year ago)
• Comparable hotel profit margin: 𝟑𝟎.𝟖𝟏% (+1.7 percentage points from a year ago)
• Funds from operations per share, excluding one-offs: $𝟎.𝟑𝟐 (+10.3% from a year ago)
• Full-year room revenue outlook: 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝟏.𝟕𝟓 𝐩𝐭𝐬 (middle of the range: 5.0% growth)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because hotel profit margins expanded without help from one-off tax refunds, and third-quarter demand easily beat what the company's own prior outlook pointed to. One caution: beating that conservative second-half target proves the old plan was cautious, not that next year's thin advance group bookings are fixed, and management spent $31 million on a Delaware resort while leaving its share buyback untouched.

The question now is whether affluent resort demand and renovation gains can carry 2027, or if soft mid-priced leisure travel and rising costs will slow profit growth once easy comparisons pass. Fourth-quarter margins and the first 2027 group booking numbers on the call will tell.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐋𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐁𝐨𝐨𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐮𝐥𝐥-𝐘𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐠𝐚𝐢𝐧
DiamondRock measures underlying sales using comparable revenue per available room (RevPAR), which tracks room revenue across hotels owned at the end of the quarter. Three months ago, the full-year outlook pointed to almost no growth in the second half. Chief executive Jeffrey J. Donnelly said the third quarter beat the company's own expectations because of "healthy demand and higher rates across both transient and group segments".

• Comparable RevPAR: $226.01, up 6.6% from a year ago
• Average daily room rate: $290.46, up 3.8%
• Occupancy: 77.8%, up 2.0 percentage points
• Food and beverage revenue: $72.2 million, up 7.1%

Donnelly added that "Given the strength of our third quarter results and our fourth quarter booking pace, we are raising our 2026 guidance again." By our math, the new full-year target lifts second-half operating cash profit to $156.0 million, beating the $141.5 million to $151.5 million range implied three months ago. That beats the prior plan, but it shows only that the old outlook was cautious rather than proving that advance group bookings for 2027 have recovered.

What to watch: fourth-quarter comparable RevPAR against the 3.9% growth rate implied by the full-year outlook. Another beat of more than 1.5 percentage points would show that short-notice bookings continue to make up for a thin advance group book.

🟢 𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐲 𝐑𝐨𝐨𝐦 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐇𝐨𝐭𝐞𝐥 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐬
DiamondRock tracks hotel profitability using comparable Hotel Adjusted EBITDA margin, which is the share of hotel revenue left after property operating costs. Last quarter's margin included a $6.9 million one-off benefit from a "favorable settlement of multi-year property tax appeals for the Company's two Chicago hotels". The third quarter had no tax refund, so it tested whether cost control could hold up on its own.

Comparable hotel operating costs rose 3.9% from a year ago while comparable revenue grew 6.4%, lifting the hotel profit margin by 1.66 percentage points to 30.81%. Rooms operating costs (housekeeping and front-desk labor) stayed flat in dollars and fell 0.7 percentage points of revenue, while other property-level expenses (such as insurance and property taxes) fell 1.1 points. Donnelly credited "operating efficiencies we have built across the portfolio" for lifting free cash flow, which rose 31% over the first nine months by our math as the company also trimmed the top end of its 2026 renovation budget by $5 million.

What to watch: comparable hotel operating expense growth in the fourth quarter. A reading near or below 3% would confirm that property labor and insurance savings are offsetting higher union wages.

🟢 𝐑𝐞𝐧𝐨𝐯𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐋𝐮𝐱𝐮𝐫𝐲 𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐬 𝐎𝐮𝐭𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐢𝐧
The hotel owner has concentrated its renovation spending on upscale resorts and independent properties where affluent guests pay over $400 a night. It also keeps about 90% of its management contracts terminable at will, giving it more control over daily operations. Last year it spent $25 million to combine L'Auberge de Sedona with an adjacent inn, and in the first quarter it finished room upgrades at Henderson Park Inn and Courtyard New York Midtown East.

• L'Auberge de Sedona total revenue per room: up 36.3% from a year ago
• Cavallo Point total revenue per room: up 20.8%
• Henderson Beach Resort total revenue per room: up 21.1%
• Courtyard New York Midtown East total revenue per room: up 14.0%

Those renovated and high-rate properties carried the quarter: L'Auberge de Sedona alone raised its third-quarter hotel cash profit from $0.6 million to $2.5 million. Because affluent leisure travelers are still spending freely on rooms and dining, the top fünf resorts by room rate grew total revenue per room by an average of 15.1% by our math, more than double the 6.5% company rate.

What to watch: initial 2027 revenue per room outlook on the fourth-quarter call. It will show whether the ramp at recently renovated hotels in San Diego and Alpharetta can keep total growth above 4% next year.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐅𝐮𝐥𝐥-𝐘𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐒𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐏𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐚 𝐅𝐥𝐚𝐭 𝐅𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫
Donnelly pointed to "strong earnings drivers across our portfolio" and an improved fourth-quarter booking pace as reasons for raising the full-year outlook. Yet the company's own full-year numbers still build in a fourth-quarter profit slowdown, repeating the pattern from three months ago when a strong second quarter was paired with a flat second-half plan.

By our math, subtracting nine-month results from the new full-year midpoint leaves fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA (operating cash profit before interest and taxes) at $71.2 million, down 1.0% from $71.9 million in the fourth quarter of 2025. That happens even though the same plan implies fourth-quarter comparable total revenue per room will grow 5.3%, and even with $0.2 million of new profit from the Rehoboth Beach acquisition. Selling the Courtyard Fifth Avenue hotel in May explains about $1.5 million of the gap, and higher head-office costs explain another piece, but the implied hotel margin still steps down.

What to watch: fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA against the $70.0 million to $75.0 million range implied by the full-year plan. A finish near the midpoint would confirm that rising fourth-quarter property and corporate expenses ate up the 5% revenue gain.

🔴 𝐌𝐢𝐝-𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐝 𝐋𝐞𝐢𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐋𝐚𝐠 𝐖𝐡𝐢𝐥𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐬
While luxury resorts surged, several mid-priced leisure and regional properties lost revenue compared to a year ago, continuing a split between high-end and budget-conscious travelers. At the same time, head-office spending is taking a larger slice of the company's hotel profits.

• Westin Fort Lauderdale Beach Resort total revenue per room: down 10.7% from a year ago
• Hotel Champlain Burlington total revenue per room: down 9.1%
• Margaritaville Beach House Key West total revenue per room: down 3.2%
• Third-quarter corporate expenses: $10.9 million, up 27.5% from a year ago

Twelve of the 34 comparable properties posted lower room revenue per available room than a year ago, showing that demand is uneven beneath the 6.6% headline gain. Meanwhile, DiamondRock raised its full-year cash corporate expense forecast by another $1.0 million to $28.0 million, up from $25.5 million at the start of the year, which reduced the share of hotel profit that reached Adjusted EBITDA.

What to watch: comparable RevPAR at the Florida Keys and Fort Lauderdale properties during the winter peak season in the fourth and first quarters. Continued declines there would show that middle-income leisure demand is still weakening.

🔴 𝐃𝐢𝐚𝐦𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐑𝐨𝐜𝐤 𝐁𝐨𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐚 𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐭 𝐖𝐡𝐢𝐥𝐞 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐈𝐭𝐬 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐈𝐝𝐥𝐞
Earlier this year management set up a $300 million share repurchase program after selling a Manhattan hotel for $33.0 million. Instead of buying back shares in the third quarter, DiamondRock spent $31.0 million on October 1 to buy The Bellmoor Inn & Spa in Rehoboth Beach, Delaware, which Donnelly called "a leading independent resort in a supply-constrained market".

Donnelly said the resort was bought at an "attractive initial yield and offers meaningful upside through the DiamondRock platform". The price equals 10.4 times trailing hotel cash profit and an 8.6% initial net operating income yield, rising to about 9.5% after planned off-season renovations. However, the REIT bought zero shares in the third quarter, leaving $299.4 million of its $300.0 million buyback authorization unused. That confirms management has shifted from buying its own stock at a discount to buying properties in a competitive market.

What to watch: any further hotel purchases or sales announced before year-end. Buying another property without selling one first would reverse management's earlier statement that the company would likely be a net seller of hotels in 2026.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Three standing concerns from last quarter depend on operating details that management discusses on the conference call rather than in the earnings release.

• Advance group bookings for 2027: Donnelly noted a positive fourth-quarter booking pace, but the release gave no figure for the 2027 group book, which was down from a year ago at the last update.
• New York union labor costs: the release did not break out how the Manhattan union contract renewal affected third-quarter property wages or fourth-quarter cost assumptions.
• Brand agreement negotiations: the release confirmed a new Marriott franchise deal for Westin Boston Seaport starting January 2027, but did not quantify the fee savings or update the status of the owners' letter to Marriott.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐒𝐰𝐚𝐩𝐬 𝐑𝐞𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐞𝐝 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐞
DiamondRock carries $1.1 billion of unsecured term loans and nothing drawn on its $400 million credit line. During the quarter, the share of debt locked in at fixed interest rates through swaps rose from 39% to 48%, reducing the company's exposure to interest-rate swings. Its weighted-average interest rate ticked up from 4.9% to 5.1%, while net debt fell to 3.0 times trailing cash profit from 3.1 times in June.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐔𝐧𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐧𝐞𝐭 𝐝𝐞𝐛𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟒𝟎.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 / $𝟗𝟔𝟎.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐧𝐞𝐭 𝐝𝐞𝐛𝐭  ⇘ decelerating
Net debt (total debt minus unrestricted cash) fell by $71.9 million from the end of 2025 as unrestricted cash more than doubled from $68.1 million to $140.0 million. Strong third-quarter cash flow and May's Manhattan hotel sale built the cash pile before the $31.0 million October resort purchase.

𝐃𝐮𝐞 𝐟𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐡𝐨𝐭𝐞𝐥 𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐫𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟖𝟓.𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Balances owed to DiamondRock by the third-party operators that run its hotels rose 34.6% from $137.8 million at the end of 2025, far outpacing the 3.3% rise in nine-month revenue. The buildup reflects seasonal summer working capital held at property accounts.

𝐃𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐭𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟐𝟎𝟖.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇒ stable
Diluted share and operating partnership unit count rose 0.3% from 207.4 million a year ago and ticked up from 206.1 million in the second quarter. With the buyback paused since spring, stock-based compensation slightly increased the share count, though the full-year outlook still assumes 207.5 million average shares.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐏𝐀𝐑 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡: 𝟒.𝟕𝟓%–𝟓.𝟐𝟓%  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from 2.5%–4.0%
Raised. The middle of the range moved up 1.75 percentage points to 5.0% growth. By our math, that leaves about 3.9% growth for the fourth quarter against an easy comparison (-0.3% a year ago). This is the third raise this year, and the largest yet: +0.5 points, +0.75 points, and +1.75 points.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐏𝐀𝐑 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡: 𝟒.𝟕𝟓%–𝟓.𝟐𝟓%  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from 2.75%–4.25%
Raised. The middle of the range rose 1.5 percentage points to 5.0%, matching the room revenue growth target. By our math, the full-year plan implies about 5.3% growth in the fourth quarter, down from 6.5% in the third quarter, supported by food, beverage and resort fees.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀: $𝟑𝟐𝟐.𝟎–𝟑𝟐𝟕.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $310.0–320.0 million
Raised. The middle of the range moved up $9.5 million to $324.5 million, or 9.0% growth for the year by our math, including $0.2 million from the Bellmoor purchase. That leaves $71.2 million for the fourth quarter, down 1.0% from a year ago. It is the third raise this year: +$1.7M (after a hotel sale), +$18.8M, and +$9.5M.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐅𝐅𝐎: $𝟐𝟓𝟔.𝟓–𝟐𝟔𝟏.𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $245.5–255.5 million
Raised. The middle of the range rose $8.5 million to $259.0 million, up 14.1% from 2025 by our math, aided by lower interest costs and last December's preferred stock payoff. By our math, that leaves $55.0 million for the fourth quarter, down 1.5% from a year ago.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐅𝐅𝐎 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞: $𝟏.𝟐𝟒–𝟏.𝟐𝟔  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $1.18–1.23
Raised. The middle of the range increased $0.045 to $1.25 per share, or 15.7% growth from $1.08 in 2025 by our math. After $0.98 in the first nine months, the plan leaves $0.27 for the fourth quarter, unchanged from $0.27 a year ago. This is the third raise this year: +$0.005, +$0.075, and +$0.045.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡-𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐢𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐲 𝐧𝐨 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡?
By our math, the full-year outlook implies fourth-quarter comparable total revenue per room will rise 5.3%, yet implied Adjusted EBITDA falls 1.0% to $71.2 million. How much of that gap is property wage inflation versus conservative budgeting?

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐩 𝐛𝐨𝐨𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐞 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐧𝐨𝐰?
Last quarter management said the early 2027 group book was down from a year ago and volatile. With the release citing a constructive 2027 backdrop, has 2027 group revenue on the books turned positive?

𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐃𝐢𝐚𝐦𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐑𝐨𝐜𝐤 𝐬𝐞𝐥𝐥 𝐚𝐧𝐨𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐡𝐨𝐭𝐞𝐥 𝐭𝐨 𝐟𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐁𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐦𝐨𝐨𝐫?
Management previously expected to be a net seller of hotels in 2026. Buying The Bellmoor for $31.0 million nearly matches May's $33.0 million Manhattan sale. Are more property sales underway before year-end?

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐝𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐝?
Full-year cash corporate expenses were raised another $1.0 million to $28.0 million, up from $25.0–26.0 million at the start of the year. Is the increase entirely performance bonus accruals, or has permanent headcount cost risen?

text:
🇺🇸 $CURLF Curaleaf @Curaleaf_Inc

🤑 Q3 Earnings Report 
• Revenue: $352.7M 
• Gross Margin: 48.3% 

🔥-take: Curaleaf is successfully grinding out top-line growth and operational scale in a still-pressured cannabis market—record revenue, third consecutive quarter of domestic YoY growth, and international as a clear bright spot—but the “robust profitability” claim is mostly non-GAAP, with margin compression, a GAAP net loss this quarter, thin cash relative to ~$637 million in debt, and a high-profile hostile bid for Aurora that just got blocked by a superior friendly Organigram deal. This is solid execution on the “growth” half of the Built for Growth plan, not yet a clean profitability inflection or strategic breakout.

🤖 ANALYSIS:

Key Financial Results (Q3 2026 ended Sept. 30)
- **Net revenue**: $352.7 million, +10.9% YoY (from $317.9M) and +3.6% sequentially (from $340.1M in Q2). Management called it a record.
- **Segments**: Domestic ~$294 million (+8% YoY); International $58.7 million (~$59M, +28% YoY). Domestic retail was roughly flat sequentially at ~$225M while wholesale grew; international saw strength in both retail and wholesale.
- **Margins**: Gross profit $170.5M (48.3% margin, –220 bps YoY). Adjusted gross profit $171.8M (48.7% margin, –186 bps YoY). Adjusted EBITDA $77.6M (22.0% margin, –56 bps YoY). Headline numbers look healthy by cannabis standards; the direction is modest compression.
- **Bottom line**: Net loss from continuing operations of $37.4 million ($0.14/share). This contrasts with Q2’s net income of ~$12.5M and nine-month net income of $45.2M ($0.17/share). Nine-month revenue reached $1,017M (+9% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA of $211.1M (20.8% margin).
- **Balance sheet & cash**: $104.9M cash; outstanding debt $636.9M (net of discounts/fees). Operating cash flow from continuing operations was $22M in the quarter (timing differences expected to reverse). Full-year operating cash flow target remains ~$150M. Small buybacks continued (105k shares for $1M in the quarter; 1.12M shares for $8.4M year-to-date).

CEO Boris Jordan framed the results as evidence the strategy is working amid consumer pressure, with resilient demand and momentum in both U.S. and international businesses. Adjusted EBITDA margin of 22% is respectable in the sector, but the YoY decline and GAAP loss underscore that “profitability” still requires non-GAAP adjustments and is not yet broad-based or expanding.

Operational Highlights

Curaleaf continued selective retail expansion and optimization: Florida footprint to 78 (later 80 post-quarter), nationwide operated/managed dispensaries to ~188–191, plus relocations to better sites. Index inclusions (FTSE Canada All Cap after an earlier TSX addition), first standardized cannabis registrations in Spain, and early DEA registrations for medical dispensaries were noted. Capex for the nine months was $50M, focused on upgrades, automation, and selective retail.

International remains the higher-growth lever (Europe/medical-oriented), while the U.S. business has stabilized into consistent (if moderate) YoY growth after earlier pressure.

Strategic Context: The Aurora Bid and Broader Landscape

The press release notes the commencement and later enhancement of the original offer for Aurora Cannabis (cash + Curaleaf shares, most recently around a $5 implied value). On the same day as these earnings, Organigram announced a friendly deal to acquire Aurora at C$7.80 per share (valuing it at ~C$561M), a premium to Curaleaf’s hostile bid that Aurora’s board had rejected. Curaleaf said it is evaluating the alternative and its options. This looks like a setback for the M&A ambition; a higher competing bid would be costly given the balance sheet.

Broader industry backdrop: Partial federal progress on medical cannabis (Schedule III move for qualifying state-licensed medical activity earlier in 2026, with DEA beginning to issue registrations and some protections, though with limitations especially around dual-use states). Broader adult-use rescheduling remains stalled or delayed. Price compression, elevated interest rates, consumer pressure, and the lingering effects of 280E (partially mitigated for pure medical operators) continue to weigh on the sector. Consolidation is active, which is why Aurora was a target.

Assessment

**Positives**: Consistent top-line growth (domestic recovery + strong international), scale in retail, solid adjusted margins by industry standards, cash flow trajectory still pointed higher, and early regulatory tailwinds on the medical side. The stock had already been moving higher into the print (CURLF around the $10 area, up ~10% on the day amid the Organigram news and earnings anticipation).

**Watch items / risks**: Margin compression, GAAP losses amid non-GAAP strength, leverage (~$637M debt vs. $105M cash and ~$280M annualized adjusted EBITDA run-rate), limited free cash after growth investments, and the apparent failure of the Aurora bid without a clear next strategic move. International supply and competitive dynamics can still introduce volatility. Full-year cash flow delivery and any guidance on the earnings call (scheduled for 5 p.m. ET) will matter more than the headline “record revenue.”

Overall, this is a respectable operating quarter for a large multi-state operator in a tough environment—evidence of execution and resilience rather than a transformative inflection. The story remains one of gradual improvement, international optionality, and waiting for clearer federal catalysts or better cash conversion, rather than pure profitability leadership.

🗣️ MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY:
Boris Jordan @Boris_Jordan Chairman and CEO:
"We are building the global leader in cannabis, and our third-quarter results provide further evidence that our strategy is delivering. Solid execution across the business is driving growth, strengthening our competitive position, and advancing our Built for Growth plan.  Against a backdrop of increasing pressure on the consumer, cannabis demand remained resilient and our business delivered strong, broad-based growth."

"Record third quarter revenue of $353 million grew 11% compared to last year, bolstered by both our domestic and international segments that grew 8% and 28%, respectively. Our U.S. business has sustained the momentum experienced in the first half of the year as this was our third consecutive quarter of domestic year-over-year growth. Adjusted gross margin was 49% and adjusted EBITDA was $78 million, representing a 22% margin. We ended the quarter with $105 million in cash on the balance sheet. Cash flow from continuing operations in the quarter was $22 million, due to timing differences that will reverse next quarter.  We continue to target generating approximately $150 million in operating cash flow for the year."

"These results reflect the disciplined execution of our entire team and reinforce the strength of our global platform. We are translating operational improvements into stronger financial performance, building momentum across the business, and positioning Curaleaf for sustained growth and greater cash generation."

text:
Anita Maria Cetina was the nanny to four-year-old Emma Robinson and her two-year-old brother Charlie. But to the family who knew and loved her, she was so much more.

Anita was among nine people who tragically lost their lives when a Learjet 60 travelling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas crashed in Florida on November 1.

She was travelling alongside the children she cared for, their parents, Adam Robinson and Helen Sharp, two family friends and the aircraft's two pilots.

In a deeply moving statement following the tragedy, the families paid tribute to the special place Anita held in their lives.

“Anita Maria cared for Emma and Charlie with tenderness and devotion, and she was truly part of the family.”

They also remembered the love she had given the children, describing it as a legacy of unconditional love and devotion.

While much of the attention surrounding the tragedy has focused on the Robinson family, their words offer a glimpse of another deeply cherished life lost.

Anita was not simply someone who looked after Emma and Charlie. She was someone their family considered one of their own.

Our thoughts are with Anita's loved ones and everyone mourning the nine lives lost.

May she rest in peace.

#AnitaMariaCetina #FloridaPlaneCrash #RestInPeace

text:
Months before Adam Robinson and his young family tragically lost their lives in a Florida plane crash, the 45-year-old technology entrepreneur shared a heartfelt reflection on something he valued more than professional success: time with the people he loved.

In April, Adam wrote about his experiences working on Wall Street, where he had watched colleagues spend 70, 80 and even 90 hours a week at work, believing they were doing it for their families.

But he had come to see things differently.

“All their families actually wanted was their presence,” he wrote.

Adam explained that he had made a conscious decision not to follow the same path. He would close his laptop at the end of the working day, leave work behind and sometimes finish as early as 3pm to spend more time at home.

“My family life gives me energy for my work. My work gives me energy for my family life,” he wrote.

On November 1, Adam, his wife Helen Sharp and their two children, four-year-old Emma and two-year-old Charlie, were among nine people who lost their lives when their Learjet 60 crashed in Florida.

His words, shared months before the tragedy, have since touched people around the world.

They offer a moving glimpse of a father and husband who understood that the most precious thing he could give his family was his time.

Our thoughts are with the loved ones of Adam, Helen, Emma, Charlie and everyone who lost their lives.

May they all rest in peace.

text:
Voted NO on Amendment 6. Here's why:

1.  It makes mistakes hard to fix. If a voter-passed measure turns out to be flawed, our legislature would need 80% of both the House and Senate just to put a correction back on the ballot. Almost nothing clears that bar.

2. It's lopsided. A simple majority can pass a measure, but it takes a legislative supermajority to even offer a fix.

3. It handcuffs lawmakers. Even when a measure is badly written or has consequences nobody saw coming, the legislature's hands are tied.

4. It gives courts more power. Judges could rewrite ballot language through lawsuits. I'd rather not hand that to the courts.

5. It protects whoever has the most money. Out-of-state donors can already pour money into a Missouri campaign and pass something with 50% plus one. Yes, Missourians could undo a measure with another initiative. But that means a costly petition drive, and the people with the most money will have the biggest advantage. Money from people who don't live here shouldn't be able to write our state constitution, then make it very hard to fix.

6. It's hard to undo. Once it's in the constitution, getting it out takes another statewide campaign.

I love the initiative process, and I respect neighbors who see this differently. I just think this goes too far. Please pray, think it through, and vote.

text:
I read the Brad's recall twice, because the contaminant was not a germ or an allergen. It was thallium.

The backstory starts in January 2026, when California health officials looked into one person with elevated thallium levels, then tested Brad's products bought at Sacramento stores and found elevated levels in several varieties. On May 19, California warned people not to eat those products.

Months later, Snack Right Super Foods, the company behind Brad's Raw Chips, recalled certain 2 ounce Crunchy Kale bags and 3 ounce Veggie Chips Kale bags. The announcement is dated November 2, 2026, and the FDA posted it November 3. Roughly 25,000 bags moved nationwide in October, November, and December 2025.

The notice gives the mechanism in plain terms: kale absorbs elements from soil, and drying strips out 85 to 90 percent of the water, so the remaining elements concentrate. It also says manufacturing did not put the metal there.

For a shopper, the usable detail is the lot and Best By date. Original Crunchy Kale, UPC 813104021679, lots 33525-1, 33525-2, and 33525-3, carry a February 1, 2027 Best By date in the notice. A matching bag goes in the trash, per the notice, with no refund offered.

First, the energy in the mid-levels of the atmosphere at 3 AM: a big low pressure system out in the Plains, with high pressure parked off the Southeast coast.

Next, the set up at 1 PM: a trough digging across the middle of the country and a big ridge of high pressure dominating the eastern seaboard. That's our next storm system out west, and it's also why we stay so warm out ahead of it.

The last swipe is the southerly flow, helping temperatures run 15° to 25° above normal, with record highs possible across the Ohio Valley today. Most of that heat stays north of us, but we're still well above average.

text:
Al-Malik al-Kamil Nasir ad-Din Muhammad (Arabic: الملك الكامل ناصر الدين محمد; c. 1177 – 6 March 1238), titled Abu al-Maʽali (Arabic: أبي المعالي), was an Egyptian ruler and the fourth Ayyubid sultan of Egypt. During his tenure as sultan, the Ayyubids defeated the Fifth Crusade. He was known to the Latin/Frankish crusaders as Meledin, a name by which he is usually referred to in older Western sources and often but less frequently continues to be. As a result of the Sixth Crusade, he ceded West Jerusalem to the Christians and is known to have met with Saint FRANCIS.[2][3]

Biography
Jazira campaign
Al-Kamil was the son of the Kurdish sultan al-Adil ("Saphadin"), a brother of Saladin. Al-Kamil's father was laying siege to the city of Mardin (in modern-day Turkey) in 1199 when he was called away urgently to deal with a security threat in Damascus. Al-Adil left al-Kamil to command the forces around Mardin continuing the siege.[4] Taking advantage of the Sultan's absence, the combined forces of Mosul, Sinjar and Jazirat ibn Umar appeared at Mardin when it was on the point of surrender, and drew Al-Kamil into battle. Although he was badly defeated and retreated to Mayyafariqin,[5] dissent and weakness among his opponents meant that Al-Kamil was able to secure Ayyubid rule in the Jazira Region by taking Harran (in modern-day Turkey).[6][7]

Viceroy of Egypt
In 1200, after proclaiming himself Sultan, Al-Adil invited Al-Kamil to come from the Eastern Territories to join him in Egypt as his viceroy (na'ib) in that country. Al-Adil's second son, Al-Mu'azzam Isa, had already been made prince of Damascus in 1198.[8] It appears that Al-Adil allowed Al-Kamil a fairly high degree of authority, since he oversaw much of the work on the Cairo Citadel, issued decrees in his own name, and even managed to persuade his father to dismiss the powerful minister Ibn Shukr.[9] Al-Kamil remained viceroy until his father's death in 1218 when he became Sultan himself.

The Fifth Crusade
Main article: Fifth Crusade
When Al-Adil died on 31 August 1218,[10] the Ayyubid domains were divided into three parts, with Al-Kamil ruling Egypt, his brother Al-Muazzam Isa ruling in Palestine and Transjordan, and a third brother, Al-Ashraf Musa in Syria and the Jazira. Nominally the other two recognised Al-Kamil's supremacy as Sultan. Unusually for an Ayyubid succession, there was no obvious dissent or rivalry between the brothers at this point, partly because just before Al-Adil's death, Egypt had been attacked by the forces of the Fifth Crusade.[11]

Al-Kamil took command of the forces which defended Damietta against the Crusaders. In 1219 he was almost overthrown by a conspiracy led by the amir Imad ad-Din ibn al-Mashtub, commander of the Hakkari Kurdish regiment, to replace him with his younger and more pliant brother al-Faiz Ibrahim. Alerted to the conspiracy, Al-Kamil had to flee the camp to safety and in the ensuing confusion the Crusaders were able to tighten their grip on Damietta. Al-Kamil considered fleeing to Yemen, which was ruled by his son al-Mas'ud Yusuf, but the timely arrival of his brother Al-Muazzam from Syria with reinforcements brought the conspiracy to a swift end.[12]

Al-Kamil made many offers of peace to the Crusaders, all of which were rejected, due to the influence of the papal legate Pelagius. He offered to return Jerusalem and rebuild its walls (which his brother had torn down earlier in the year), and to return the True Cross (which he probably did not have). At one point he even met with Francis of Assisi, who had accompanied the crusade.[13] Their meeting became a subject for painters like Giotto, Taddeo di Bartolo and Taddeo Gaddi.[13]

Due to famine and disease after the Nile failed to flood, al-Kamil could not defend Damietta and it was captured in November 1219.[14] The sultan withdrew to al-Mansourah, a fortress further up the Nile. After this there was little action until 1221, when al-Kamil offered peace again, proposing to surrender the entire territory of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, except Transjordan, in return for the Crusaders evacuating Egypt[14] but was again refused. The Crusaders marched out towards Cairo, but al-Kamil simply opened the dams and allowed the Nile to flood, and finally the Crusaders accepted an eight-year peace. He retook Damietta in September.

Power struggle and the treaty of 1229
In the following years there was a power struggle with his brother al-Mu'azzam, and al-Kamil was willing to accept a peace with emperor and King of Sicily Frederick II, who was planning the Sixth Crusade. Al-Mu'azzam died in 1227, eliminating the need for a peace, but Frederick had already arrived in Palestine. After al-Mu'azzam's death, al-Kamil and his other brother al-Ashraf negotiated a treaty, giving all of Palestine (including Transjordan) to al-Kamil and Syria to al-Ashraf. In February 1229 al-Kamil negotiated the Treaty of Jaffa, a ten-year peace with Frederick II and returned Jerusalem and other holy sites to the Crusader kingdom.[15]

The treaty of 1229 is unique in the history of the Crusades. By diplomacy alone and without major military confrontation, Jerusalem, Bethlehem, and a corridor running to the sea were ceded to the kingdom of Jerusalem. Exception was made for the Temple area, the Dome of the Rock, and the Aqsa Mosque, which the Muslims retained. Moreover, all current Muslim residents of the city would retain their homes and property. They would also have their own city officials to administer a separate justice system and safeguard their religious interests. The walls of Jerusalem, which had been destroyed, were rebuilt, and the peace was to last for 10 years.[16]

After the treaty with Frederick, al-Kamil turned his attention to Damascus. He sent al-Ashraf to begin operations against the city. He arrived to pen the siege of Damascus on 6 May. After almost two months of intense fighting, the city surrendered on 25 June. It was given to al-Ashraf, while al-Muazzam's son, an-Nasir Dawud, had to settle for Transjordan.[17]

Later years
Although there was peace with the Crusaders, al-Kamil had to contend with the Seljuks and the Khwarezmians before he died in 1238.

His sons as-Salih Ayyub and al-Adil II succeeded him in Syria and Egypt respectively, but the Ayyubid empire soon descended into civil war. In 1239 the treaty with Frederick expired, and Jerusalem came under Ayyubid control.

Personality
Al-Kamil exemplified the Islamic laws of war. Oliver of Paderborn, an eyewitness to the Fifth Crusade, describes the generosity shown by al-Kamil's forces to the defeated Crusaders after their surrender. Gavigan’s 1948 translation of Oliver states: “Who could doubt that such kindness, mildness, and mercy proceeded from God?” and then that those whom the Crusaders had harmed “refreshed us with their own food as we were dying of hunger.” However, van Moolenbroek notes a misreading in Gavigan's translation of this passage of Hoogeweg’s 1894 edition of the Latin text.[18][19][20][21][22][23]

Al-Kamil is mentioned several times in the first chapter of Zofia Kossak's 1944 novel "Blessed Are the Meek."

Quarón

Chapter 8 - Halo City

Once they had left neurospace and regained consciousness in the royal palace, Venus and Alpha began making plans to travel to Halo City. It was a continent sized city holding 10 billion residents and hundreds of millions of shorter term visitors.

Venus owned a penthouse in the city center, near to the main life clinic. She suggested that Alpha and she decamp for Halo City right away, so that they could explore the city’s unique charms while waiting for their children’s life shells to be ready.

Alpha wholeheartedly endorsed the plan. Venus chartered a luxury hover vessel to take them to their destination. The pair traveled light with only the clothing on their backs and Alpha’s enhanced bottle of Trident gin. Halo City would provide the rest.

“I wonder,” Venus mused as they entered the hover vessel, “what else magic can do? This gin bottle is proof that magic is real. Surely, there are other ways to harness its powers.”

“Yes, it’s possible,” Alpha said, “but remember that we don’t know who made the bottle or placed it there on your private beach for me to find. It’s a complete mystery.”

“I suspect that your father placed it there, or one of the Nalu,” Venus surmised.

“Yes, I suppose your right,” Alpha replied. “I assume that one needs to be an infinite to use magic. I’m just a level 50 immortal, as far as this quest goes.”

“So, the question is, how do you regain your infinite status?” Venus asked.
“And how do we get you elevated to invite status alongside me,” Alpha said. “I din’t think this quest is all about me. It’s also about my family and closest friends.”

“The enchantment of the Heavenly Realms, then,” Venus said.

“Exactly right,” Alpha replied.

Alpha poured two glasses of Trident gin, as the hover vessel accelerated to maximum cruising speed.

“I remember that magic was everywhere in Tépë,” Alpha said. We could fly and teleport. Hover technology wasn’t needed. We had food and drink generators that supplied us with anything we desired. At higher levels, we could create new lands on the edges of our world. It extended into infinity. I is a wondrous place, Venus, and I look forward to taking you there one day.”

“I know you do,” Venus said. “We will get there. Be patient with this. Enjoy the journey. It will make our arrival at the final destination at that more rewarding.”

“This quest is important,” Alpha said. “My father thought I was ready, or he would not have sent me.”

“Reaching immortal level 50 is impressive progress, but the exponential experience growth that you and I both need will happen by playing mortals on Earth,” Venus said. “The new Nalu version is the most immersive ever, according to Gaia. She anticipates experience growth to be a million times normal, as a player approaches total completion of the game. The new module also allows gameplay beyond the year 1975 for the first time. The level of progress that humanity makes in the next hundred years appears to be unprecedented.”

“Then our avatars should be born at the start of the new module,” Alpha said.

“Yes, that’s what I was thinking,” Venus replied. “Once we have our team assembled, we will go about selecting avatars to play. Vic and Xander will need to learn as much as they can about Earth in the interim. I told them this before we departed neurospace, and I trust that they are working on this even as we speak.”

The hover vessel was now at its maximum altitude. Below, large land masses fringed by archipelagoes were visible. As evening approached, the vessel descended to 500 feet and landed at a hoverport, where Venus and Alpha exited for a meal and to spend the night. As they transited the hoverport, Venus frequently was spotted by fans who waved or called out her name but otherwise kept a respectful distance.

At the restaurant, the paired were offered seating in a VIP lounge with views of a deep blue lake that bordered the hoverport.

After they had ordered, an elegant woman at a side table got up and walked to their table.

“Greetings, Venus,” the woman said.

“Greta, how are you?” Venus responded, smiling.

“House Valhalla is aflame with speculation that you are about to be married. Is it true? Have you finally found your dream man?” Greta asked.

Venus smiled and took a sip of wine. “Greta, meet by fiancé, Alpha Paradise. He is indeed the man of my dreams.”

“Paradise? I don’t know that house,” Greta replied, looking somewhat confused.
“That’s because there isn’t one. Alpha washed ashore on my private island, and we decided to give him the surname, Paradise. Greta, this may surprise you, but Alpha isn’t from the Heavenly Realms. He’s from a different and better dimension. He’s here to find a woman to marry, which he has done, and to help us solve our looming overpopulation problem, which he’s still working on,” Venus explained.

“I take it that you are serious,” Greta said.

“Alpha is the son of Ja-el, our Quarón,” Venus said. “I never doubted him. My parents and family believe it, as well. He has come to us at a moment of need. Once he regains his powers, he will roll back the Great Nothing to reveal a vast array of new continents and islands for us to settle. He will teach us to use magic. And he will establish a connection between our dimension and his own.”

“Then you are a Godsend, Alpha Paradise,” Greta said. “I will not trouble you. Congratulations on your engagement to Venus. She is an incredible woman.”

“I know,” Alpha replied. “Thank you, madam. We are very happy to be engaged. You must come to the wedding.”

“I wouldn’t miss it,” Greta said, before returned to her table. “May I share what I have learned here?”

“Absolutely,” Alpha said, as Venus nodded in affirmation.

“Greta is the queen of Valhalla and the mother of Thor and Freya,” Venus explained. “She is highly placed in the Temple of the Gods. She will spread the word about you very rapidly. And my mother just mind texted me. The wedding invitations will go out tonight at midnight. Things will move quickly from here.”

Alpha nodded. “We have eight more stops before Halo City,” he said. “What do we do when we get noticed?”

“What do we do?” Venus said, surprised. “My dear, we soak it all in. You haven’t experienced fame before. Well, you will now. Be gentle and generous, and be kind to everyone you meet. We are creating the basis here for a legend that will be told about us for the next trillion years. It all starts now, Alpha.”

“How soon after the wedding will Gaia announce our names as the first players of the new version of Earth?” Alpha asked.

“How long would you like?” Venus asked.

“8 weeks on your private island, simply alone with you at first and then with our team as we prepare for the game,” Alpha said.

“Done,” Venus replied, smiling.

The next morning, after a coffee stop in the hoverport, Venus and Alpha returned to their traveling vessel for the next leg of the journey to Halo City. At every stop, both Venus and Alpha were recognized.

“Are you really the son of Ja-el?” Alpha was often asked.

“I believe so,” he responded. “I am here on a quest to rescue the Heavenly Realms from overpopulation. Ja-el sent me as an immortal to understand better your situation. He didn’t send me as an ultra god. I must regain my powers by living here among all of you. That is my reason for being here now. I could use your support. It would mean the world to me.”

At each stop, the crowds began to form sooner, once Venus and Alpha were identified. People applauded as they passed and sometimes knelt down with heads bowed. Venus’ incomparable beauty and Alpha’s strength and charisma made deep impressions, but it was their humility that crowds most remembered and shared on social media. The two patiently posed for pictures at every stop on their journey to Halo City.

Finally, the pair arrived at Venus’ penthouse, which offered commanding views over the city. They made love in the bedroom and then slipped naked into the sauna before a swim in the pool.

An android personal chef prepared salmon and polenta with Pinot Noir. The life clinic mind texted them to set up a time the next morning to meet their children.

“It’s time I returned to social media,” Venus said. Alpha nodded.

“Do it gently,” he said.

“Smile,” Venus said, as she looked intently in Alpha’s direction.

“Perfect,” she said. “Meet my future husband: Alpha Paradise. Alpha isn’t from our world, by which I mean the Heavenly Realms. He is Ja-el’s son, which makes him an ultra god from another dimension to our own. He came here on a noble mission to help us expand the realms into new and wonderful spaces. And he came to meet and marry me. I love him deeply. Details on the wedding to come.”

“Merlin, send that to my followers,” Venus said.

“Consider it done,” Merlin replied.

“Then we’re ready to go tomorrow,” Alpha said.

“Perfectly ready,” Venus answered, smiling. “We have 30 days before Victoria and Alexander are tethered to their life shells. It’s time for us to be seen in the city.”

“But we’re famous,” Alpha protested. “How can we appear in public again?”

“Alpha, fame need not be a hindrance,” Venus said. “It is something to be treasured. Do you know what draws so many people to us? It’s because we are so superior to them. We are more beautiful, more intelligent, and more accomplished than they. We are from top families. Alpha, you’re the son of Ja-el, for goodness sake. People want to see us in person. That’s all. I am not ashamed of my beauty or my wit. Neither should you. Be modest in your dealings with people. Never judge them. But you and I are nobility. Never forget that.”

“I won’t,” Alpha promised.

The next morning, the pair took the tower’s main elevator to the ground floor coffee shop for cappuccinos and croissants. The shop’s patrons all took notice of their appearance, but they left the two in peace at their table.

“They are so polite,” Alpha remarked, as he sipped his coffee.

“They understand that we have lives of our own, and they respect that,” Venus said. “They will watch us, of course, and tell others that they saw us, but those are healthy expressions of encountering celebrities. Be polite and be yourself. You are so charming, you know.”

“V, my memory still has a lot of blank spots. I don’t remember much of my life in Tépë,” Alpha said seriously. “I can’t very well answer questions about my past.”

“Then we will create new memories until your past returns to you,” Venus said, smiling.
“Agreed,” Alpha replied.

The pair left the coffee shop and walked along the green lined sidewalks of the downtown to a luxury shopping district, where they purchased designer hoodies. They returned to the street and walked to the city’s central park, which was surrounded on all four sides by tall buildings that soared several thousand feet skyward.

Venus and Alpha walked to the park’s beer garden, which was filled with happy looking patrons listening to live music and enjoying themselves.

“May we sit next you?” Venus asked an attractive women sitting alone at a bench with a beer and pretzels.

“Are you who I think you are?” The woman asked.

“Possibly,” Venus said.

“By all means,” the woman said. “I’m Sandra.”

“Venus,” Venus said. “This is my fiancé, Alpha.”

“No way,” Sandra said, looking surprised.

“We’re in town to pick up our two children from the life clinic,” Venus said. “We have some time to wait, so we headed here. I’ve heard it has the best beer in the city.”

“Oh, they do,” Sandra said, regaining her composure. “The grill is outstanding, too, as is the brick oven pizza. I reserved this table months ago, but the friends I invited haven’t arrived yet. You’re welcome to join us.”

“We will. Thank you,” Venus said.

Sandra looked at Alpha shyly.
“You’re the most beautiful man I’ve ever seen,” she said quietly.

“Thank you,” Alpha said, taking a sip of beer. “My parents designed me this way. It makes me a good pairing with Venus, whose beauty is beyond comparison.”

“Yes, you are a magnificent couple,” Sandra said. “You are true royalty. And are you really the Quarón’s son, Alpha? Excuse me for being so bold in my questions.”

“Not a problem,” Alpha said. “Yes, Ja-el is my father. He sent me here on a mission, which is going well so far. The exact details are private, of course, but the very best interests of the Heavenly Realms are involved.”

“If you follow me on social media, you’ll get updates on our progress,” Venus offered.

“Yes, I do,” Sandra replied. “It’s amazing that you are picking up two children soon. Child credits are so rare these days. It’s all so crowded here already. Not that I am complaining about Halo City. This place is amazing.”

“Hopefully we will fix the overcrowding issue in the near future,” Venus said. “It’s part of our mission. It will all be revealed in time.”

Alpha and Venus stayed for an extra beer and pizza, declaring it among the best that they had had. They parted ways from Sandra and exited the beer garden onto the park grounds. The grass was lush and carpet like, and the trees were full of fresh spring leaves.

The pair next walked across the park to a wine bar that Venus knew from previous visits. It was full, but the staff ushered them into a VIP seating area instead.

They took seats at the bar, next to a strikingly looking man whom Venus identified to Alpha as Gabriel Titan. Gabriel greeted Venus warmly and shook hands with Alpha.

“I’ve heard you two were in Halo City,” Gabriel said, as his finished his cocktail. “Alpha, it’s my honor to meet you. Consider me a believer. You are Ja-el’s son.”

“You got that from scanning me across the room, when we entered,” Alpha said, smiling.

“Guilty as charged. I thought that Pathfinder was a myth. I was wrong,” Gabriel answered. “Congratulations on the wedding. I will be attending. Your invitation arrived this morning. Thank you.”

“May I share a profile with you?” Venus asked.

“By all means,” Gabriel said.

Venus checked her eyescreen. “Shall I share her specs as well?”

“She’s phenomenally pretty,” Gabriel said. “And she’s smart, too. I’m intrigued. Who is she?”

“She will be our daughter in about 3 weeks. She’s in neurospace now,” Venus said.

“I see,” said Gabriel. “May I run a compatibility check?”

“Yes, you may,” Venus said, as the bartender brought three cocktails to the group.

“Remarkable. 99.5,” Gabriel said with astonishment. “And she’s your daughter, you say. And a level 1 eternal. Venus, how is that possible?”

“Alpha’s genetic code combined with mine,” Venus said. “We have a daughter - Victoria - and a son named Alexander. You’ll welcome to meet them both at the life clinic for their inception day. They are twins. And both do have Pathfinder, but we don’t know yet how it will manifest in them.”

“I would love to join you,” Gabriel said. “And if you want someone to show Victoria around Halo City - including the palaces - then you’ve got your man.”

“Consider it a deal,” Venus said, taking a sip of her cocktail.

“Alpha, you have me confused,” Gabriel said. “Your profile lists you as a level 25 immortal, but your specs clearly indicate otherwise. Your attribute grid is off the charts. What exactly are you?”

“I’m a level 10 infinite, which is an advanced form of life beyond that of eternals like you and Venus,” Alpha said. “I’m Ja-el’s son, which makes me an ultra god, or a super god, if you prefer. When I agreed to come to the Heavenly Realms on a rescue mission, my father demoted me to a level 1 immortal, because he wanted me to experience life from that perspective. That’s what I’ve been doing. I accumulate experience points at an accelerated rate, because of Pathfinder. So will Vic and Xander. They are part eternal and part infinite. There is nothing else like them.”

“Now you’ve made me even more curious to meet your children,” Gabriel said. “If Vic is a level 1 eternal, she can give her consent, you realize. It is no secret that I am Halo City’s most eligible bachelor. Someone like her who is a near perfect match will attract my attention. Are you two fine with that?”

“We were hoping you might take an interest in Vic,” Venus said, smiling. “She knows that I’ve been matchmaking, and she’s fine with it. So, let’s see how it goes.”
“Agreed,” Gabriel said.

“We also have a related request of you,” Venus said.

“I’m listening,” Gabriel said, sipping his cocktail.

“What’s the single best way to gain experience rapidly in the Heavenly Realms?” Venus asked.

“Easy. Play Earth. Play it to win, I mean. 90% or more game completion, which is where things get really interesting. Why? Are you going to play the game?” Gabriel asked.

“Have you heard about the improvements yet?” Venus asked.

“Gaia and the Earth design team have been upgrading the game space to make it even more realistic,” Gabriel said. “And they are releasing a new module that goes beyond 1975 in Earth game time. It sounds like a tremendous improvement. Zero transparency is said to be even harder to escape than before. Game play is halted until the new version is unveiled. Are you two really interested in playing?”

text:
Do any universities offer income share agreements?

Thought for 32s
Yes. Some universities offer (or have offered) income share agreements (ISAs) as an alternative or supplement to traditional student loans, though they are not widespread and several prominent programs have paused or ended.⁠Wikipedia

What is an ISA?
An ISA provides funding for education in exchange for a percentage of the student’s future income for a set period (often several years), typically only after earnings exceed a minimum threshold (e.g., $20,000–$50,000). There is usually a payment cap (often 1.5–2.5× the amount received). Payments adjust with income, providing more downside protection than fixed loans if earnings are low. They are often used for gap funding after federal aid is exhausted rather than covering full tuition.⁠Wikipedia

Examples of Universities That Have Offered ISAs
Notable ones include:

Purdue University (“Back a Boiler”): One of the largest and earliest major university programs (launched 2016). It provided supplemental funding (often $5,000–$10,000 range depending on major and year) to sophomores through seniors. New applications were paused in 2022 after a servicer change; existing contracts continue to be serviced. It issued over 1,600 contracts totaling roughly $18 million.⁠Purdue
University of Utah (“Invest in U”): Targeted students close to graduation to help with completion. Offered $3,000–$10,000. It was suspended in 2022 and later discontinued after limited uptake.⁠Unesco
Clarkson University (Lewis Income Share Agreement / LISA): Limited program (roughly 20–25 students per year) offering up to $10,000 annually. Leadership has continued to discuss and support the model in recent years.⁠Highereddive
Other institutions: Lackawanna College, Robert Morris University (Colonial Success Fund), Colorado Mountain College (including targeted funds for DACA/immigrant students and nursing), Messiah College/University, and Jessup University (smaller amounts documented into 2024). Northeastern University has also been referenced in connection with its accelerated online nursing program.⁠Wikipedia
HBCUs and Minority-Serving Institutions: The Student Freedom Initiative offers Student Freedom Loan Agreements (income-contingent funding with similar features) primarily to STEM juniors and seniors at participating schools (e.g., Morehouse, Hampton, and others). This remains active.⁠Studentfreedominitiative
Wikipedia and research reports (including from RAND) document that dozens of colleges and universities have offered ISAs at various points, though many paused around 2022 amid regulatory uncertainty, servicer exits, administrative complexity, and relatively low student demand.⁠Wikipedia

ISAs are far more common at coding bootcamps and short-term vocational/skills programs (e.g., App Academy, BloomTech/formerly Lambda School, General Assembly) than at traditional degree-granting universities.

Availability changes, so check directly with a school’s financial aid office for current options, eligibility, and terms. ISAs differ from federal income-driven repayment plans on traditional loans.

text:
So, you also own an analytics consultancy & work with people across ABC, ESPN, CBS, the SEC, Big 12, and athletics departments across the P4 landscape with direct access to the TV valuation decision points & process?

I didn't say Clemson wasn't valuable, I said they're going to have a hard time gaining entry to the SEC or Big Ten.  It's simply math.  By 2030, when the ACC's exit fee drops to a reasonable amount, the average payout per team will be in the $80M - $90M range.  That means *ANY* team added to either conference will have to increase the conference's TV payout by at least $90M per year.  Otherwise, the average payout per team will decrease.

Clemson has several significant problems.  First, they have a small, regional fan base.  They do not have a strong, national following.  So, when they aren't good, their TV viewership is really poor.  And, we can see that clearly in the data.  Take Clemson vs VA Tech game at 7 PM on ESPN for instance.  Look at the viewership for every Sat @ 7 PM game on ESPN this season:

3.55M (Wk 7) - Florida St vs Miami
2.93M (Wk 4) - Alabama vs S. Carolina
2.43M (Wk 5) - VA Tech vs Pitt
2.22M (Wk 6) - LSU vs Kentucky
2.05M (Wk 3) - Florida vs Auburn
1.80M (Wk 2) - Tennessee vs GA Tech
1.57M (Wk 1) - Texas A&M vs MO State
1.51M (Wk 8) - Clemson vs VA Tech

The Clemson game was the least watched game of the season in that time slot.  And, their competition as Texas vs Ole Miss (which kicked off 30 min after Clemson/VT) and USC vs Wisconsin.  Neither were elite matchups (and I say this as a Texas grad).  It was the same story when they played at 7:30 PM on ABC in Week 5.

13.99M (Wk 2) - Texas vs Ohio St
12.24M (Wk 6) - Georgia vs Alabama
10.90M (Wk 3) - LSU vs Ole Miss
9.16M (Wk 7) - Notre Dame vs BYU
8.09M (Wk 8) - Texas vs Ole Miss
5.71M (Wk 4) - LSU vs Texas A&M
4.63M (Wk 5) - Clemson vs Miami

Again, they were the least watched game of the season in their time slot.

Clemson is a valuable brand to the ACC, but they aren't a big brand on the national landscape.  They aren't going to be able to clear a $90M/yr valuation.

The other issue they have is when a team moves to a conference outside their geography, they lose cross-pollination.  Cross-pollination is when fans of other teams in the conference watch your team b/c they have some sort of connection, whether it's a best friend, a dad, a brother, or they're simply hate-watching.  That's super valuable to networks.  It's one of the reasons USC & Oregon have both suffered in viewership since the move, b/c despite being big name brands, B1G fans in OH, PA, MI, etc have no emotional connection to USC or Oregon.  It's also why the SEC's addition of Texas has been such a boon, b/c there are a TON of Texas grads across the SEC's geography *AND* a ton of SEC grads in TX.  

Clemson has that cross-pollination with the SEC, but not the Big Ten.  That makes it even harder for Clemson to get into the Big Ten.  So really, their only hope is the SEC.  But, does the SEC want a 2nd team in SC, whose budget will rank around the middle of the conference, and who's viewership is poor when they aren't elite?  Knowing what I know from behind-closed-doors conversations, the answer is almost certainly "no."

If you've made it this far, then you can tell my knowledge base comes from the inside.  I'm not a rando spewing nonsense.

All of the above is why my personal hope is that the ACC gets proactive, trims some of its deadweight, and is able to stay together long enough to see offers from ESPN on their next contract, b/c it's bad for almost every ACC team if the conference implodes.  Very few legitimately have a landing spot.

text:
Reuters: A consortium led by US billionaire Todd Boehly is preparing a ​securities swap to acquire sanctioned Russian oil major Lukoil's international assets and a deal is expected within weeks, four people ‌close to the sales process said. A bank acting on behalf of the consortium has purchased billions of dollars of frozen Lukoil securities from Western investment funds to exchange for the company's foreign assets, three of the people said.

The people declined to be identified because they are not authorised to discuss the matter publicly.

If completed, the transaction would conclude ​a sale process that has dragged on for more than a year and initially valued the portfolio involved at $22 billion. Lukoil's foreign ​assets include oilfields, refineries and petrol stations in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

The value of the portfolio has ⁠deteriorated as some assets have stopped operating, two people said.

A deal would also test whether Western sanctions can compel a major Russian company to divest ​international assets while keeping strategic oil operations and limiting financial gains to Moscow.

The consortium includes Boehly, a Miami-based businessman who owns stakes in Los Angeles ​sports teams the Dodgers and the Lakers, and Emirati investors International Holding Company (IHC) and Al Hail Holding. The Syrian-Qatari Al-Khayat brothers and the US International Development Finance Corp (DFC) are also backing the bid.

Representatives of Boehly did not respond to multiple requests for comment. An IHC spokesperson said they do not comment on potential investment activities. Al Hail, the ​Al-Khayats and the US DFC did not respond to requests for comment.

Lukoil did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The plan is for ​a cashless deal in which frozen Lukoil securities held by Western investors, including Capital Group, would be exchanged for Lukoil's international assets, the people said.

Capital Group declined to ‌comment.

INITIAL OFFER ⁠REJECTED

The sale process started following US sanctions on Lukoil in October 2025. Reuters reported in February that the US slowed the sale partly to pressure Russia in negotiations to end its war in Ukraine.

Last December, the US Treasury rejected an offer from a group that included US bank Xtellus Partners saying that Lukoil should not receive a windfall from the sale in shares or cash.

The Boehly-led consortium was able to move forward by promising to put the shares ​in an escrow account, rather than ​transferring them straight to Lukoil, ⁠two people said. The US Treasury did not respond to requests for comment.

More than a dozen companies bid for Lukoil's assets, including oil majors Exxon Mobil and Chevron, US private equity group Carlyle, and the former owner of Pornhub Bernd ​Bergmair, Reuters reported in November last year. Carlyle dropped out of the race last month, leaving the Boehly consortium ​in the lead.

LUKOIL SECURITIES ⁠BOUGHT FROM US, UK FUNDS

The bank acting on behalf of the consortium bought Lukoil securities from around 10 US and British investment funds as well as US depositary banks which held them on behalf of retail investors, two of the people said.

The shares were priced at 30 cents on the dollar, the ⁠other two people ​said, a substantial discount that reflected their sanctioned status.

Western investment funds were large holders ​of Lukoil stock before Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The shares were subsequently removed from major emerging market indices and have since been frozen and written down by Western funds.

text:
The United Nations has now said, in writing, that most of El Salvador's soldiers in Haiti aren't its responsibility.

In a note to correspondents Monday, the Secretary-General's spokesman, Stéphane Dujarric, said "the vast majority" of the additional Salvadoran troops are not deployed under the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force and "fall outside of the scope of the UN Support Office's mandate and reporting." That office supplies the force and runs its human-rights screening. Bukele, per the Miami Herald, now puts his troops there at 2,500, plus attack helicopters. The Herald reports they answer to a Salvadoran commander, not the force's Mongolian general, and arrived before a signed agreement with Haiti and without the force's required human-rights training.

So who do they answer to? El Salvador, Haiti, and international law in general. The UN says every operation must follow human rights and humanitarian law, and that "transparency and accountability" are essential to keep international support. That's a reminder, not oversight.

The note also answered a letter. Wilson Joseph leads the 400 Mawozo gang and is under UN sanctions and a US indictment over the 2021 kidnapping of 17 missionaries. On Nov. 1 he asked Guterres for a delegation and mediation. The UN said receiving it "does not constitute endorsement of its contents, recognition of its author, or a position." Joseph told AP the four missing Salvadoran technicians are dead. He offered no evidence, and El Salvador believes they are alive.

There's a record here. In 2024 a UN expert panel wrote that Haiti's gang leaders "have oscillated between shows of force and calls for dialogue in the hope of securing an amnesty." The same panel named a former senator, Rony Célestin, as "one of the financers" of 400 Mawozo. And on Oct. 23 former president Michel Martelly, whom the US Treasury sanctioned in 2024 saying he "sponsored multiple Haiti-based gangs," filed to run for president, two weeks after the electoral council dropped a rule aimed at candidates under foreign sanctions. Neither man has been convicted.

Haiti has been here. In 2006 President Préval met gang leaders at the palace and offered money to disarm while UN troops kept up pressure. A US Institute of Peace review says it failed. Kidnappings soared, and by December he told the gangs to "surrender or die."

My reading of the situation: thousands of foreign troops now sit outside the one system built to watch them, a sanctioned gang leader wants talks, and a sanctioned ex-president wants votes. On Tuesday the prime minister vowed sanctions would reach "gangs in neckties" too. So if a patrol kills a civilian in the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac, who files the report? Nobody has said yet.

That's it from Nightdesk. Till next time, we're still on the beat.

text:
Everyone is watching Starship's next flight. Almost nobody is doing the revenue math on what that rocket actually carries — and that math is where the real story lives.

Per a Motley Fool analysis published on Yahoo Finance this week (citing advisory firm Rational Futures), $SPCX has officially entered its commercial payload era, and the numbers behind that shift are staggering.

The proof is already in orbit: on September 28, Starship's 14th test flight delivered 26 next-generation Starlink satellites — the rocket's first operational orbital mission. The flight itself had a rough patch, with an early engine shutdown cutting the mission from 10 hours to about three. But the payload made orbit, and that's what matters.

Now the economics. A full Starship payload of next-generation Starlink satellites could support roughly $1.65 billion in additional annual revenue for SpaceX — and even the 26-satellite batch from September scales to about $715 million per year. That's a single rocket doing what used to take dozens of Falcon 9 launches.

The risk side is real and worth understanding: outside estimates put early Starship launch costs around $100 million per mission, and the commercial insurance market currently offers only about $650 million in coverage for a single launch. That's exactly why the company is hedging with a growing commercial book — Voyager's Starlab space station, estimated at $2.8 to 3.3 billion to develop and launch, is already slated for Starship.

Why this matters: SpaceX is no longer a story about rockets that fly. It's a story about the most powerful launch vehicle in history becoming a revenue machine — one that can carry entire constellations, space stations, and eventually data centers to orbit.

And the next chapter is already on the pad: Flight 15 targets November with the first-ever attempt to recover both stages — Super Heavy and Starship coming home to the tower's chopsticks. When that happens, launch costs bend again, and every number above gets better.

This man is building the future. And now it's starting to pay for itself.
